incidents.title: Qubole trusted AWS access abused to breach customer accounts
incidents.victim: Multiple Qubole customers using Qubole-connected AWS accounts
incidents.attacker: Unidentified attacker; Wiz researchers observed the activity and did not link it to a known campaign.
incidents.what: The attacker used credentials for Qubole's AWS account to assume trusted IAM roles in customer AWS environments. The intruder accessed Lambda environment variables, AWS Secrets Manager, SSM Parameter Store, and S3, tested recovered AWS, Entra ID, and Okta credentials, and copied data from accessible buckets. A separate activity from October 8 to October 11 used some customers' AWS access keys and compromised a few cloud environments; researchers did not link that activity to the AssumeRole abuse.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The incident abused a trusted data-platform integration to obtain privileged access inside multiple customers' cloud accounts, exposing reusable credentials and stored data. Some victims lacked S3 object-level logging, so the full scope of accessed data could not be determined.
incidents.significance: Wiz and Sentra observed successful cross-customer AssumeRole activity using Qubole's trusted AWS account, followed by secret discovery and S3 data copying. The event demonstrates compromise of a trusted vendor access path, although Qubole and Idera had not publicly stated the cause or complete victim scope at publication.

severity.reason: Researchers observed successful access to multiple customer AWS environments, including theft of stored secrets and copying of S3 data. The available reporting does not establish service disruption, financial loss, or the complete number of affected customers.

updates.what: The attacker used compromised Qubole IAM credentials to assume customer-configured cross-account AWS roles, enumerate environments, collect secrets and configurations, test credentials, and exfiltrate data from S3 buckets. Researchers observed some entire buckets downloaded in a single session; a separate October 8–11 campaign also tested and sometimes used customer-owned AWS keys.

The attacker used compromised Qubole IAM identities to assume trusted cross-account roles in customer AWS environments. Wiz observed resource enumeration, retrieval of secrets and environment variables, validation of AWS, Microsoft Entra ID, and Okta credentials, and downloads from accessible S3 buckets.

incidents.title: Sutherland employee-delegation incident exposed health-plan data
incidents.victim: Sutherland Healthcare Solutions and affected health-plan members
incidents.attacker: An unauthorized individual engaged by a Sutherland employee; malicious intent was not reported
incidents.what: Between July 29, 2024, and July 10, 2026, the unauthorized individual accessed names, addresses, dates of birth, health-plan information, Social Security numbers, health-insurance claims data, and stated gender. The employee’s access was terminated after discovery; Sutherland reported no identified misuse.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The incident involved confirmed unauthorized access to sensitive health, identity, and insurance information held by a healthcare business associate, although the affected population and any misuse remain undisclosed.
incidents.significance: Sutherland provides revenue-cycle and related services to healthcare organizations, and the accessed information included Social Security numbers, claims data, and health-plan details. The number of affected people has not been publicly disclosed.

severity.reason: Unauthorized access to sensitive health and identity information was confirmed. No service disruption, misuse, affected count, or financial loss was reported.

incidents.title: Hoag Memorial Hospital Presbyterian confirms network intrusion
incidents.victim: Hoag Memorial Hospital Presbyterian
incidents.attacker: Unidentified; external cybersecurity and digital-forensics experts confirmed unauthorized access
incidents.what: Hoag identified suspicious network activity on October 8, 2026. Investigators confirmed unauthorized access to its computer network, and Hoag confirmed on October 25 that files containing personal and protected health information had been exposed and potentially stolen.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The incident compromised a hospital network and exposed patient information, creating confirmed healthcare privacy consequences even though the affected count and precise data types were not publicly disclosed.
incidents.significance: Hoag is a nonprofit hospital network serving Orange County, and the confirmed intrusion reached files containing personal and protected health information. The hospital provided credit monitoring and identity-theft protection to affected individuals.

severity.reason: Unauthorized network access and exposure of personal and protected health information were confirmed. Reporting did not establish service disruption, the number of affected individuals, specific data types, or financial loss.

incidents.title: Santa Barbara Endodontics ransomware attack encrypted patient records
incidents.victim: Santa Barbara Endodontics, California
incidents.attacker: The Gentlemen, identified by the practice as the threat actor; attribution is not independently established in the report
incidents.what: The practice identified a ransomware intrusion after receiving a ransom note. Patient records were encrypted, restored from backups, and may have been stolen; the investigation remains ongoing.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The potentially affected information includes names, Social Security numbers, medical and dental histories, diagnoses, insurance information, and payment-claim data. The practice said it was monitoring threats to publish stolen data, but the extent of data access or theft is not yet established.
incidents.significance: This was a confirmed ransomware compromise of a healthcare provider involving encryption of patient records and potential theft of sensitive health and identity information.

severity.reason: Patient records were confirmed encrypted and later restored from backups. Possible theft of sensitive patient data is under investigation, and no ransom payment was reported.

incidents.title: Hollister Family Dental appointment system accessed by an intruder
incidents.victim: Hollister Family Dental & Implant Center, California
incidents.attacker: Unknown unauthorized third party
incidents.what: A third-party appointment-management system used by the practice was accessed intermittently by an unauthorized party. Patient information may have been viewed or acquired.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: Potentially exposed information included names, contact details, dates of birth, appointment details, dental-care questions, providers, symptoms, and medications. The number of affected individuals was not disclosed and no misuse had been identified.
incidents.significance: A confirmed compromise of a trusted healthcare-related appointment platform exposed sensitive patient and treatment information, although the final scope and theft status remain unresolved.

severity.reason: Forensic investigation confirmed unauthorized access over several months, but the reporting only says data may have been viewed or acquired and does not establish the number of affected people.

incidents.title: Park Dental Partners network intrusion exposed patient information
incidents.victim: Park Dental Partners, Inc., a dental resource organization serving practices in Minnesota, Wisconsin, Arizona, and North Carolina
incidents.attacker: Unknown unauthorized third party
incidents.what: An unauthorized party accessed Park Dental Partners’ network over two days. The subsequent review found that names, dates of birth, diagnoses, treatment information, and health-insurance policy information were potentially viewed or obtained.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The event involved confirmed unauthorized network access and potential exposure of sensitive health and insurance information. The number of affected individuals had not been disclosed.
incidents.significance: The compromise affected a dental-sector support organization and involved potentially exposed diagnoses, treatment details, and insurance information across practices it supports.

severity.reason: Network access and potential viewing or acquisition of sensitive patient information were reported, but the affected population and confirmed theft scope remain unknown.

incidents.title: Turla Cereal malware compromised government Exchange servers
incidents.victim: Government organizations in Kazakhstan and Romania
incidents.attacker: Turla, also known as Snake, Secret Blizzard, and Waterbug; ESET and reporting link the group to Russia’s FSB, but attribution remains researcher-assessed.
incidents.what: ESET found the Cereal toolset on a Kazakh government body and later on a Romanian government agency compromised on December 23, 2025. CerealBox injected into Microsoft Exchange and selectively collected emails, including messages involving NATO and EU representatives; related components enabled querying Active Directory, extracting credentials, reading files, and executing commands in memory.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The incident demonstrates sustained unauthorized access to government email infrastructure and the theft of sensitive diplomatic and administrative correspondence while normal Exchange delivery continued, making the compromise difficult to detect.
incidents.where: Government organizations in Kazakhstan and Romania
incidents.significance: ESET directly observed the Cereal toolset on government Exchange servers and documented selective email collection, credential extraction, directory reconnaissance, and command execution. The malware was designed for long-term, stealthy espionage and used the compromised Exchange server as its control point.

severity.reason: Researchers observed actual compromise of government Exchange servers and selective theft of email correspondence, including messages involving NATO and EU representatives. Normal email delivery was not interrupted, and broader downstream impact or financial loss was not reported.

updates.what: Attackers used the previously unknown Cereal toolkit, including CerealBox embedded in Microsoft Exchange, to monitor email traffic, capture selected messages, and maintain covert access. In Romania, the malware collected correspondence with NATO and EU institutions; the initial access method and total amount of stolen information were not determined.

ESET observed the previously undocumented Cereal toolset compromising Microsoft Exchange servers at two government entities. The malware enabled command execution, network mapping, credential-secret extraction, and targeted harvesting and exfiltration of emails and attachments.

incidents.title: Barracuda ESG flaws exploited for root access
incidents.victim: A limited number of organizations using Barracuda Email Security Gateway and other affected Barracuda products
incidents.attacker: Unknown; Barracuda reported exploitation activity but did not identify the attackers.
incidents.what: Attackers exploited CVE-2026-116606 and CVE-2026-111560 against Barracuda products. In combination, the flaws could bypass authorization and enable unauthenticated operating-system command execution with root privileges; Barracuda confirmed exploitation affecting a small number of organizations.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The incident demonstrates confirmed compromise of business security appliances with privileged access, although the available report does not establish data theft, persistence, or service disruption.
incidents.significance: Barracuda confirmed active exploitation against a limited number of customers, with potential root-level control of affected email-security and related appliances.

severity.reason: Barracuda confirmed exploitation affecting a small number of organizations and described possible root access. Data theft, operational disruption, and financial loss were not established in the available reporting.

incidents.title: Fireworks AI development machines breached through cloud provider
incidents.victim: Fireworks AI and some customers
incidents.attacker: Fireworks said evidence indicated links to a financially motivated cybercriminal group; attribution remains unconfirmed.
incidents.what: After a third-party cloud provider experienced a security incident on October 23, attackers used it on October 24 to reach Fireworks development machines and run an unauthorized workload. The breach exposed resource metadata, billing information, and incomplete model weights and datasets for some customers; Fireworks said payment-card numbers were not accessible.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The incident compromised an AI-infrastructure provider through a trusted cloud provider and exposed customer business information and proprietary AI assets. Fireworks detected the activity the same day, revoked credentials, isolated systems, and began a broader investigation.
incidents.significance: Fireworks confirmed unauthorized access through a third-party cloud provider to development machines, followed by customer-data impact involving billing records and incomplete model weights and datasets.

severity.reason: Fireworks confirmed unauthorized access and exposure of customer resource metadata, billing information, and some model weights and datasets. The available reporting does not establish the number of affected customers, service disruption, or financial losses.

incidents.title: Xen Orchestra auth bypass exploited to hijack virtualization hosts
incidents.victim: Organizations operating Xen Orchestra or Xen Orchestra Appliance to manage XCP-ng environments; specific victims were not reported
incidents.attacker: Unknown attackers; Vates confirmed active exploitation and provided campaign indicators, but did not attribute it
incidents.what: Attackers exploited VSA-2026-062 by sending a specially crafted authentication cookie, bypassing credentials and obtaining administrator-level access. Vates reported that compromise can enable arbitrary code execution on managed pools and root takeover of XCP-ng nodes; indicators included a VM named pivot2 and malicious cron files.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: This is a confirmed exploitation campaign against virtualization-management infrastructure, with reported access to administrative functions and potential control of managed virtual machines and hosts.
incidents.significance: Vates confirmed active exploitation of a flaw that can bypass authentication, expose reusable login tokens, and provide administrator privileges over virtualization environments. Specific compromised organizations and observed downstream damage were not reported.

severity.reason: Active exploitation and attack artifacts were confirmed by Vates, but the reporting does not identify victims or establish service outages, data theft, or financial losses.

incidents.title: Microsoft Outlook zero-day exploited to steal NTLM hashes
incidents.victim: Organizations and users running affected Microsoft Outlook versions; specific victims were not reported
incidents.attacker: Not reported; Microsoft and BleepingComputer report exploitation in attacks
incidents.what: Attackers sent specially crafted Outlook message files that, when opened, caused connections to attacker-controlled network locations and disclosed NTLMv2 authentication hashes. The hashes could be cracked or used to impersonate users and access corporate accounts.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The flaw was actively exploited rather than merely disclosed, creating a path to credential theft and possible unauthorized corporate-account access. The reporting does not identify victims or confirm successful account compromise beyond hash disclosure.
incidents.significance: This is an actively exploited zero-day affecting Outlook and exposing reusable authentication material through malicious attachments; Microsoft issued a security fix on November 10, 2026.

severity.reason: Microsoft and BleepingComputer report exploitation to disclose NTLMv2 authentication hashes. Specific victims, account takeovers, service disruption, and financial losses were not reported.

incidents.title: Fireworks says first October breach stole customer and billing data
incidents.victim: Fireworks AI and a limited number of customer accounts
incidents.attacker: A financially motivated cybercriminal group; specific group not identified.
incidents.what: Fireworks said investigators found unauthorized access that resulted in theft of account and billing information, invoices, payment history, secrets, datasets, and other AI-related data. The company said a limited number of customer accounts were affected and notified those customers.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The incident involved confirmed unauthorized access to an AI infrastructure provider and theft of customer-related sensitive information and reusable secrets. The source does not establish the final number of affected records or customers.
incidents.where: San Mateo, California, United States (vendor headquarters; affected customer locations not reported)
incidents.significance: Fireworks provides AI infrastructure to more than 10,000 customers; investigators confirmed theft of billing data, secrets, datasets, and AI-related information, although the company described the directly affected account count as limited.

severity.reason: Fireworks confirmed theft of account, billing, payment-history, dataset, AI-related data, and secrets affecting a limited number of customer accounts. Service disruption and financial losses were not established for this first breach.

incidents.title: SilentDelivery watering-hole campaign deployed Sparrow backdoors
incidents.victim: Government, shipping, IT, and research-sector website visitors and organizations in Europe and Asia
incidents.attacker: SilentDelivery cluster; linked by Check Point Research to the CopperDragon Sparrow malware ecosystem and China-nexus actors. Attribution is assessed, not definitive.
incidents.what: Attackers compromised legitimate websites and injected obfuscated JavaScript that selectively displayed a fake Chrome certificate warning. Victims who installed the purported certificate-repair utility received the SquadC or SparrowDoor backdoor; phishing emails also delivered SquadC to Indonesian organizations.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The campaign used compromised websites and trojanized installers to obtain unauthorized access to systems in government, shipping, IT, and research sectors. The reporting identifies foothold malware and persistence, but does not establish final victim counts or operational losses.
incidents.where: Czech Republic, Germany, France, Taiwan, Nepal, Hong Kong, and Indonesia; indications of related activity in Egypt and the Philippines
incidents.significance: Check Point Research observed compromised websites and malware delivery targeting selected organizations across multiple countries. The campaign demonstrates consequential access to victim systems, although downstream effects are not reported.

severity.reason: Researchers observed compromised websites delivering backdoors to targeted users and organizations. The available reporting does not establish service outages, data theft, or financial losses.

incidents.title: OceanGate campaign moved from Linux servers into Windows networks
incidents.victim: Asian organizations; specific victims were not reported
incidents.attacker: OceanGate cluster; linked by Check Point Research to the CopperDragon Sparrow malware ecosystem and China-nexus actors. Attribution is assessed, not definitive.
incidents.what: Attackers compromised internet-facing Linux servers, deployed AnnobinDoor and SparrowShell, harvested credentials, and moved laterally into Windows environments. In an observed intrusion, the actor authenticated to Windows systems with an administrator account and deployed reconnaissance, keylogging, credential-dumping, and backdoor tooling.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The campaign achieved unauthorized access across Linux and Windows environments and included administrator access, credential collection, lateral movement, and attempted sensitive-data exfiltration. The report does not provide a confirmed victim count or quantify stolen data.
incidents.significance: Check Point Research documented cross-platform compromise, successful administrator authentication, lateral movement, and credential-harvesting capabilities in real victim environments.

severity.reason: Observed activity included compromise of internet-facing servers, administrator access to Windows systems, lateral movement, and credential harvesting. Confirmed service disruption and final data-loss scope are not reported.

incidents.title: DarkWire campaign compromised telecom and government organizations
incidents.victim: Telecommunications providers and government organizations in Latin America; specific victims were not reported
incidents.attacker: DarkWire cluster; linked by Check Point Research to the CopperDragon Sparrow malware ecosystem and China-nexus actors. Attribution is assessed, not definitive.
incidents.what: Attackers compromised organizations and deployed CopperDoor and CopperDNS backdoors, along with loaders, proxies, DNS tunneling, and LSASS credential-dumping tools. Operations relied on DLL sideloading and existing system paths to reduce their footprint.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The campaign established unauthorized access to telecommunications and government networks and deployed persistent backdoor and credential-theft tooling. The available reporting does not establish specific outages, stolen-data totals, or victim names.
incidents.significance: The campaign affected telecommunications and government targets and used memory-resident backdoors, DNS tunneling, proxying, and credential harvesting to maintain access and evade detection.

severity.reason: Researchers reported compromises and deployment of backdoors and credential-dumping tools against telecom and government organizations. Operational disruption and confirmed data theft are not quantified.

incidents.title: SGLang flaw breached NEAR AI inference infrastructure
incidents.victim: NEAR AI, including NEAR AI Agents and Private Chat users
incidents.attacker: Unidentified attacker; attribution was not reported.
incidents.what: The attacker exploited a remote-code-execution flaw in the SGLang inference engine and ran code on a NEAR AI inference server, including inside a trusted execution environment. They moved into internal systems, downloaded account details for about 100 Private Chat users, accessed data from 18 older AI agents, and exposed two customers’ NEAR AI Cloud API keys.
incidents.ai_role: The compromised system was an AI inference engine and AI-agent infrastructure; the reporting does not indicate that AI performed the attack.
incidents.why: The incident bypassed the privacy protections expected from a TEE and exposed user information, agent histories, settings, logs, and reusable cloud credentials. NEAR AI revoked sessions and credentials, replaced agent tokens, took Private Chat offline, and patched its inference servers.
incidents.significance: NEAR AI confirmed unauthorized code execution on an inference server and subsequent internal access. The compromise affected an AI service, 18 agents, about 100 user accounts, and two customer API keys, although the company found no evidence that stored Private Chat conversations or uploaded files were accessed.

severity.reason: NEAR AI took Private Chat offline, revoked active sessions and credentials, and replaced agent tokens. Confirmed access included account details, agent data, and two API keys; stored Private Chat conversations and uploaded files were reportedly not accessed, and broader request exposure remains uncertain.

incidents.title: French supermarket refrigeration controllers altered in October attacks
incidents.victim: An estimated 250 to 350 French supermarkets
incidents.attacker: Malicious cyber actors; attribution not reported
incidents.what: Attackers compromised refrigeration controllers and remotely activated defrost functions, raising temperatures in refrigerators and freezers.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The incident affected operational refrigeration systems at hundreds of supermarkets and created a risk of inventory spoilage and unsafe storage conditions.
incidents.significance: The reported compromise affected industrial control systems across an estimated 250 to 350 supermarkets, with refrigeration temperatures altered through unauthorized controller access.

severity.reason: Refrigeration settings were changed across hundreds of supermarkets. The reporting describes potential spoilage and safety consequences but gives no confirmed loss amount.

updates.what: Attackers remotely altered Danfoss refrigeration-controller settings, causing supermarket refrigerators and freezers to defrost overnight. Temperatures reportedly reached 50°C for up to six hours, spoiling food and forcing affected products to be withdrawn from sale.

CERT-FR reported compromises of Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC refrigeration controllers and later added Copeland XWEB and Dixell XWEB systems. About 700 French supermarkets were reportedly affected; refrigeration failures caused food disposal, and prosecutors said the attack also caused fires.

Hackers compromised industrial refrigeration controllers and remotely changed defrost settings to high temperatures. French authorities said approximately 700 retail locations were targeted, causing food losses, at least 15 fires, and significant material damage.

Attackers sabotaged refrigeration systems at French food retailers. Authorities reported extensive food losses and at least 15 fires. ANSSI also identified concurrent targeting of Schneider Electric equipment at several small hydroelectric facilities, causing moderate disruption.

Attackers remotely accessed Danfoss and Dixell refrigeration-controller web interfaces, set defrost cycles to abnormally high temperatures without time limits, and disabled temperature-probe safety alerts. The attack caused food losses and about 20 fires; French authorities estimated losses at several tens of millions of euros.

incidents.title: Xen Orchestra auth bypass exploited to hijack virtualization hosts
incidents.victim: Organizations operating Xen Orchestra or Xen Orchestra Appliance to manage XCP-ng environments; specific victims were not reported
incidents.attacker: Unidentified threat actor; Vates reported exploitation from 91.211.251[.]112 and a Tor onion service. Attribution is not established.
incidents.what: Attackers exploited Xen Orchestra flaw VSA-2026-062 by submitting a specially crafted authentication cookie. The bypass could disclose reusable tokens, grant administrator privileges, enable arbitrary actions on managed pools, and lead to root takeover of XCP-ng nodes; Vates reported active exploitation and supplied indicators of compromise.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The incident enabled unauthorized administrative access to virtualization-management infrastructure and potential root control of managed hosts. Vates reported active exploitation, although specific compromised organizations and resulting damage were not reported.
incidents.significance: Vendor reporting confirms exploitation in the wild against a platform that manages virtualized infrastructure; the described attack path can expose reusable authentication tokens and provide administrator or root-level control of managed environments.

severity.reason: Vates reported active exploitation and described administrator-level actions and potential root takeover of XCP-ng nodes. Specific victims, service effects, data theft, and financial losses were not reported.

incidents.title: Fireworks AI breach expanded to customer datasets and Notion AI chats
incidents.victim: Fireworks AI, a limited set of customer accounts, and fewer than 1% of Notion workspaces
incidents.attacker: Unnamed third-party/cybercriminal threat actor; Fireworks assessed links to a financially motivated group seeking to sell stolen LLM access, but attribution was not established.
incidents.what: Attackers reached Fireworks development machines through an unnamed cloud provider on October 23, then used an unauthorized workload to access resource metadata, billing information, incomplete model weights, and datasets for some customers. The incident also affected Notion AI Insights data, including unattributable chat transcripts.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The compromise crossed from a trusted cloud provider into Fireworks development infrastructure and exposed customer secrets, billing records, model artifacts, datasets, and potentially sensitive AI chat content. Fireworks said payment-card numbers were not stored or impacted, and Notion said no other platform features were affected.
incidents.significance: Fireworks confirmed unauthorized access to its development environment and additional customer-data impact, while Notion disclosed exposure affecting fewer than 1% of workspaces. The event expands the previously reported Fireworks breach and demonstrates downstream impact on a customer using Fireworks-hosted AI infrastructure.

severity.reason: Fireworks confirmed access to customer billing information, datasets, incomplete model weights, resource metadata, and secrets; Notion confirmed affected AI chat transcripts. Fireworks isolated systems and rotated credentials, while Notion disabled its Insights feature; final scope and financial losses were not reported.

incidents.title: AhsayCBS flaws exploited to deploy webshells and cryptominers
incidents.victim: At least five organizations using AhsayCBS backup management software
incidents.attacker: Unidentified threat actors; attribution was not reported.
incidents.what: Attackers chained two unpatched AhsayCBS vulnerabilities to bypass authentication, execute commands with System privileges, deploy JSP webshells, establish persistence through a disguised Windows service, and install XMRig cryptominers. Huntress also observed an AI-assisted PowerShell script used to monitor Task Manager and terminate it.
incidents.ai_role: Attackers planted an AI-assisted PowerShell script to monitor Task Manager and terminate it; the reporting does not establish that AI carried out the intrusion.
incidents.why: The campaign compromised exposed backup-management systems and achieved unauthenticated remote code execution, persistence, and cryptomining activity. AhsayCBS is used by MSPs and system integrators, increasing the operational significance of the intrusions.
incidents.significance: Huntress directly observed exploitation, webshell deployment, persistence, and cryptocurrency miners on affected systems; at least five organizations had been targeted by October 8. The full scope and any downstream impact were not reported.

severity.reason: Huntress observed unauthenticated remote code execution, System-level access, webshells, persistence, and cryptomining across a campaign involving at least five organizations. Service disruption, victim losses, and complete compromise scope were not established.

updates.what: Attackers chained two authentication-bypass and remote-code-execution vulnerabilities to access AhsayCBS systems, deploy JSP webshells, establish persistence, and install XMRig cryptocurrency miners. Huntress also observed an AI-assisted PowerShell script used to monitor Task Manager and terminate it.

Huntress observed attackers chaining CVE-2026-105133 and CVE-2026-105134 to bypass authentication and execute commands on AhsayCBS systems. The intrusions deployed JSP web shells, XMRig miners, tunneling and remote-access tools, Microsoft Defender exclusions, and a sandbox-evading Python backdoor; activity also included a Veeam credential-theft query in a related environment.

incidents.title: Railway breach exposed customer environment variables and secrets
incidents.victim: Railway and a subset of its customer workspaces
incidents.attacker: Unauthorized third party; identity not reported. Railway said the campaign targeted its infrastructure, apparently seeking AI-provider API keys for distillation attacks.
incidents.what: Railway disclosed anomalous activity in systems storing customer environment variables. Its investigation found that an unauthorized party may have accessed encrypted variables and, in some cases, their decrypted contents. Railway assessed that variables associated with at most 1.85% of workspaces—about 100,000—may have been compromised and worked with providers to revoke potentially exposed keys.
incidents.ai_role: Railway reported that attackers used AI-powered agents to identify and exploit vulnerabilities during the roughly 26-hour intrusion; the stolen credentials were also used for unauthorized AI usage.
incidents.why: Compromised environment variables can contain API keys, database credentials, private registry credentials, cryptocurrency wallet keys, and other reusable secrets. Railway also reported build failures, queued deployments, temporarily paused signups, and credential-token rotation while responding.
incidents.significance: This was a confirmed compromise of a cloud platform's systems with potential access to sensitive customer secrets across up to about 100,000 workspaces. Railway confirmed that some decrypted contents may have been obtained, although the number of definitively affected customers and any downstream misuse remain unclear.

severity.reason: Railway confirmed unauthorized access to systems storing customer environment variables and possible access to decrypted secrets; it also reported build failures, queued deployments, and temporarily paused signups. The exact number of affected workspaces and any financial losses are not established.

updates.what: Railway disclosed sustained targeted activity against systems storing customer environment variables. The attacker may have accessed encrypted variables and, in some cases, their decrypted contents; Railway assessed that variables associated with at most 1.85% of workspaces, about 100,000, may have been compromised. A researcher also reported cryptocurrency wallets being drained when private keys were stored on Railway.

Attackers exploited vulnerabilities in Railway’s build infrastructure and trust relationships, accessed internal source code and decrypted customer environment variables, and obtained linked-account tokens for 1,852 users. Stolen credentials generated approximately $740,000 in unauthorized AI usage.

incidents.title: Nitori confirms unauthorized access potentially exposing 37.62M records
incidents.victim: Nitori Co., Ltd., a Japanese furniture and home-accessories retailer
incidents.attacker: Unidentified third party; attribution was not reported.
incidents.what: Nitori confirmed unauthorized access to a company-managed system on November 6, 2026. Its investigation found the attacker may have accessed the system since mid-October, and up to 37.62 million records may have been leaked, including names, addresses, telephone numbers, dates of birth, membership details, and order information. Passwords and credit-card information were reportedly not exposed.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The incident potentially exposed a very large volume of customer and corporate-member personal information, creating phishing and fraud risks. Nitori blocked access and notified Japanese authorities; the cause, whether ransomware was involved, and the number of affected customers remain under investigation.
incidents.significance: Nitori confirmed a real unauthorized system intrusion and reported that up to 37.62 million personal-information records may have been leaked. The scale is widespread, although the final number of affected customers and confirmed exfiltration remain unresolved.

severity.reason: Nitori confirmed unauthorized access and reported potential external leakage of up to 37.62 million records containing personal, corporate-member, and order information. No service outage or financial loss was reported, and the company had not confirmed the final affected count or whether all potentially exposed data was exfiltrated.

incidents.title: Hackers disrupted refrigeration at more than 115 European stores
incidents.victim: Multiple supermarket chains and independent food retailers in Belgium, the Netherlands, Sweden, Luxembourg, Ireland, and Estonia
incidents.attacker: Unknown; attackers remotely changed refrigeration settings, but attribution was not reported.
incidents.what: Attackers remotely altered freezer and cooling-system settings, including shutting down refrigeration and activating defrost cycles. More than 115 stores were affected, with some reporting rising temperatures, discarded frozen food, and early intervention by store managers.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The incident disrupted business-critical refrigeration across grocery stores and caused documented product losses and operational intervention. The reporting does not establish whether the affected stores were compromised through one coordinated campaign or through separate attacks, nor does it provide a quantified financial loss.
incidents.where: Belgium, the Netherlands, Sweden, Luxembourg, Ireland, and Estonia
incidents.significance: Victim spokespeople confirmed refrigeration-system disruption at multiple chains, including Ahold Delhaize, Carrefour, Coop, ICA, Spar Colruyt, Intermarché, SuperValu, and Selver. The attack affected food-cooling operations at more than 115 stores and caused at least some product disposal.

severity.reason: More than 115 stores across six European countries experienced remotely altered or disabled refrigeration, and at least one store discarded frozen food after temperatures were changed. The article reports significant product losses but gives no monetary estimate.

updates.what: Attackers compromised refrigeration controllers, including Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC systems and Copeland XWEB/Dixell XWEB systems. Reported manipulation of defrost cycles delayed alarms and caused refrigeration failures.

Attackers remotely changed refrigeration settings, shut down units, or activated defrost functions. Confirmed affected operators included ICA, Coop, Ahold Delhaize, Carrefour, Spar Colruyt, Intermarché, SuperValu, Selver, and Dutch butcher shops and neighborhood stores.

Attackers accessed internet-reachable refrigeration-management systems, apparently including Danfoss and Copeland controllers, and forced evaporators into defrost mode. Temperatures in some units reached 50°C, disrupting refrigeration at more than 100 stores; reported affected examples included Delhaize, Carrefour, Colruyt, SuperValu, ICA, Coop, and Intermarché locations.

Attackers accessed vulnerable Copeland XWEB refrigeration controllers and remotely changed operating parameters, including putting a refrigerator into defrost mode. The suppliers were reportedly exposed through authentication-bypass vulnerabilities in XWEB firmware version 1.12.1 and earlier.

Attackers remotely altered refrigeration-controller settings, including switching Belgian units to defrost mode and raising temperatures as high as 50°C in stores in Sweden and Estonia. Reported victims included Delhaize, Carrefour, Intermarché, Spar, IKEA, ICA, Coop, Musgrave/SuperValu, Selver, Kesko, and other retailers.

Attackers remotely accessed refrigeration and cold-chain monitoring systems, reportedly using default credentials, and altered temperature and defrost settings. Hundreds of French supermarkets discarded produce, while EFS reported dangerously high temperatures in blood-product storage rooms before corrective action prevented loss.
Attackers compromised refrigeration systems at more than 115 stores; some systems shut down and others raised temperatures as high as 50°C (122°F).

Threat actors exploited weaknesses in internet-accessible industrial refrigeration controllers to alter temperatures or force cooling units into defrost mode. The French Blood Establishment confirmed that an incident affecting a refrigeration-equipment provider changed temperature and defrost settings to extremely high levels at three blood-plasma storage facilities.

incidents.title: Plex2Shell exploited Plex servers to install miners and proxy software
incidents.victim: Organizations and users operating vulnerable Plex Media Server installations; specific victims were not reported
incidents.attacker: Not reported; CISA listed the vulnerabilities in its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
incidents.what: Attackers chained four Plex Media Server vulnerabilities—CVE-2026-96652, CVE-2026-96654, CVE-2026-96655, and CVE-2026-96656—in the Plex2Shell exploit to compromise servers and deliver cryptocurrency miners and proxy software.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The vulnerabilities were exploited in the wild and resulted in unauthorized software delivery to Plex servers, although the number and identities of affected victims were not reported.
incidents.significance: This was confirmed in-the-wild exploitation of a widely deployed media-server platform, with attackers gaining sufficient access to install miners and proxy software. Victim count and operational consequences remain unspecified.

severity.reason: In-the-wild exploitation and installation of attacker-controlled miners and proxy software were reported. The available reporting does not establish the number of compromised servers, service outages, or financial losses.

updates.what: QNAP reported multiple customer reports that Plex Media Server installations on exposed NAS devices appeared to have been compromised through the Plex2Shell vulnerability chain. The vendor warned that attackers may have installed payloads and advised clean reinstallation, credential resets, and log review.

Attackers exploited the Plex2Shell chain of four vulnerabilities in Plex Media Server to execute arbitrary code on exposed QNAP NAS servers without valid credentials. QNAP reported that some users' Plex applications appeared compromised.

incidents.title: Revolve breach exposed payment-card information
incidents.victim: Revolve, an online fashion retailer, and customers who saved payment information in Revolve accounts
incidents.attacker: Unknown cybercriminals; attribution was not reported.
incidents.what: Hackers accessed multiple Revolve systems and used automated means to obtain customer names, contact information, payment-card numbers, and expiration dates. Revolve reported at least 127,200 affected people in Texas and 1,328 in Vermont, with notifications also filed in Massachusetts.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The incident involved unauthorized access to sensitive payment-card data held by a major e-commerce retailer. Revolve said there were no operational disruptions and no material financial impact was expected; the total affected population remains unknown.
incidents.significance: A credible report based on Revolve’s SEC filing and regulatory notifications documents theft of payment-card information from an online retailer, with at least 128,528 affected people identified in Texas and Vermont.

severity.reason: Revolve confirmed unauthorized access and its investigation found that customer personal and payment-card information may have been accessed and exfiltrated. The company reported no operational disruption and no quantified financial loss.

updates.what: Hackers gained access to multiple Revolve systems and used automated means to obtain customer names, contact information, payment-card numbers, and expiration dates. Revolve reported 127,200 affected people in Texas, 1,328 in Vermont, and additional notifications in Massachusetts.

Attackers gained unauthorized access to systems including Revolve’s online shopping platform and may have exfiltrated customers’ names, addresses, payment-card numbers, and expiration dates. Revolve contained and remediated the activity and notified at least 197,072 people.

An unauthorized party accessed some Revolve systems, including its e-commerce platform, and may have used automated means to collect customers’ names, contact information, mailing addresses, card numbers, and expiration dates. Revolve became aware of the intrusion on September 29 and disclosed it in October.

incidents.title: Frontline Education breach exposed data of over 1.3 million
incidents.victim: Frontline Education and affected K-12 school-district staff and students
incidents.attacker: Unknown hackers; attribution was not reported.
incidents.what: Attackers exploited a vulnerability in a third-party software product to enter Frontline’s environment. The investigation found that personal information was stolen from the Frontline Central and School Health Management products, including names, Social Security numbers, dates of birth, government ID numbers, health-insurance or Medicaid IDs, and student IDs.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The breach affected at least 1,298,917 people according to state attorney-general filings, with the total likely higher. Frontline contained the attack by August 15 and began notifying affected districts and individuals.
incidents.where: United States; specific affected locations were not reported
incidents.significance: Frontline confirmed unauthorized access and theft of sensitive student and staff information. State filings document nearly 1.3 million affected people, meeting the threshold for a large-scale data breach.

severity.reason: Sensitive personal, government-identification, health-insurance, and student information was stolen from Frontline systems. The attack was contained within about one day; broader operational effects and financial losses were not reported.

updates.what: Attackers exploited a vulnerability in an unnamed third-party software product to access part of Frontline Education’s environment. Personal information was stolen from Frontline Central and School Health Management, potentially including Social Security numbers, dates of birth, government ID numbers, health-insurance information, and student IDs.

incidents.title: Amplifon Americas breach exposed data of 1.33 million people
incidents.victim: Amplifon Americas
incidents.attacker: Unidentified hackers; attribution was not reported.
incidents.what: Hackers accessed Amplifon Americas’ internal systems in January 2026 and copied files from certain systems between January 18 and February 8. The company reported that the stolen information included names, contact details, government identification numbers, dates of birth, hearing and medical information, health-insurance information, and, for some individuals, Social Security numbers and financial information.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The company’s review identified 1,332,826 affected people nationwide, making this a large-scale theft of sensitive health, identity, and financial information.
incidents.significance: Amplifon Americas reported that files were copied from its internal systems and disclosed a nationwide affected count of 1,332,826 people, including medical, insurance, government-ID, and some Social Security and financial information.

severity.reason: Amplifon reported unauthorized access and file copying, with sensitive medical, identity, insurance, and some financial information compromised. The company said it was not aware of fraudulent use, and no financial loss was reported.

updates.what: Amplifon said attackers accessed company files from January 18 through February 8, after suspicious activity was discovered on February 11. Confirmed breach notices identified 85,804 affected people in Texas and 1,027 in Vermont; California notices were also filed. Exposed data included names, driver’s licenses, state IDs, medical information, health-insurance data and financial information.

incidents.title: Weill Cornell Medicine patient PHI uploaded to AI tools
incidents.victim: Weill Cornell Medicine and patients receiving radiology services at NewYork-Presbyterian facilities
incidents.attacker: Unauthorized use by individuals involved in a radiology research study; no external attacker reported.
incidents.what: Protected health information from radiology services was entered into unauthorized AI and machine-learning tools. The data included medical record and radiology identifiers, service details, facility and provider names, and clinical radiology information, but not names, contact details, Social Security numbers, or financial information.
incidents.ai_role: Patient information was uploaded to AI and machine-learning tools without authorization.
incidents.why: The incident involved confirmed disclosure of sensitive medical information to unauthorized AI tools. Weill Cornell suspended the research activity and requested deletion; the number of affected patients and any misuse remain undisclosed.
incidents.significance: A healthcare research activity exposed patient radiology and clinical information to unauthorized AI tools. The provider reported no identified misuse, and the affected population has not been publicly disclosed.

severity.reason: Patient PHI was actually uploaded to unauthorized AI tools, and the research activity was suspended. No misuse, financial loss, or effect on clinical services was reported.

incidents.title: Lake Burien facility patient records uploaded to ChatGPT
incidents.victim: Lake Burien Transitional Care Facility patients operated by Washington State’s Department of Social and Health Services
incidents.attacker: A facility staff member using a personal ChatGPT account; no external attacker reported.
incidents.what: A staff member used a personal ChatGPT account to draft case-note summaries containing patient names, diagnoses, medications, and other personal health information. The investigation found one identified instance and multiple prior uses; the state wrote to 12 affected patient families.
incidents.ai_role: A staff member uploaded protected health information to a personal, unauthorized ChatGPT account for case-summary drafting.
incidents.why: Confirmed unauthorized disclosure exposed mental-health patients’ sensitive medical information to a consumer AI service. Employees were instructed to delete prompts and their accounts; no further misuse was reported.
incidents.significance: The incident demonstrates an actual healthcare-record disclosure through unauthorized use of a consumer AI tool, affecting patients at a state-operated mental-health facility.

severity.reason: Patient names, diagnoses, medications, and case-note information were uploaded to ChatGPT, with 12 families notified. No clinical-service disruption or financial loss was reported.

incidents.title: Western State Hospital patient PHI uploaded to ChatGPT
incidents.victim: Western State Hospital patients operated by Washington State’s Department of Social and Health Services
incidents.attacker: Hospital employees using ChatGPT; no external attacker reported.
incidents.what: Protected health information from four Western State Hospital patients was impermissibly uploaded to ChatGPT. The reporting does not specify all fields involved, but identifies the event as affecting patient PHI.
incidents.ai_role: Employees uploaded patient PHI to ChatGPT without authorization.
incidents.why: The incident involved confirmed disclosure of sensitive healthcare information to an unauthorized AI service. Employees were instructed to delete ChatGPT prompts and their accounts; no misuse or service disruption was reported.
incidents.significance: Four mental-health patients’ PHI was actually disclosed through unauthorized use of ChatGPT, creating a documented privacy compromise in a healthcare setting.

severity.reason: The source confirms PHI for four patients was uploaded to ChatGPT. It reports no clinical disruption, financial loss, or subsequent misuse.

incidents.title: York University breach exposed sensitive information from online forms
incidents.victim: York University
incidents.attacker: Unknown; no perpetrator details were reported.
incidents.what: York University confirmed that an unauthorized actor accessed limited online forms on 14 university websites. The stolen information varied by person and included contact details, York identification numbers, government ID information, health information, academic and employment history, financial status, criminal background, demographic details, and images.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The incident involved confirmed unauthorized access and theft of sensitive university records, including government ID, health, and financial information. The number of affected individuals and the full scope of the theft remain undisclosed.
incidents.significance: York University confirmed theft of personal information submitted through departmental forms dating from 2007 to 2026, with sensitive categories including government ID, health, financial, and criminal-background information. The university secured the forms and offered credit monitoring to affected individuals, but did not disclose the number impacted.

severity.reason: The university confirmed theft of personal information from online forms, including sensitive health, government-ID, and financial information. No service outage or financial loss was reported, and the number of affected people remains unknown.

incidents.title: ARARA newsletter breach exposed 2.2 million SEGA addresses
incidents.victim: SEGA and SEGA Fave newsletter subscribers; ARARA email-distribution service
incidents.attacker: Unknown; ARARA said the intrusion method and timing remain under investigation.
incidents.what: A breach of third-party newsletter provider ARARA exposed 2.2 million email addresses associated with 11 SEGA and SEGA Fave newsletters, including 92,300 records with additional information still being determined. ARARA said the broader incident affected 77 million addresses from nearly 380 corporate clients and attackers used the service to send more than 7 million impersonation emails.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The incident compromised a trusted service provider and exposed a large volume of subscriber data across many corporate clients. SEGA said names, addresses, payment details, passwords, and other listed account information were not included, and no misuse was confirmed.
incidents.significance: SEGA confirmed that its newsletter data was exposed through ARARA, while ARARA disclosed compromise affecting 77 million email addresses and nearly 380 clients.

severity.reason: The breach exposed 2.2 million SEGA-related email addresses and a broader 77 million addresses across ARARA clients. Reporting says names, payment data, passwords, and other specified personal details were not exposed, and confirmed misuse was not established.

incidents.title: SEGA Fave arcade network breached and taken offline
incidents.victim: SEGA Fave's ALL.Net and Aime arcade gaming network services, including related online services and SEGA ID registration
incidents.attacker: Unknown; SEGA did not identify the attacker.
incidents.what: SEGA Fave disclosed unauthorized access to servers supporting its ALL.Net and Aime arcade networks. It suspended online gameplay, SEGA Lucky Kuji Online, and new SEGA ID registrations while conducting maintenance and safety checks.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The compromise disrupted SEGA Fave's business-critical arcade and online services. SEGA said its initial investigation found no evidence that customer or business-partner data was exfiltrated and that payment information was stored separately.
incidents.significance: Unauthorized access caused a service shutdown affecting arcade network operations and associated online services; SEGA separately stated this incident was unrelated to the ARARA newsletter breach.

severity.reason: SEGA suspended multiple arcade-network and online services for maintenance and safety checks after unauthorized server access. Data theft was not evidenced in the initial investigation, and the duration and financial impact were not reported.

incidents.title: Beget cloud infrastructure wiped in destructive attack
incidents.victim: Beget, a Russian cloud, web-hosting, and domain-registration provider, and its hosted customers
incidents.attacker: Unknown; Beget reported unauthorized access but no attribution.
incidents.what: The attacker accessed Beget’s management layer and deployed data-zeroing malware across its infrastructure. VPS, S3, Kubernetes, CDN settings, IP configurations, and VPS binary backups were lost; Beget disconnected servers and is rebuilding roughly 1,000 servers.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The attack caused major disruption to a cloud and hosting provider serving more than 200,000 customers. Beget reported that more than a week later only 60% of shared hosting and 40% of dedicated servers had been restored, with VPS file backups expected to be available for only about half of users.
incidents.significance: Beget’s management systems for its entire architecture were compromised and destructive scripts erased infrastructure and backups, disrupting hosted websites and services during an ongoing recovery.

severity.reason: Beget confirmed unauthorized access, infrastructure-wide data wiping, server disconnection, and prolonged restoration affecting its hosted services. The reporting says the attack appeared focused on destruction and found no evidence that data was downloaded or modified before wiping.

incidents.title: SSHole flaw exploited to compromise Linux systems
incidents.victim: Organizations operating affected OpenSSH on musl-based Linux systems; specific victims were not reported
incidents.attacker: Unidentified actors; GreyNoise observed activity from six source IPs, while other researchers associated exploitation with botnets and cryptomining activity
incidents.what: Attackers exploited CVE-2026-123158, known as SSHole, to bypass authentication on certain OpenSSH deployments. GreyNoise recorded 16 successful exploitation chains, including reconnaissance, cloud-metadata queries, attempts to access password hashes and SSH keys, authorized_keys modification, and one case of root access with TAC Agent installation.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The attacks demonstrate active compromise of exposed Linux systems, including administrative access and attempted persistence. The reporting does not establish the identities of victims or broader operational or data-theft consequences.
incidents.significance: Independent security firms observed successful exploitation in real environments, including one attacker obtaining root privileges and installing a command-and-control agent. The campaign matters because the flaw can enable unauthorized access and persistence on affected cloud and virtualized Linux systems.

severity.reason: GreyNoise documented 16 successful exploitation chains against protected networks and observed one root-level compromise with TAC Agent installation. Credential theft and persistence were attempted, but confirmed data theft, service disruption, and financial losses were not reported.

incidents.title: Mittwald MCP flaw compromised 56 customer projects
incidents.victim: Mittwald CM Service and 56 customer projects
incidents.attacker: Unidentified hackers; AI assistance was alleged by Mittwald but not independently substantiated.
incidents.what: Attackers exploited a flaw in Mittwald’s Model Context Protocol server, which connects customer AI assistants to its mStudio hosting-management platform. Mittwald said the attackers remained undetected for eight days and compromised 56 customer projects.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The incident involved confirmed unauthorized access through a hosting provider’s management infrastructure and affected multiple customer projects. Mittwald said forensic analysis and scans found no additional attacker activity as of the reported date.
incidents.significance: A hosting provider’s MCP integration was exploited to reach 56 customer projects, demonstrating consequential compromise of a trusted service-management interface. The reported speed of activity suggested possible AI use, but the company provided no evidence distinguishing AI tools from conventional automation.

severity.reason: Mittwald confirmed compromise of 56 customer projects and eight days of attacker presence. The available reporting does not establish data theft, service outage, or financial loss.

incidents.title: Gnosis Pay card-system breach exposed customer information
incidents.victim: Gnosis Pay users and the system powering Gnosis Pay-branded cards
incidents.attacker: Unknown; Gnosis Pay reported unauthorized access but did not identify the attacker.
incidents.what: Gnosis Pay detected unauthorized access to the system powering its branded cards. The company said customer information was exposed, notified users about the data accessed, and added mandatory 3D Secure for online card payments.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The compromised card-service system handled customer information and required heightened fraud monitoring and payment controls, although the number of affected customers and any financial loss were not reported.
incidents.significance: Gnosis Pay confirmed unauthorized access to a business-critical card system and exposure of customer information. The response included increased monitoring of card activity and wallets and mandatory 3D Secure.

severity.reason: The company confirmed unauthorized access and exposure of customer information, but did not disclose the affected customer count, specific data fields, or financial losses. Card services remained subject to additional controls rather than a reported outage.

incidents.title: Attackers used compromised refrigeration controllers as proxy infrastructure
incidents.victim: Operators of Dixell/Copeland XWEB PRO refrigeration controllers; specific organizations were not reported
incidents.attacker: Unknown; SecurityScorecard reported a suspected coordinated SMTP botnet using compromised controllers.
incidents.what: SecurityScorecard identified a cluster of nine IP addresses associated with suspected SMTP abuse, including three confirmed refrigeration controllers. The compromised controllers were reportedly used as proxy exits and spam senders.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The reporting substantiates unauthorized compromise of refrigeration-control devices and their reuse for malicious network activity, although it does not establish disruption to refrigeration operations or identify the affected operators.
incidents.significance: Operational refrigeration controllers were confirmed inside an abuse infrastructure cluster, showing compromise of devices used in food and cold-chain environments. The observed activity involved proxying and spam delivery rather than documented loss of temperature control.

severity.reason: Three refrigeration controllers were confirmed in the SMTP cluster, and the report described them as compromised and used for proxy exits and spam. No service interruption, data theft, financial loss, or food-safety consequence was reported.

incidents.title: Web3Auth flaw exposed Keplr wallet private keys
incidents.victim: Web3Auth and Keplr users who created wallets with Google or Apple login
incidents.attacker: Unknown; Web3Auth and Keplr confirmed unauthorized exploitation, but did not identify the attacker.
incidents.what: An attacker exploited a flaw in Web3Auth infrastructure supporting certain Keplr social-login wallets, resulting in a private-key breach for some Google- and Apple-linked accounts. Web3Auth also moved funds from other at-risk wallets into recovery wallets, with assistance from Keplr.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: Private-key access enabled unauthorized transfers from affected cryptocurrency wallets. Keplr paused Google and Apple sign-in while investigating; the companies have not reported the full scope or final losses.
incidents.significance: The incident compromised reusable wallet credentials and led to confirmed unauthorized cryptocurrency movement. GoPlus reported at least about $1 million stolen, while Bitquery recorded $6.01 million moved from more than 44,000 wallets, much of it apparently transferred for recovery rather than theft.

severity.reason: Web3Auth and Keplr confirmed the infrastructure flaw and private-key compromise; users experienced unauthorized wallet transfers and the login service was paused. GoPlus reported at least about $1 million stolen, but the companies have not confirmed a final loss total, and many transfers were rescue operations.

incidents.title: BOSSAI agents accessed emergency and institutional data
incidents.victim: Taipei emergency-dispatch system and fire-service technology, a Taiwanese lending firm, three Thai universities, and Mexican individuals whose records were collected from public-sector and telecom sources
incidents.attacker: Acronis researchers attribute the operation with high confidence to a single attacker probably based in Hualien City, Taiwan; motive and sponsorship are unclear.
incidents.what: The attacker operated BOSSAI, a system of 12 AI agents, nine of which were used to scan targets and conduct attacks. The agents pulled Taipei 119 emergency-dispatch records covering seven districts, accessed at least 18 database tables at a fire-dispatch technology vendor after logging in with default root credentials, extracted data from a Taiwanese lender through SQL injection, collected data from three Thai universities through SQL injection, and obtained about 206,800 Mexican home-phone records containing names and addresses.
incidents.ai_role: AI agents carried out unauthorized scanning, credential-based access, SQL injection, and data collection under the attacker's direction. The agents were run mainly on locally hosted models with safety training removed; commercial models generally refused direct attack requests.
incidents.why: The campaign demonstrated operational use of AI agents to reach hundreds of organizations across at least 11 countries and resulted in confirmed access to or collection of emergency-service, medical, personal, financial, and university data. Many other targets were only scanned or unsuccessfully attacked, and the reporting does not establish service disruption or the full scope of stolen data.
incidents.significance: Researchers found the attacker’s operational server containing agent conversations, command history, credentials, tools, and victim data. Confirmed activity included emergency-dispatch records, access to fire-service databases, lender data extraction, university data collection, and approximately 206,800 Mexican phone records.

severity.reason: Researchers observed confirmed unauthorized access to and collection of emergency-service, medical, personal, financial, and university data across Taiwan, Thailand, and Mexico. No operational outage or financial loss was reported; some additional targets were only scanned or unsuccessfully attacked.

incidents.title: LNbits server exploited to withdraw users’ Lightning funds
incidents.victim: Kevin Ravensberg’s LNbits server and BitTipBot users; other LNbits operators were warned of attacks
incidents.attacker: Unknown; the server operator and LNbits developers confirmed exploitation, but did not identify the attacker.
incidents.what: An attacker exploited an LNbits extension vulnerability to withdraw 2,285,545 satoshis, approximately 0.023 bitcoin, from an operator’s server. The operator said the attack ran from 09:22 to 14:00 UTC before the project issued its first warning; the exact exploited extension had not been publicly named.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The compromise resulted in cryptocurrency theft and temporarily prevented BitTipBot users from reaching their funds. LNbits also shut down its hosted my.lnbits.com instances while fixes were pending, although the total number of affected servers and overall loss remained unknown.
incidents.significance: The operator reported an actual unauthorized withdrawal of 2,285,545 satoshis, and LNbits urged all operators to shut down servers because the vulnerability remained unpatched. The broader attack scope and total financial impact were not established.

severity.reason: A confirmed exploited server lost 2,285,545 satoshis, and BitTipBot users temporarily could not access funds. The report provides no US-dollar loss figure or confirmed count of additional compromised servers.

incidents.title: Ethersphere releases compromised to steal Swarm wallet keys
incidents.victim: Ethersphere project and users of bee-js and Swarm Desktop
incidents.attacker: Unidentified attackers used stolen Ethersphere CI credentials; Socket and Pluto Security linked the payloads with high confidence to the group behind SleepyDuck, but attribution is not confirmed.
incidents.what: Attackers used the project's release automation to publish malicious bee-js 13.3.0 and Swarm Desktop 0.56.2 releases. The payload could send Swarm wallet key files and plaintext passwords to the attackers, install backdoors on Windows, macOS, and Linux, and provide remote access.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: This was a confirmed compromise of production release infrastructure and a software supply-chain attack. The releases were available on npm for about 75 minutes and Swarm Desktop for about 8.5 hours; the malicious versions were withdrawn, but no wallet-fund theft had been reported.
incidents.significance: Attackers abused trusted GitHub, npm, signing, and notarization workflows to distribute malware through legitimate project releases. The malware targeted wallet credentials and installed persistent backdoors, although the number of compromised machines and any resulting theft were not established.

severity.reason: The malicious releases were published through compromised release automation and downloaded, with Swarm Desktop downloads reaching 65 and bee-js estimated at about 10 downloads; those counts included researchers, scanners, and mirrors. No theft of wallet funds or confirmed infected-machine count was reported.

incidents.title: Bitter campaign deploys PapRAT against South Asian organizations
incidents.victim: South Asian organizations; specific victims were not reported
incidents.attacker: Bitter, also known as APT-C-08, APT-Q-37, Hazy Tiger, Orange Yali, T-APT-17, and TA397; attribution is based on Fortinet FortiGuard Labs analysis
incidents.what: Fortinet observed a campaign using LNK, VHDX, URL shortcut, WebDAV, MSI, and PowerShell execution chains to deploy the previously unreported PapRAT remote-access trojan. PapRAT supports remote shell and command execution, file upload/download/deletion, directory and drive enumeration, screenshots, and PowerShell execution; reconnaissance data was exfiltrated to attacker-controlled infrastructure.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The campaign establishes persistent remote access and enables collection or manipulation of files and system information on compromised organizational systems. Fortinet observed multiple infection chains and exfiltration behavior, although specific victims and final operational consequences were not reported.
incidents.significance: Fortinet researcher evidence documents active malware deployment against organizations, including reconnaissance collection and exfiltration to command-and-control infrastructure. The campaign uses several delivery chains and a customizable RAT capable of sustained remote control.

severity.reason: Fortinet reported observed PapRAT deployment against South Asian organizations and exfiltration of reconnaissance data. The available reporting does not establish service outages, destructive effects, stolen sensitive records, or financial loss.

incidents.title: Iris Plaza cloud breach may expose data of 7.7 million people
incidents.victim: Iris Ohyama and its Iris Plaza online shopping platform customers
incidents.attacker: Unknown; Iris Plaza said it had not identified the perpetrators and received no direct attacker communication.
incidents.what: Unauthorized access was confirmed in a third-party cloud service used by the Iris Plaza online store. Data potentially accessed included names, physical addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, gender, dates of birth, and encrypted account passwords, affecting up to 5.8 million members and former members and 1.9 million non-members.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The incident involved confirmed unauthorized access to a trusted third-party cloud service and potentially exposed sensitive personal data at widespread scale. Iris Plaza suspended its online store and related systems, while the final number of affected records remains under investigation.
incidents.significance: Iris Plaza confirmed third-party unauthorized access and potential exposure of personal information belonging to up to 7.7 million people. The incident also caused the temporary suspension of Iris Plaza and related service websites.

severity.reason: The company confirmed unauthorized access and potential access to personal and account data for up to 7.7 million people. Online shopping and related service systems were suspended; as of November 5, no misuse or financial loss tied to the incident had been reported.

incidents.title: SonicOS SSL-VPN MFA-bypass flaw exploited in attacks
incidents.victim: Organizations operating SonicWall firewalls with affected SonicOS SSL-VPN SAML configurations; specific victims were not reported
incidents.attacker: Unknown; SonicWall investigated a report of exploitation, and CISA listed CVE-2026-19868 as known exploited
incidents.what: Attackers exploited CVE-2026-19868 to bypass SAML authentication controls, potentially including SAML-enforced MFA, when valid credentials for an alternate authentication method were available.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The exploitation could provide unauthorized access through enterprise remote-access infrastructure despite enforced MFA. SonicWall and CISA confirmed exploitation, but the reporting gives no victim, access, or downstream-impact details.
incidents.significance: This is an exploited authentication-bypass flaw affecting SSL-VPN access and capable of undermining SAML-enforced MFA. CISA's KEV listing corroborates real-world exploitation, although affected organizations and consequences remain undisclosed.

severity.reason: SonicWall and CISA substantiate exploitation of the authentication-bypass vulnerability, but the available reporting does not establish which victims were compromised or what access attackers obtained beyond the bypass capability.

incidents.title: Crédit Mutuel Arkéa account used in major fraudulent transfer attack
incidents.victim: Crédit Mutuel Arkéa
incidents.attacker: Unidentified attacker; Crédit Mutuel Arkéa described it as a sophisticated attack and is investigating with authorities.
incidents.what: The attacker reached Arkéa's network through a service-provider platform, obtained access to the bank's own account, and initiated fraudulent transactions to other banking organizations before converting funds into cryptocurrency. The bank suspended certain systems and said some funds were blocked.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: This was a confirmed compromise of a major banking group that enabled fraudulent transactions potentially worth tens or hundreds of millions of dollars and caused delays to some transfers. Customer assets were reportedly unaffected, but the final stolen amount and attack method remain under investigation.
incidents.significance: Crédit Mutuel Arkéa confirmed the incident and acknowledged a significant financial order of magnitude; reporting cited an estimate of up to $133 million, although the bank did not confirm that exact loss.

severity.reason: Arkéa confirmed attackers accessed the banking group through a service provider and used its account for unauthorized transfers. The reported loss is estimated above $133 million, but the bank has not finalized the amount; customer accounts and assets were reportedly unaffected.

updates.what: Attackers used Arkéa’s own account to transfer funds to other financial institutions, with some assets potentially converted to cryptocurrency. Arkéa said customer accounts and assets were not accessed, and some converted assets were frozen.

incidents.title: Chainalysis discloses AI-driven breach exposing customer data
incidents.victim: Chainalysis
incidents.attacker: An external actor using offensive agentic techniques; attribution not reported.
incidents.what: Chainalysis said the attacker gained unauthorized access to its systems and internal tools. The accessed data included some non-sensitive customer information, including user IDs, full names, email addresses, and organization role labels.
incidents.ai_role: Chainalysis attributed the intrusion to offensive agentic techniques used by the external actor.
incidents.why: The company confirmed an AI-involved compromise of internal systems and exposure of customer-related records, while stating that investigation content, transaction or query results, plaintext passwords, credentials, and secrets were not compromised.
incidents.significance: Chainalysis confirmed unauthorized access to internal systems and tools and exposure of customer identity and organizational-role data. The full scope and number of affected individuals remain under investigation.

severity.reason: Chainalysis confirmed exposure of data for all users and took multiple products offline after abnormal activity. The available report does not establish final misuse or financial loss.

updates.what: Chainalysis said the actor gained unauthorized access to its systems and internal tools.
