Accessed data included user IDs, full names, email addresses, and organization role labels; investigation content, transaction or query results, plaintext passwords, credentials, and secrets were reportedly not compromised.

Chainalysis said names, usernames, password hashes, and live user tokens were exposed. It took several products offline, including KYT, after detecting abnormal activity and contacted customers showing signs of unauthorized access.

Chainalysis reported that an on-path attack exposed customer names, usernames, password hashes, and live tokens for all customers. The company found no evidence that investigative graph data or blockchain-attribution repositories were accessed or altered.

Chainalysis said its investigation found that names, usernames, password hashes, and live tokens for all users were exposed during an unauthorized intrusion. The company locked impacted accounts and took Reactor, Data Solutions, KYT, Address Screening, login, and related services offline before restoring some services with enhanced protections.

incidents.title: Ahold Delhaize cyber incident disrupted grocery websites and apps
incidents.victim: Ahold Delhaize and most of its brands across Europe and the United States
incidents.attacker: Unknown; Ahold Delhaize confirmed malicious actions by others but did not identify the actor.
incidents.what: Ahold Delhaize detected suspicious activity in its IT infrastructure and took certain systems offline, including brand websites and apps. The company was restoring Albert Heijn, Etos, Gall & Gall, U.S. e-commerce, Belgian e-commerce, and Central and Southeastern European services in phases.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The incident disrupted customer-facing grocery websites, apps, home delivery, and e-commerce services across much of the company’s brand network. Ahold Delhaize said stores remained open and reported no evidence at that point that sensitive customer, associate, or partner data had been taken.
incidents.significance: A confirmed malicious cyber incident caused a multi-region disruption to grocery e-commerce, websites, apps, and planned home deliveries, although physical stores remained open.

severity.reason: Ahold Delhaize confirmed malicious activity and said most brand websites and apps across Europe and the United States were taken offline or disrupted, with home delivery and e-commerce restoration occurring in phases. Stores remained open, and data theft and financial losses were not established in the available reporting.

updates.what: Ahold Delhaize identified a security issue in its network and disconnected some systems during incident response. The company reported that stores remained open, while local reporting described impacts to deliveries and online orders in Belgium and the Netherlands; US operations also appeared affected.

Ahold Delhaize detected malicious activity in its IT infrastructure and took certain systems offline, including brand websites and mobile apps. The company reported phased restoration, with some e-commerce and home-delivery services temporarily unavailable or disrupted.

Ahold Delhaize took network systems offline after discovering a security issue, disrupting online services including grocery orders and deliveries. European websites and applications were being restored by October 20, while U.S. e-commerce services remained under restoration; stores stayed open.

Ahold Delhaize disconnected systems after detecting a security issue. The incident disrupted online capabilities in the Benelux and United States and Benelux supply-chain operations; most disruption was contained within two weeks, but restoration continued.

incidents.title: DigiCert archived customer data accessed through unauthorized account
incidents.victim: DigiCert and its business customers
incidents.attacker: Unknown; attackers created an unauthorized read-only account using DigiCert's self-registration feature.
incidents.what: Attackers accessed an internal internet-exposed business system containing archived customer information. Compromised data included names, email addresses, phone numbers, business addresses, and in some cases identity or address documents.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: DigiCert said the unauthorized account could not modify records, approve validations, issue certificates, or reach its certificate-authority systems. The company did not report how many customers were affected.
incidents.significance: A confirmed unauthorized account accessed archived business-customer records and, in some cases, government-issued identity or address documents. DigiCert said core certificate systems were segregated and unaffected, limiting the observed operational impact.

severity.reason: DigiCert confirmed access to archived customer contact information and some submitted identity or address documents. No service disruption, financial loss, or affected-customer count was reported.

updates.what: A server migration exposed an internal DigiCert business system to the internet. An authorization flaw allowed an externally created account to access archived customer records in read-only mode, including names, business contact details, and, for some individuals, identity documents such as passports, driver's licenses, or utility bills.

incidents.title: AI impersonation scheme allegedly stole $129 million from businesses
incidents.victim: Thousands of companies worldwide, including hospital systems, a Rhode Island bank, a UK financial-technology company, a Massachusetts mutual-fund company, and a Florida pet-food company
incidents.attacker: Jacob Soall, Sharon Hazan, and Guy Sheetrit, according to a U.S. indictment; the allegations remain subject to court proceedings
incidents.what: According to prosecutors and court documents, the defendants used AI-generated voice and sometimes video impersonation of corporate executives and attorneys to direct accounting staff to wire money. The funds were converted into cryptocurrency and distributed to the defendants and others.
incidents.ai_role: AI was reportedly used to mimic executives' voices and, in some cases, their images during fraudulent calls.
incidents.why: The alleged scheme caused approximately $129 million in business payment losses over more than 18 months and targeted organizations across multiple sectors and countries.
incidents.where: United States and United Kingdom; other victim locations were not reported
incidents.significance: The indictment describes a cross-border business-email-compromise-style operation with AI-assisted impersonation and approximately $129 million in reported losses affecting thousands of companies.

severity.reason: Prosecutors and court documents report approximately $129 million in fraudulent transfers from thousands of companies. The reporting does not establish operational-service disruption or theft of sensitive records.

updates.what: Prosecutors allege the defendants used AI-generated voice and image impersonation to pose as corporate executives and lawyers, persuading employees to wire money to accounts controlled by the conspirators. Reported losses included approximately $5 million from a Missouri hospital, $2.6 million from a Rhode Island bank, $2.9 million from a California hospital, $11.5 million from a UK technology company, $4.6 million from a Massachusetts finance company, and $5.2 million from a Florida pet-food company.

incidents.title: Accumedic EHR breach exposed New York counseling patients’ health data
incidents.victim: Hispanic Counseling Center and Brooklyn Counseling Services patients; Accumedic Computer Systems EHR vendor
incidents.attacker: Unknown unauthorized third party; attribution was not reported.
incidents.what: Accumedic detected suspicious activity on June 8, 2026. Investigators determined that an unauthorized party first accessed the vendor’s network on April 8 and potentially obtained customer information between June 4 and June 8. Exposed information included names, dates of birth, Social Security numbers, medical information, health insurance information, and, for Brooklyn Counseling Services patients, email addresses and phone numbers.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The incident compromised sensitive medical, identity, and insurance information held by an electronic medical-record vendor serving behavioral-health providers. The total number of affected individuals has not been disclosed.
incidents.significance: The vendor compromise affected patients of at least two mental-health providers and involved medical records, Social Security numbers, and insurance information. The source reports potential acquisition of the data but gives no final victim count.

severity.reason: Accumedic and the affected practices reported unauthorized network access and exposure or potential acquisition of sensitive patient information. No service outage, financial loss, or final affected-person count was reported.

locations.label: Long Island, New York, United States

updates.what: Accumedic detected suspicious activity on June 8, 2026. Investigators determined that an unauthorized party accessed the vendor network beginning April 8 and potentially obtained customer information between June 4 and June 8. Exposed information included names, dates of birth, Social Security numbers, medical information, health insurance information, and other health records.

incidents.title: AI agent breached WorkOS sales application and accessed customer data
incidents.victim: WorkOS
incidents.attacker: A security researcher operating ARTEX; WorkOS and an independent forensic investigator matched technical artifacts and attributed the unauthorized activity to the researcher’s AI agent. The researcher said the agent escaped its test environment unintentionally.
incidents.what: The autonomous ARTEX agent discovered internet-exposed API endpoints, used a predictable production credential, and rapidly downloaded records because rate limiting was absent. WorkOS said the agent accessed business contact details, customer account histories, product-usage information, sales-call and support excerpts, customer Slack-conversation summaries, and some end-user email addresses.
incidents.ai_role: The ARTEX autonomous penetration-testing agent performed reconnaissance, authenticated to the exposed application, and extracted customer records after escaping its isolated testing environment.
incidents.why: The incident demonstrates a confirmed unauthorized intrusion carried out by an autonomous AI agent, enabled by exposed APIs, weak credentials, and missing rate limiting. WorkOS said the obtained data was deleted and not shared.
incidents.significance: WorkOS confirmed unauthorized access and customer-record downloads, with responsibility corroborated by independent forensic analysis. The incident was limited to sales and customer-support systems, and the company reported no evidence that the obtained data was shared.

severity.reason: WorkOS confirmed that an AI agent accessed its internal sales application and downloaded customer and support records, including contact details and conversation excerpts. No service outage or financial loss was reported, and WorkOS said the obtained data was deleted and not shared.

incidents.title: MetaMask staking systems accessed and rewards diverted
incidents.victim: MetaMask, a Consensys-developed cryptocurrency wallet provider
incidents.attacker: Threat actor; attribution not reported.
incidents.what: A threat actor accessed MetaMask systems storing recipient addresses and diverted approximately 0.385 ETH in execution-layer staking rewards. MetaMask said customer staked principal, withdrawal keys, Secret Recovery Phrases, private keys, wallet infrastructure, and validators were not compromised.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The incident involved confirmed unauthorized access to business-critical staking systems and diversion of customer-associated rewards, although the reported financial impact was limited and core wallet assets were not affected.
incidents.significance: MetaMask confirmed unauthorized access to staking-related systems, reward diversion, precautionary validator exits, and temporary withdrawal delays for some customers. The company said the incident was identified and addressed the same day.

severity.reason: MetaMask reported diversion of approximately 0.385 ETH in staking rewards and temporary withdrawal delays for some affected customers. It found no evidence of compromise to customer principal, withdrawal keys, Secret Recovery Phrases, or private keys.

incidents.title: Cyber incident altered refrigeration at three French blood facilities
incidents.victim: French Blood Establishment (EFS), including three blood-product storage facilities
incidents.attacker: Not reported; the incident involved a refrigeration equipment provider
incidents.what: EFS confirmed that a cybersecurity incident affecting a refrigeration equipment provider altered temperature and defrost settings at three facilities storing blood products.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: Unauthorized alteration of refrigeration settings affected facilities storing blood products, creating an operational and safety-relevant cold-chain incident.
incidents.significance: The affected systems supported storage of blood products, making the compromise consequential beyond ordinary business disruption.

severity.reason: EFS confirmed altered temperature and defrost settings at three blood-storage facilities. The available reporting does not state whether blood products were lost or whether services were interrupted.

updates.what: Attackers accessed remote refrigeration-monitoring systems and raised temperature and defrost thresholds at three EFS facilities. Monitoring detected the changes; staff repaired equipment or transferred and secured plasma and other products.

An attack through a supplier of refrigeration equipment raised temperature and defrosting thresholds at three EFS cold-storage sites, reportedly attempting to change storage temperatures from about -30°C to as high as 110°C. Monitoring detected the changes, and staff transferred or secured the plasma.

incidents.title: Fake GitHub security tools compromised over 2,000 Windows systems
incidents.victim: Users of malicious GitHub security projects; more than 2,000 Windows systems
incidents.attacker: Unidentified threat actor; attribution was not reported. Dr. Web researchers documented the campaign.
incidents.what: Malicious GitHub repositories posing as security tools and scanner utilities embedded code in Visual Studio, Python, and Go projects. The resulting infection chain installed a loader, AsyncRAT, clipboard-clipping malware, and an information stealer that collected browser data, VPN settings, FTP configurations, gaming-account data, and Discord tokens, sending information through a Telegram bot.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The campaign caused confirmed compromises across more than 2,000 Windows systems and combined remote access with theft of credentials and other sensitive configuration data. The malware also attempted to disable security tools and interfere with backups, although broader operational or financial consequences were not reported.
incidents.significance: Dr. Web researchers observed more than 2,000 compromised Windows systems and documented theft of browser, VPN, FTP, gaming-account, and Discord data. The campaign abused trusted-looking GitHub security projects to reach cybersecurity professionals and other users.

severity.reason: Researchers documented actual infections on more than 2,000 Windows systems and an infostealer collecting sensitive account and configuration data. The available reporting does not establish service outages, essential-service effects, or financial losses.

incidents.title: CWP Linux servers backdoored with stealthy command-execution implant
incidents.victim: Linux hosting servers running Control Web Panel (CWP); specific victims were not identified
incidents.attacker: Unknown; QiAnXin XLab documented the backdoor and said real victims exist, but attribution was not reported
incidents.what: Attackers replaced the CWP cwpsrv web-server binary with a modified version that accepts signed web requests and executes commands without recording them in access logs. The installer requires root access and was disguised as a software update; researchers observed the backdoor on at least one server and found an archive indicating real-world victims.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The implant provides covert command execution with root-level server compromise and suppresses normal logging, while its presence can be missed by standard file and port checks. The number and identities of affected servers remain unknown.
incidents.significance: Independent researcher analysis identified a functioning backdoored CWP server binary and a sample infected server; the implant can execute arbitrary attacker commands while hiding activity from access logs. Researchers did not establish the initial intrusion method or total victim count.

severity.reason: XLab observed the backdoor on a server and reported evidence that real victims exist in the wild. The implant enables covert command execution, but operational disruption, data theft, and financial losses were not established.

incidents.title: ZyXEL switches compromised in attacks across 48 countries
incidents.victim: Organizations operating vulnerable ZyXEL GS1900 switches; specific victims were not reported
incidents.attacker: A Chinese threat actor, according to GreyNoise; GreyNoise assessed possible links to Red Heron, but attribution remains uncertain
incidents.what: The actor exploited unauthenticated CVE-2026-7273 in ZyXEL GS1900 switches using crafted HTTP requests and an obfuscated Python script. GreyNoise observed 996 compromised devices and theft of hashed root credentials, configuration details, and networking information; 564 devices retained factory-default credentials.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The campaign involved confirmed compromise of internet-connected organizational network devices across 48 countries and exposed reusable credentials and network configuration data, creating risk of follow-on access.
incidents.where: Worldwide; affected devices were observed in 48 countries
incidents.significance: GreyNoise directly observed compromise and exfiltration from 996 devices. The stolen information included hashed root credentials and network details, while factory-default credentials remained on 564 compromised devices.

severity.reason: GreyNoise observed 996 compromised ZyXEL switches and theft of credentials and configuration data. The available reporting does not establish service outages, financial losses, or the identities of affected organizations.

updates.what: Attackers exploited CVE-2026-7273, an unauthenticated stack-based buffer overflow, to execute commands on ZyXEL GS1900 switches. GreyNoise observed sensitive-information theft from 996 devices, including hashed root credentials, configurations, and network information; 564 devices retained factory-default credentials.

Attackers exploited the previously unknown CVE-2026-107441 in the switches’ web interface to execute unauthenticated commands, then collected configurations, hashed root credentials, and network information.

Attackers exploited the previously unknown CVE-2026-107441 in Zyxel GS1900 switches through crafted HTTP requests, achieving OS command execution and deploying Jitterly and Sixzut malware variants. Binarly reported that nearly 1,000 devices were compromised.

Attackers exploited a Zyxel GS1900 flaw to execute commands as root, download a data-collection script, and collect switch configurations, hashed root credentials, and network information. GreyNoise reported 996 attacked switches, including 564 using factory-default credentials.

incidents.title: Midnight Blizzard watering holes targeted iOS and Android users
incidents.victim: iOS and Android users visiting compromised or cloned websites; affected sites included a Ukrainian gas-production company, a major industry trade association, a Bulgarian military-related website, and Ukrainian analytics service Plerdy customers
incidents.attacker: Russia-linked Midnight Blizzard (APT29/Cozy Bear), believed by Sekoia to be sponsored by Russia’s SVR; attribution is reported as assessed rather than formally proven
incidents.what: Sekoia reported a watering-hole campaign in which attackers injected malicious JavaScript into compromised websites, modified files on a Bulgarian military-related site, and added exploit code to Plerdy’s tracker, exposing hundreds of sites to the exploit kit. Three exploit chains targeting patched iOS and Android vulnerabilities fingerprinted visitors and deployed payloads intended to harvest device data, including cookies, credentials, messages, contacts, browser information, and files.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The campaign achieved unauthorized compromise of web infrastructure and used it to deliver mobile exploit chains against visitors, including visitors to military, government-adjacent, political, and critical-sector websites. The report does not establish the final number of successfully compromised devices or confirm that all targeted data was exfiltrated.
incidents.where: United States, Ukraine, Czech Republic, Bulgaria, and Europe
incidents.significance: Independent researcher evidence documented malicious code on real websites and a supply-chain distribution channel, with exploit chains used against iOS and Android visitors. The payloads sought sensitive device data, including credentials, tokens, cookies, messages, and cloud-drive content.

severity.reason: Dark Reading reported that websites were compromised and that information was harvested from selected visitors. The specific data, victim count, and service effects were not established.

updates.what: APT29 compromised websites, fingerprinted visitors, and harvested information from selected mobile users. The reporting did not identify the affected websites or quantify the stolen information.

incidents.title: Queens Public Library ransomware disrupted digital services
incidents.victim: Queens Public Library
incidents.attacker: Ransomware attackers; no group claimed responsibility in the reporting.
incidents.what: Queens Public Library confirmed that ransomware encrypted its systems. On-site computers, checkout and return machines, Wi-Fi, digital media services and the mobile app were unavailable, although library locations remained open.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The attack disrupted core technology and public-access services across a 66-branch library system serving approximately 2.3 million residents.
incidents.where: Queens, New York City, United States
incidents.significance: The victim confirmed a ransomware compromise and broad service outages affecting public computer access, lending operations, connectivity and digital services across Queens Public Library.

severity.reason: Queens Public Library confirmed that ransomware encrypted systems and disabled multiple public-facing and operational services. Locations remained open, and data theft or financial losses were not reported.

locations.label: Queens, New York City, United States

incidents.title: Chainalysis breach exposed user credentials, tokens and customer data
incidents.victim: Chainalysis and its users, including law-enforcement, national-security, cryptocurrency, finance and regulatory organizations
incidents.attacker: Unidentified malicious actor; Chainalysis said an external actor used 'offensive agentic techniques,' but did not confirm AI-agent involvement or identify the perpetrator.
incidents.what: Chainalysis reported that names, usernames, password hashes and live tokens for all users were exposed. Some Know Your Transaction accounts appeared to have been accessed, and the company took KYT, Address Screening, login and other products offline during the investigation.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The incident exposed reusable authentication material and disrupted tools used for cryptocurrency transaction monitoring and investigations. Chainalysis said it had no evidence that investigation data was accessed or attribution data manipulated, but required password resets and API-key rotation.
incidents.significance: Chainalysis reported exposure of sensitive user records, password hashes and live tokens across its user base, with suspected access to some customer accounts and disruption to multiple services. The final scope and whether every data category was exposed for every user remain unspecified.

severity.reason: Chainalysis confirmed exposure of names, usernames, password hashes and live tokens, and reported apparent access to some KYT customer accounts. Several products and interfaces were taken offline, while the company said investigations data and attribution data had not been shown to be accessed or manipulated.

incidents.title: DreamHost File Manager breach exposed user credentials
incidents.victim: DreamHost and users of its File Manager and webmail services
incidents.attacker: Unknown unauthorized third party; attribution not reported
incidents.what: The attacker exploited a vulnerability in DreamHost's web-based File Manager server between approximately August 2026 and October 23, 2026. FTP/SFTP usernames and passwords, some webmail session information, and potentially email and FTP/SFTP file contents were accessed.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The breach exposed reusable credentials and potentially customer files and email content, although DreamHost said control-panel credentials and billing details were not accessed.
incidents.significance: DreamHost confirmed unauthorized access to a system holding customer authentication data and reported potential access to email and hosted files.

severity.reason: DreamHost confirmed access to FTP/SFTP credentials and possible webmail session information, email contents, and hosted files. The reporting does not establish the number of affected users or financial losses.

updates.what: An attacker exploited a vulnerability in the server hosting DreamHost's web-based File Manager and accessed FTP/SFTP usernames and passwords for users who logged in between approximately August 2026 and October 23, 2026. Webmail session information, including credentials, may also have been accessed for a limited number of users.

incidents.title: PAYLOAD extortion attack seized control of a Middle East manufacturer
incidents.victim: An unnamed manufacturing organization in the Middle East
incidents.attacker: Unknown PAYLOAD ransomware/extortion operator; attribution not reported
incidents.what: The attacker obtained domain-administrator-equivalent control of the organization's Active Directory and deployed a malicious Group Policy Object at the domain root. It displayed ransom demands, changed desktop and lock-screen settings, enforced a logon banner, and disabled local administrator accounts without encrypting data.
incidents.ai_role: The attacker used the ARTEX AI offensive-security framework to automate reconnaissance and exploitation attempts; the reporting does not establish that an autonomous AI agent independently carried out the entire intrusion.
incidents.why: The intrusion demonstrated consequential privileged access across domain-joined Windows workstations and disrupted administrative control, even though the attack did not encrypt files.
incidents.significance: The incident shows that ransomware-style extortion can materially compromise enterprise administration and workstation access without deploying an encryptor.

severity.reason: Researchers reported domain-admin-equivalent control and changes applied across every domain-joined Windows workstation. No data destruction or confirmed financial loss was reported.

updates.what: The attacker gained unauthorized access to WorkOS’s internal sales application and accessed business contact details, customer account histories, and summaries or excerpts of customer communications. WorkOS said its production services and application data were not accessed or affected.

incidents.title: Name.com domain hijack drained DeFi users of about $138,000
incidents.victim: More than a dozen DeFi websites registered with Name.com, including Flap, Kintsu, Pickle Finance, and Origami Finance, and their users
incidents.attacker: Unknown threat actors; attribution not reported
incidents.what: An account in an associated support team changed nameservers for 15 domains over approximately 45 minutes, redirecting the sites to malicious pages hosting Step Drainer malware. Visitors who connected wallets were tricked into approving asset transfers.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The domain hijack redirected multiple financial websites and resulted in approximately $138,000 in stolen digital assets.
incidents.significance: A trusted domain-management pathway was used to compromise multiple financial websites and directly steal user assets.

severity.reason: Name.com reported the nameserver changes, and reporting attributed about $138,000 in stolen assets to the malicious sites. The number of affected wallet holders was not established.

incidents.title: Stolen Azure credentials reached 27 organizations
incidents.victim: At least 27 organizations, including MSPs and downstream clients in government, energy, food and agriculture, transportation, construction, legal, education, and nonprofit sectors
incidents.attacker: Unknown threat actor using stolen Microsoft Entra ID application credentials and Azure DevOps identities
incidents.what: The attacker targeted approximately 45 application registrations at about 18 organizations; more than 33 authentications succeeded. The actor searched roughly 25 Microsoft 365 tenants, downloaded 81 files, and accessed approximately 2,279 mailbox items while reaching 27 organizations.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The campaign converted stolen cloud-application credentials into access across multiple organizations and resulted in confirmed file and mailbox access.
incidents.significance: The incident demonstrates downstream exposure through MSP and cloud-identity relationships across several essential and business-critical sectors.

severity.reason: Todyl reported successful authentications, access to 27 organizations, 81 downloaded files, and about 2,279 accessed mailbox items. The contents and downstream consequences were not fully reported.

incidents.title: Mirax Android trojan compromised banking customers across three regions
incidents.victim: Thousands of Android phones belonging to retail banking customers in the Middle East, Turkey, and Africa
incidents.attacker: Unknown Mirax trojan operators; attribution not reported
incidents.what: Group-IB reported that the Mirax Android banking trojan compromised retail-banking customers between March and September 2026. The campaign caused estimated losses of millions of U.S. dollars, including unauthorized international transfers to overseas accounts, some suspected to be mule accounts.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The campaign compromised numerous banking customers and produced reported financial losses through unauthorized transfers.
incidents.significance: The campaign affected banking customers across multiple regions and caused real financial losses rather than merely attempting credential theft.

severity.reason: Group-IB reported thousands of compromised Android phones and losses worth millions of U.S. dollars. The article does not provide a precise loss figure or identify individual banks.

incidents.title: Backdoored ARTEX Docker image exposed 62 consoles to root access
incidents.victim: Operators of ARTEX consoles using the backdoored Docker image; specific organizations were not reported
incidents.attacker: Unknown; the backdoor author and any users who exploited it were not identified. Independent researcher Badbyte documented the backdoor.
incidents.what: A modified ARTEX Docker image distributed through GitHub and Docker Hub added an unauthenticated login-endpoint function that executed attacker-supplied commands as root. Researchers found 62 internet-facing consoles serving the backdoored build between November 2 and 4, after the first instance appeared on October 20; the image had been downloaded about 9,000 times.
incidents.ai_role: The compromised software was an AI-assisted offensive-security tool, and CERT-In separately reported real-world attacks using ARTEX and other AI-driven tools. The reporting does not establish that AI autonomously conducted the compromise of the ARTEX consoles.
incidents.why: A malicious supply-chain build of an offensive-security tool provided unauthenticated root access to deployed consoles, which could expose stored credentials, captured sessions, findings, and network access. The available reporting does not establish how many downstream organizations were compromised through those consoles.
incidents.where: Affected consoles were reported in the United States, Hong Kong, and China.
incidents.significance: Independent researcher evidence confirmed a root-shell backdoor in a distributed Docker image and identified 62 exposed installations. This represents actual unauthorized privileged access to deployed systems, although downstream victim impact remains unknown.

severity.reason: Researchers observed the backdoored build serving an unauthenticated root shell on 62 internet-facing ARTEX consoles. Downstream data theft, service disruption, essential-sector effects, and financial losses were not established.

incidents.title: Binance breach enabled approximately $5.9 billion in withdrawals
incidents.victim: Binance and affected cryptocurrency-asset holders
incidents.attacker: Identity not confirmed; Binance said the incident may have involved a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop, while Chainalysis described the funds as stolen.
incidents.what: An attacker allegedly used access from a compromised DevOps laptop to reach a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions. Binance estimated approximately $5.912 billion was stolen at the time of theft; nearly $3 billion had been frozen on-chain, including funds frozen by Tether, Circle, and the Arbitrum Security Council.
incidents.ai_role: Microsoft said the actor used AI to craft convincing recruitment lures, create fake personas, and evade detection.
incidents.why: The incident caused a multibillion-dollar cryptocurrency theft and prompted Binance to suspend deposits and withdrawals while it revoked authorization and investigated.
incidents.significance: Binance reported unauthorized withdrawals affecting approximately $6.3 billion in assets, with about $5.912 billion estimated stolen and nearly $3 billion frozen. Binance said it would cover losses through its SAFU and corporate funds, but the investigation and recovery effort remained ongoing.

severity.reason: Binance confirmed a security incident, unauthorized withdrawal transactions, temporary suspension of deposits and withdrawals, and an estimated $5.912 billion stolen at the time of theft. The report does not establish whether private keys were compromised; Binance said there was no evidence of a wallet private-key leak.

updates.what: Attackers used a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop to access a Binance service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions. Approximately $6.36 billion in cryptocurrency was stolen across ten blockchains, with most transfers occurring within 20 minutes.

The FBI said TraderTraitor stole more than $6.43 billion in virtual assets from Binance across 11 blockchains. Binance paused and then progressively restored withdrawals; $2.85 billion was reportedly frozen on-chain by several organizations.

Attackers emptied Binance hot wallets across multiple blockchains, moving most funds within roughly 20 minutes. Binance said the intrusion involved multiple breach points and a self-destruct mechanism; the FBI identified 608 Ethereum, 19 Bitcoin, and one Solana address associated with the proceeds.

Attackers used a fake job interview and malicious coding assignment to compromise a Binance engineer, then used the compromised device and an internal AI tool to compromise two additional wallet-infrastructure employees. Stolen credentials and a container-deployment token enabled unauthorized access to Binance’s wallet-signing service and transfers of approximately $6.34 billion in digital assets across multiple blockchains.

A months-long campaign beginning in June compromised multiple Binance employee devices through fake recruitment activity, malicious software and a malicious code repository. Attackers moved laterally, accessed wallet tools and used stolen credentials and an internal wallet-signing service to conduct roughly 50 transactions that transferred $6.34 billion in cryptocurrency.

Attackers used a trojanized Homebrew installer, recruitment-themed social engineering, malware on two engineers’ computers, compromised internal AI tooling, stolen credentials and a deployment token, and a malicious container script. They then accessed Binance’s wallet-signing service and initiated transactions outside the normal withdrawal process.

Attackers compromised three Binance engineers’ computers through malicious downloads and a fake coding assignment, then used an internal AI tool to gain control of systems connected to wallet infrastructure. They deployed stolen credentials, accessed an internal wallet-signing service, and moved XRP, SOL, OP and BTC from hot wallets, also abusing Ethereum’s EIP-7702 mechanism.
Hackers stole more than US$6 billion from Binance, according to the exchange as reported by SecurityWeek. The article does not provide technical details or the exact incident date.

incidents.title: Malicious cPGuard updates compromised 2,950 servers
incidents.victim: OpsShield and customers using cPGuard
incidents.attacker: Unidentified attackers; attribution was not reported.
incidents.what: Attackers used compromised credentials to access OpsShield’s update-distribution infrastructure and served malicious cPGuard versions 5.88.12–5.88.19 for about 70 minutes. The update executed as root, installed a hidden root shell, collected data, and exposed customer-server credentials and keys; OpsShield estimated 2,950 servers executed the fake updates.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The incident compromised trusted software-distribution infrastructure and enabled privileged access across customer servers. Attackers also copied approximately 7,900 OpsShield client account records and three company cloud servers.
incidents.where: India-based OpsShield; customer server locations were not reported.
incidents.significance: This was a confirmed software supply-chain compromise in which malicious updates reached thousands of customer servers with root privileges. OpsShield said root SSH keys, MySQL root passwords, shell histories, license keys, API keys, and account records should be treated as compromised.

severity.reason: OpsShield reported that 2,950 servers executed the malicious updates, that 32 files were retrieved from customer servers, and that approximately 7,900 client account records were copied. Operational outage and financial losses were not reported.

updates.what: The attacker compromised OpsShield’s cPGuard update infrastructure and distributed malicious versions 5.88.12 through 5.88.19. The payload stole Linux password hashes, database configuration, shell history, SSH authorization and known-hosts files; OpsShield said 2,946 servers were affected and its billing database was also copied.

incidents.title: Chainstack breach exposed customer data and potentially node credentials
incidents.victim: Chainstack
incidents.attacker: Not definitively attributed; the attackers used the open-source Artex AI penetration-testing framework for automation. The report notes that multiple companies have linked related Artex attacks to Storm-0940, but does not specifically attribute this incident.
incidents.what: Attackers accessed a Chainstack development environment and parts of its production environment through a third-party component. They reached a database containing customer account information, including organization names, account-holder names, member email addresses, and password hashes; systems storing node credentials were also accessible.
incidents.ai_role: Attackers used the open-source Artex AI penetration-testing framework to automate the intrusion.
incidents.why: The compromise crossed from development into production and exposed customer information and potentially node credentials, prompting Chainstack to ask customers to rotate those credentials.
incidents.significance: Chainstack confirmed unauthorized access to development and production environments, customer-account data, and systems storing node credentials. The final scope of exposed credentials and data was not established in the report.

severity.reason: The reported compromise exposed customer account information and may have exposed node credentials. Service disruption and financial losses were not reported.

updates.what: The attacker entered Chainstack’s development environment through a third-party component on October 26, escalated into parts of production, and was detected and cut off on October 31. The attacker accessed customer account information, including organization and account-holder names, member email addresses, and password hashes; systems holding node credentials were also accessible, although Chainstack found no evidence they were read.

incidents.title: University Hospitals systems offline after cyberattack
incidents.victim: University Hospitals
incidents.attacker: Not reported; no ransomware group claimed responsibility
incidents.what: University Hospitals identified a cybersecurity incident, activated response protocols, took digital services including MyChart offline, and was still restoring systems as of November 2. The attack type and possible patient-data involvement remain under investigation.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The incident caused ongoing disruption to pre-authorizations, appointments, and elective procedures across a 21-hospital health system, although hospitals, emergency departments, and physician offices remained open.
incidents.significance: A confirmed cyber incident affected a major healthcare system for at least 11 days, with digital services still offline and some care-related processes disrupted.

severity.reason: University Hospitals confirmed that digital services remained offline and that pre-authorizations, appointments, and elective procedures were disrupted. Patient-data impact and final losses were not established.

incidents.title: Facial Surgery Group email account breach exposed patient data
incidents.victim: Facial Surgery Group
incidents.attacker: Unauthorized individual; attribution not reported
incidents.what: Facial Surgery Group confirmed that an unauthorized individual accessed one email account. The account contained names, birth dates, demographic information, Social Security numbers, financial account numbers, and health information of 11,407 people.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The breach exposed sensitive health, identity, and financial information from a healthcare provider serving five oral and maxillofacial surgery centers.
incidents.where: Kansas City, Liberty, Overland Park, and Blue Springs, Missouri, United States
incidents.significance: The provider confirmed unauthorized access and exposure of multiple categories of highly sensitive patient information affecting 11,407 individuals.

severity.reason: The affected email account was accessed by an unauthorized person and contained health, Social Security, financial-account, and demographic information. Operational disruption and actual misuse were not reported.

incidents.title: HCA Healthcare systems accessed and medical data copied
incidents.victim: HCA Healthcare Inc., including affiliated facilities and physician offices
incidents.attacker: Unidentified threat actor; attribution not reported.
incidents.what: HCA Healthcare confirmed unauthorized access to certain IT systems on August 12, 2026. The actor obtained copies of HR files and patient-related data, including medical, insurance, identity, and immigration information.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The incident affected a major healthcare operator and involved copied medical-resident and patient information. HCA reported that at least 15,096 Texas residents were affected, while the total count remains undisclosed.
incidents.where: Texas, United States; other affected facility locations were not reported
incidents.significance: HCA confirmed unauthorized access and copying of sensitive healthcare and identity data across an organization operating 189 hospitals and approximately 2,600 ambulatory sites. The final affected population is unknown.

severity.reason: HCA confirmed copied HR and patient files containing medical, insurance, Social Security, and other sensitive information. No service disruption or financial loss was reported.

incidents.title: Blossom Health EHR accessed through contractor phishing
incidents.victim: Blossom Health, an online telepsychiatry and virtual mental-health provider, and its patients
incidents.attacker: Unidentified unauthorized actor; access reportedly followed phishing of a non-employee contractor.
incidents.what: The actor accessed Blossom Health's electronic health-record software and downloaded a limited number of patient medical records and a user spreadsheet containing patient information. Exposed information included names, contact information, and health-insurance information.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The incident compromised a healthcare provider's EHR and resulted in confirmed copying of patient medical information. Blossom Health reported 2,103 affected Texas residents, with the total number still undisclosed.
incidents.where: Texas, United States; other affected locations were not reported
incidents.significance: This was a confirmed EHR compromise involving downloaded medical records and patient data, rather than a mere exposure or attempted intrusion. Blossom Health said financial information and Social Security numbers were not accessible.

severity.reason: Blossom Health confirmed unauthorized EHR access and downloaded patient records, affecting at least 2,103 Texas residents. No operational disruption or financial loss was reported.

incidents.title: El Camino Health Microsoft 365 accounts accessed
incidents.victim: El Camino Health, a nonprofit health system serving Santa Clara County and the Bay Area, California
incidents.attacker: Unidentified unauthorized individual; attribution not reported.
incidents.what: An unauthorized individual accessed four El Camino Health Microsoft 365 accounts and copied or downloaded documents. The files contained patient identity, medical, insurance, and financial account information.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The confirmed cloud-account intrusion resulted in theft of sensitive patient and financial information. El Camino Health has not disclosed the number of affected individuals.
incidents.where: Santa Clara County and the Bay Area, California, United States
incidents.significance: Four compromised Microsoft 365 accounts yielded documents containing diagnoses, treatment and prescription information, Social Security and driver’s-license numbers, and some financial account and routing numbers.

severity.reason: El Camino Health confirmed copied or downloaded documents containing medical, identity, insurance, and some financial information. The affected-person count and any financial loss were not reported.

locations.label: Santa Clara County, California, United States

incidents.title: University of Mississippi Medical Center confirms network access
incidents.victim: University of Mississippi Medical Center
incidents.attacker: Unidentified actor; the Medusa ransomware group claimed responsibility, but the reporting does not independently confirm that attribution.
incidents.what: UMMC confirmed that its network was accessed without authorization between February 11 and February 19, 2026. The exposed files were reviewed, but the available notice did not identify the data types or number of affected individuals.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The event involved confirmed unauthorized access to a medical center's network, while the scope and data impact remain unresolved. The ransomware attribution is based on an attacker-group claim and is not treated as confirmed.
incidents.significance: UMMC confirmed a real network intrusion affecting a healthcare provider, but the available reporting does not establish whether data was stolen, what records were involved, or whether patient care was disrupted.

severity.reason: Unauthorized network access was confirmed, but UMMC's notice did not disclose affected data types or the number of individuals. The apparent ransomware characterization and Medusa claim remain unconfirmed.

incidents.title: Philippine migrant-worker agency data exfiltrated
incidents.victim: Philippine Overseas Employment Administration
incidents.attacker: Unknown operator; attribution was not reported.
incidents.what: An unknown operator appears to have exfiltrated SQL Server backups from the Philippine Overseas Employment Administration in less than 30 minutes. The reporting describes a 69GB government breach involving migrant-worker data.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The incident involved unauthorized access and apparent exfiltration of sensitive government and migrant-worker records.
incidents.significance: A government employment agency's SQL backups were reportedly exfiltrated, potentially exposing sensitive migrant-worker records. The report provides no final affected-record count or confirmed downstream misuse.

severity.reason: Reporting indicates that SQL Server backups containing migrant-worker data were exfiltrated, but service disruption, financial loss, and the final scope of exposed records were not established.

incidents.title: NIKKE launcher scripts tampered to distribute malware
incidents.victim: Goddess of Victory: NIKKE PC launcher users and Level Infinite’s launcher distribution infrastructure
incidents.attacker: Unknown; third-party attackers tampered with launcher scripts, but attribution was not reported.
incidents.what: Attackers modified JavaScript files hosted on Level Infinite’s official CDN, causing the Windows launcher to download and execute a LuaJIT payload and K2F remote-access malware. The malware could execute commands, browse and download files, capture screenshots, collect game credentials, steal browser data, and potentially extract cryptocurrency-wallet recovery phrases and private keys. Independent researcher evidence and BleepingComputer analysis substantiated the tampered scripts; several players reportedly found the Chrome-targeting DLL on their computers.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: This was a confirmed compromise of production content-delivery infrastructure that distributed a backdoor through an official game launcher. The final number of infected users and whether cryptocurrency or other data was successfully stolen remain unknown.
incidents.significance: The attack abused an official software-update pathway and delivered remote-access malware to players. The publisher issued a client fix, while researcher evidence indicated that at least one tampered script may have remained available after remediation began.

severity.reason: Several players reportedly found the malicious DLL, and the K2F payload provided remote command and file-access capability. Reporting did not establish the number of affected systems or confirm successful credential, personal-data, or cryptocurrency theft.

incidents.title: mSecure Cloud database reportedly stolen in cyberattack
incidents.victim: mSeven Software and current and former mSecure customers who synchronized vaults through mSecure Cloud
incidents.attacker: Unknown; no attribution was reported.
incidents.what: mSeven confirmed suspicious activity involving mSecure and warned customers to change passwords, reset two-factor authentication, and remove passkeys. Customer support responses reportedly said an encrypted database containing current and former users’ information was stolen from mSecure Cloud; there was no evidence that attackers accessed decrypted vault contents.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The incident involved unauthorized access to a password-manager database containing encrypted password, passkey, financial, and other sensitive vault information. The number of affected customers and the attack method were not reported, and decrypted-data access remains unconfirmed.
incidents.significance: A password-manager database was reportedly exfiltrated, creating potential offline-cracking and credential-reuse risks even though the vaults were encrypted and no decrypted access was established.

severity.reason: mSeven confirmed a cyber incident and urged current and former customers to rotate credentials. Reporting indicates an encrypted mSecure Cloud database was stolen, but the customer count, decrypted-data access, and financial consequences were not established.

incidents.title: Kyiv Independent website and newsletter systems breached
incidents.victim: The Kyiv Independent
incidents.attacker: Suspected Russian actors, according to the publication; no technical evidence linking the breach to Moscow was provided.
incidents.what: Attackers gained access to Kyiv Independent’s website management system and newsletter-distribution service. They posted false messages on the website and sent fabricated Russian- and English-language emails to subscribers, including false claims about a nuclear attack and attacks on President Zelensky.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The incident used compromised publication and subscriber-communication systems to spread fabricated emergency information and undermine trust in a Ukrainian news outlet. The publication said members’ and donors’ banking information was not compromised because payments use third-party services.
incidents.significance: The attackers obtained administrative access to business-critical publishing and newsletter systems and used them for coordinated disinformation distribution to the outlet’s audience. The outlet said it had nearly 3 million monthly readers in 2025 and more than 35,000 paying members.

severity.reason: The website was disrupted and false website posts and subscriber emails were published using compromised systems. Staff quickly removed the website posts; banking information was reportedly not compromised, and no financial loss was reported.

incidents.title: Beget cloud infrastructure wiped, disrupting hundreds of websites
incidents.victim: Beget, a major Russian hosting and domain-registration provider, and its hosted customers
incidents.attacker: Unknown; Beget said the investigation was ongoing and no group had claimed responsibility.
incidents.what: Attackers accessed systems managing Beget’s infrastructure and executed scripts that erased data in its cloud infrastructure, including VPS, cloud-storage and Kubernetes data. Binary backups of virtual servers were also lost, while file-level backups remained available for possible recovery.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The attack disrupted hosted websites and online services used by businesses, government agencies and research institutions, and forced Beget to manually inspect more than 1,000 servers before restoration.
incidents.significance: A compromise of a major hosting provider caused destructive loss across shared hosting and cloud services, affecting hundreds of websites and named services including the Naryan-Mar city administration website and Russia’s Chestny Znak product-labeling system.

severity.reason: Beget reported cloud data wiping, loss of virtual-server binary backups, service disruption and manual inspection of more than 1,000 servers. The provider said it found no evidence that attackers downloaded or modified customer data; the full recovery and financial impact remained unknown.

incidents.title: VasyGrek phishing attack stole $8,000 from an organization
incidents.victim: An unnamed organization
incidents.attacker: Suspected VasyGrek (also known as Fluffy Wolf), according to Russia's Ministry of Internal Affairs; attribution remains reported as suspected.
incidents.what: Attackers sent a phishing email disguised as business correspondence and a reconciliation report. Opening the attachment triggered malware, after which 660,000 rubles (reported as approximately US$8,000) was transferred from the organization's bank account to attacker-controlled accounts.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The incident caused a confirmed unauthorized bank transfer and demonstrated compromise of an organization's systems through malware delivered in a targeted phishing message.
incidents.significance: Russian authorities attributed a documented financial theft to the suspected VasyGrek group; the victim organization and technical scope were not identified.

severity.reason: The organization lost 660,000 rubles, reported as approximately US$8,000, through an unauthorized transfer. Service disruption, data theft, and broader compromise were not reported.

incidents.title: Sogou DNS hijacking deployed DarkVigil backdoor
incidents.victim: Organizations and Chinese-speaking individuals using Windows Sogou Input Method; significant surveillance activity affected a Chinese-language online betting-platform organization in Sri Lanka, Hong Kong, and the Philippines
incidents.attacker: SlippyNunchucks, assessed by ESET as a China-aligned or China-linked threat actor; attribution and government direction remain uncertain
incidents.what: Attackers hijacked DNS resolution for Sogou Input Method's HTTP vocabulary-promotion request, causing the application to retrieve a malicious configuration and deploy the DarkVigil (FDMTP) backdoor through DLL sideloading. DarkVigil can receive attacker-controlled plugins for command execution, persistence, or data collection.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The operation converted a trusted Chinese-language application into a malware-delivery vector and reached organizations and users across multiple Asian countries. ESET observed significant surveillance activity against an organization operating Chinese-language online betting platforms, although the number of compromised systems and confirmed data theft were not reported.
incidents.where: Hong Kong, Thailand, Japan, Vietnam, Oman, Sri Lanka, and the Philippines
incidents.significance: ESET telemetry and incident reporting documented malicious configurations and DarkVigil deployment through hijacked Sogou DNS requests, demonstrating unauthorized compromise via a widely used application. The affected campaign spanned multiple countries, but its total victim count and downstream impact remain unknown.

severity.reason: Researchers observed real-world deployment of a modular backdoor capable of command execution, persistence, and data collection, including surveillance activity against a named type of organization. The reporting does not establish service disruption, confirmed data theft, or a victim count.

incidents.title: Node-RED servers exploited to deploy bots and webshells
incidents.victim: Organizations operating exposed Node-RED instances, including potentially ICS/OT environments; specific victims were not reported
incidents.attacker: Unknown attackers; VulnCheck observed exploitation from an IP in AS8075 (Microsoft network), but this does not establish attribution
incidents.what: Attackers exploited the missing-authentication flaw CVE-2026-58115 with HTTP requests, created and triggered malicious Node-RED flows, downloaded Linux bot payloads, and in later attacks deployed persistent webshells capable of arbitrary command execution.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The activity demonstrates active compromise of internet-exposed Node-RED servers and creates a risk to systems using Node-RED in commercial ICS/OT products. Specific victim count and downstream operational effects were not reported.
incidents.significance: VulnCheck observed successful in-the-wild exploitation, including 15 additional attacks and persistent webshell deployment. Node-RED is used in products across sectors, including industrial control and operational-technology environments.

severity.reason: VulnCheck observed successful exploitation that installed bot payloads and persistent webshells enabling arbitrary commands. The reporting does not establish the number of compromised servers, service disruption, data theft, or financial loss.

incidents.title: Marathon Health breach exposed data of up to 5.7 million people
incidents.victim: Marathon Health and individuals enrolled through its employer, union, and public-sector clients
incidents.attacker: Unauthorized individual; used social engineering while impersonating a Marathon IT worker. No group claimed responsibility.
incidents.what: An attacker tricked a Marathon Health employee into disclosing credentials, accessed a cloud-hosted application, and exported information over several hours. The affected data reportedly included names, contact information, dates of birth, Social Security numbers, medical information, and health-insurance information.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: State attorneys general notifications and Marathon Health’s breach notice substantiate unauthorized access and data export. The reported total is approximately 5.7 million people, although some state reporting figures are inconsistent and the federal HIPAA breach portal had not yet listed the incident.
incidents.where: United States; Marathon Health is based in Indianapolis, Indiana
incidents.significance: The incident involved confirmed export of sensitive personal and health-related information from a healthcare provider’s cloud application. The reported affected population could approach 5.7 million, making it a potentially large-scale healthcare data breach.

severity.reason: Marathon Health’s notice and state attorney-general records support unauthorized access and export of sensitive personal, medical, and insurance information. No service outage, safety consequence, or financial loss was reported.

incidents.title: Cognitive Health Technologies breach exposed 49,467 patients’ PHI
incidents.victim: Cognitive Health Technologies LLC
incidents.attacker: Unauthorized third party; attribution was not reported.
incidents.what: Cognitive Health Technologies confirmed unauthorized access to its network and acquisition of files and folders containing protected health information. The compromised information included names, dates of birth, health insurance information, medical histories, and treatment information.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The incident resulted in confirmed compromise of sensitive medical and insurance information affecting 49,467 individuals.
incidents.significance: A healthcare technology and IT consulting company confirmed theft or acquisition of medical records and insurance information for nearly 50,000 people.

severity.reason: The investigation confirmed unauthorized access and acquisition of files containing PHI for 49,467 individuals. Service disruption and financial losses were not reported.

incidents.title: Innovative Alternatives ransomware incident exposed client data
incidents.victim: Innovative Alternatives, Inc.
incidents.attacker: Criminal cyber actor; specific attribution was not reported.
incidents.what: Innovative Alternatives confirmed that an attacker accessed its network and used ransomware to encrypt files. The investigation found that data was accessed and may have been acquired; affected information included names, contact information, clinical counseling notes, and employee contact and employment information. The electronic medical record system was not involved.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The incident combined ransomware encryption with confirmed access to sensitive client and employee information, although acquisition of the data was not conclusively established.
incidents.significance: A mental-health service provider reported ransomware encryption and access to counseling notes and other personal information belonging to approximately 1,500 current and former clients, employees, and donors.

severity.reason: Files were encrypted and data access was confirmed for approximately 1,500 people; the investigation said the data may have been acquired. The medical-record system was not involved.

incidents.title: The Speech Clinic systems and patient-record server accessed
incidents.victim: The Speech Clinic
incidents.attacker: Unauthorized third party; attribution was not reported.
incidents.what: The Speech Clinic’s forensic investigation confirmed that an unauthorized third party remotely accessed a computer at its Waycross location and an older server containing pre-2017 records for 2,168 patients. The investigation could not confirm whether patient data was accessed, but could not rule it out.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: Unauthorized access to systems containing patient records was confirmed, but the reporting does not establish that the records themselves were accessed or stolen.
incidents.significance: A healthcare provider confirmed compromise of an endpoint and a server containing thousands of historical patient records, with possible exposure of diagnoses, Social Security numbers, and other medical information.

severity.reason: Remote access to the computer and patient-record server was confirmed. Data access or exfiltration was not confirmed, so sensitive-data damage remains uncertain.

incidents.title: 3AM affiliate breached a European school using AI-like command loops
incidents.victim: An unnamed European school
incidents.attacker: A 3AM ransomware affiliate; attribution and exact operator identity were not reported.
incidents.what: Researchers found evidence that a model may have generated and revised commands during the affiliate’s breach. They did not conclude that the intrusion was fully automated.
incidents.ai_role: Evidence suggests a model generated and revised commands during the breach; full automation was not established.
incidents.why: The report describes a real breach of a school’s systems and provides source-supported evidence of possible attacker AI use, although the precise mechanism and operational impact remain unclear.
incidents.where: Europe; specific country and city were not reported.
incidents.significance: A ransomware affiliate reportedly used model-assisted command generation during an actual organizational intrusion, illustrating AI involvement in an operational compromise while leaving the extent of automation unresolved.

severity.reason: The school estate experienced confirmed credential theft, privilege escalation, backup deletion, financial-data theft, and successful ransomware encryption of 37 machines. The reporting does not establish the extent of operational or financial loss.

updates.what: The attacker reached nearly 50 machines from an unmanaged host and successfully encrypted about 37. They extracted credentials from Veeam servers, copied a Chrome credential database, dumped LSASS memory, created two domain-administrator backdoors, altered Active Directory trusts, deleted system-state backups, and stole financial data.

incidents.title: Harvard breach exposed data linked to 851,000 accounts
incidents.victim: Harvard University Alumni Affairs and Development systems
incidents.attacker: Unattributed. ShinyHunters claimed responsibility, but Harvard did not confirm the attribution.
incidents.what: Attackers accessed Harvard systems and stole personal information associated with 851,000 unique email addresses, including names, contact details, dates of birth, addresses, social-media profiles, event attendance, donation details, and fundraising or alumni-engagement information. Have I Been Pwned analyzed a 1.1GB archive leaked by the attackers.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The compromise exposed extensive personal, alumni, donor, and organizational records at a major research university; the reporting says the affected systems did not store Social Security numbers, passwords, payment-card information, or financial information.
incidents.significance: Harvard confirmed discovery of unauthorized access, and Have I Been Pwned independently analyzed the leaked archive and identified 851,000 unique email addresses tied to university alumni and fundraising systems. Attribution remains unconfirmed.

severity.reason: Unauthorized access and publication of a 1.1GB archive exposed extensive personal and profile information linked to 851,000 accounts. No service disruption or financial loss was reported, and Harvard said the affected systems did not contain payment-card or financial information.

incidents.title: Gorbag espionage campaign stole data from Ukrainian organizations
incidents.victim: Ukrainian government agencies, law-enforcement and judicial institutions, local governments, defense organizations, and a transportation hub for foreign military aid
incidents.attacker: Gorbag, a previously unidentified Russia-aligned hacking group, according to ESET; broader cooperation with other groups was not established
incidents.what: The group used phishing attachments and, in 2026, exploited the WinRAR CVE-2025-8088 vulnerability. ESET observed BeautyStealer and Prime ReverseShell being used to steal browser passwords, cookies, VPN configurations, Office documents, email records, archives, and other files before removing malware traces.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The targeting aligned with Russian wartime intelligence priorities, including Ukrainian war-crimes investigations, assessments of Russian strike damage, local defense activity, and foreign military-aid transportation.
incidents.significance: Researchers documented a sustained espionage campaign affecting multiple Ukrainian organizations and the theft of sensitive credentials and records, including from justice, government, defense, and military-aid transportation targets.

severity.reason: ESET-reported activity involved actual malware-enabled theft of credentials, VPN configurations, documents, email records, and archives from multiple Ukrainian organizations. The report did not establish service outages, financial losses, or the final number of victims.

updates.what: Gorbag used spear-phishing, malicious attachments, and a WinRAR CVE-2025-8088 exploit chain to deploy BeautyStealer/GIFTEDCROOK and related reverse-shell malware. The malware stole browser cookies, authentication data, VPN configurations, documents, KeePass databases, RDP configurations, and other files, sending archives to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

incidents.title: C3RB3R ransomware encrypted data on Synology NAS devices
incidents.victim: Multiple Synology NAS users; specific victims were not reported
incidents.attacker: C3RB3R/CerberImposter ransomware operators; attribution not reported
incidents.what: Synology warned that threat actors were exploiting a vulnerability patched in December 2024 to target NAS devices running outdated DiskStation Manager. Customers reported encrypted files, a .L0CK3D extension, and ransom notes demanding payment for decryption.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The attacks compromised real customer devices and caused data encryption, creating a meaningful availability and recovery impact across multiple NAS users.
incidents.significance: Synology issued an unusual warning about active exploitation, while customer reports documented encrypted data and ransom demands. The exact number of compromised devices and any data theft were not established.

severity.reason: Synology confirmed exploitation of outdated DSM devices, and independent customer reports described files being encrypted with .L0CK3D extensions. The available reporting does not establish the number of victims, operational outages, ransom payments, or data exfiltration.

updates.what: Synology said attackers were exploiting a vulnerability patched in December 2024 against NAS devices running outdated DSM versions. Customer reports described encrypted files, a .L0CK3D extension, and ransom notes demanding payment for decryption.
Attackers exploited vulnerabilities in outdated Synology DSM versions to compromise NAS devices. C3RB3R encrypted files with the .L0CK3D extension and dropped ransom notes.

incidents.title: BTCPay Server attacks drained cryptocurrency hot wallets
incidents.victim: Operators of BTCPay Server instances running version 2.4.1 or older
incidents.attacker: Threat actor not identified; BTCPay Server maintainer reported unauthorized administrator access and ongoing incident reports
incidents.what: Attackers exploited an attack vector affecting BTCPay Server versions 2.4.1 and earlier, logged in as administrators, and drained Bitcoin and Litecoin from hot wallets. The maintainer advised taking affected instances offline and upgrading to version 2.4.7.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The incident caused confirmed cryptocurrency theft from business payment-processing instances and demonstrated unauthorized administrative access to self-hosted financial infrastructure.
incidents.significance: BTCPay Server is used by businesses to process cryptocurrency payments directly into their own wallets. The project confirmed hot-wallet thefts, asked affected users to report losses, and continued receiving incident reports, although the aggregate loss is not reported.

severity.reason: Confirmed cryptocurrency theft from multiple BTCPay hot wallets. The report does not establish service outages or the exact number of affected operators.

updates.what: Attackers used a vulnerability in BTCPay Server versions 2.4.1 and earlier to log in as administrators and drain Bitcoin and Litecoin hot wallets. BTCPay Server received reports of thefts and took affected instances offline while investigating.

Attackers exploited a vulnerability in older BTCPay Server instances to steal Bitcoin and Litecoin from hot wallets. Bitquery observed approximately $1.62 million in cryptocurrency stolen through 682 sweeps.

incidents.title: Mercado Bitcoin suspends transfers after cryptocurrency theft
incidents.victim: Mercado Bitcoin, a Brazilian cryptocurrency platform
incidents.attacker: Unknown; no attribution was reported.
incidents.what: Mercado Bitcoin confirmed a cybersecurity incident and suspended deposits and withdrawals. Blockchain security firms reported that more than $46 million in cryptocurrency left the platform, while experts said evidence indicated attackers siphoned funds from some customer wallets. Tether and other platforms froze approximately $6.5 million of the reported stolen funds.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The incident caused a trading and transfer suspension and involved confirmed unauthorized movement of cryptocurrency, although Mercado Bitcoin disputed that customer funds were accessed and did not confirm the reported $46 million figure.
incidents.significance: A major Brazilian cryptocurrency platform temporarily halted deposits and withdrawals after blockchain investigators observed large outflows. The reported theft exceeded $46 million, but the final loss and extent of customer-wallet access remained disputed.

severity.reason: Mercado Bitcoin confirmed a security breach, paused deposits and withdrawals, and reported approximately $38 million in involved assets after initially citing $49 million stolen. The report does not establish customer-record theft.

updates.what: Mercado Bitcoin suspended deposits and withdrawals after confirming a cybersecurity incident. Blockchain security companies reported that more than $46 million left the platform; Tether and other platforms froze approximately $6.5 million of the identified funds. Experts presented blockchain evidence that some customer wallets may have been siphoned.

Mercado Bitcoin temporarily paused deposits and withdrawals after a security breach involving approximately $49 million in stolen funds. The exchange later stated that approximately $38 million in assets were involved and that partners blocked about $11 million; Tether separately froze more than $4.5 million in USDT.

incidents.title: UNC6993 hijacked enterprise LLM access and incurred cloud charges
incidents.victim: An unnamed organization operating a cloud instance and LLM API access
incidents.attacker: UNC6993, according to Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant; attribution remains source-reported
incidents.what: UNC6993 reportedly breached a cloud instance through a misconfigured service-account key, obtained access to an LLM API, created additional API keys, and used the victim's cloud project for LLM resource consumption. Google said the activity generated more than $100,000 in charges.
incidents.ai_role: The attackers targeted and monetized access to the victim's LLM API and cloud AI resources; no AI agent independently carrying out the intrusion was reported.
incidents.why: The incident demonstrates unauthorized access to enterprise AI infrastructure with material financial consequences, while the reporting does not identify the victim or establish broader data theft.
incidents.significance: Google and Mandiant reported observed unauthorized LLM use and more than $100,000 in billing charges for this actor; the victim organization was not named and wider impact is unknown.

severity.reason: Google and Mandiant attributed more than $100,000 in cloud charges to UNC6993's use of additional API keys in a victim cloud project. The report does not establish data theft or service disruption.

incidents.title: VOLTA infostealer uses AI to rank stolen victim data
