incidents.victim: Windows users targeted by VOLTA-AUTODOXER; specific victims were not reported
incidents.attacker: Unknown malware operator; attribution was not reported. Cisco Talos researchers identified the malware.
incidents.what: Cisco Talos researchers identified VOLTA-AUTODOXER, a Windows infostealer that harvests browser credentials and cookies, payment cards, cryptocurrency-wallet seed phrases, messaging and gaming sessions, OAuth tokens, SSH and cloud keys, Wi-Fi profiles, screenshots, and Gmail receipt data. The malware exfiltrates collected data and AI-generated assessments through Telegram.
incidents.ai_role: VOLTA sends structured bundles of stolen victim data through OpenRouter to Claude Opus 4.6, with fallback to Kimi K2 and Gemini 2.5 Flash, to rank victims and monetizable assets. AI involvement is source-supported attacker use.
incidents.why: The AI triage layer turns stolen credentials, financial information, private records, and access tokens into prioritized victim dossiers, potentially helping operators select high-value targets for further exploitation or extortion.
incidents.significance: Researcher analysis documents a mature infostealer designed to collect sensitive data and transmit it for AI-based monetization assessment. The malware's collection and exfiltration capabilities include reusable credentials, payment information, wallet seed phrases, and cloud keys, although the report does not quantify confirmed victims or losses.

severity.reason: Cisco Talos observed and analyzed malware capable of stealing sensitive records, credentials, payment data, and cryptocurrency-wallet seed phrases, followed by exfiltration over Telegram. The available reporting does not establish the number of compromised victims or realized financial losses.

incidents.title: Polymarket halted trading after DebugBear script compromise
incidents.victim: Polymarket and users of Polymarket.com; DebugBear third-party RUM service
incidents.attacker: Unknown; researchers traced approximately $2.57 million in POL transfers to a suspected attacker-controlled wallet.
incidents.what: Attackers compromised Polymarket’s third-party DebugBear monitoring service and distributed malicious JavaScript through its infrastructure. The script targeted authenticated Polymarket sessions, attempted to liquidate prediction-market positions and transfer cryptocurrency or tokens, and communicated account and transaction data to attacker-controlled infrastructure.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The compromise affected a cryptocurrency prediction-market platform and its trusted third-party script provider, creating a path to unauthorized financial transactions. Polymarket temporarily halted trading and said it would reimburse affected traders, but it did not disclose the number of affected users or confirmed stolen amount.
incidents.significance: Polymarket confirmed the third-party-provider compromise and temporarily suspended trading. Hudson Rock researcher evidence and blockchain analysis identified malicious code and approximately $2.57 million in transfers to a suspected attacker wallet, although the final theft and affected-user count remain unconfirmed.

severity.reason: Polymarket experienced outages and temporarily halted trading. Security companies traced more than $2.1 million in cryptocurrency losses to user accounts, but the final loss and number of victims were not established by the company.

updates.what: Attackers compromised DebugBear's third-party monitoring service and distributed malicious JavaScript through its infrastructure. The script targeted authenticated Polymarket sessions, attempted to liquidate prediction-market positions and transfer cryptocurrency, and sent account and transaction data to DebugBear infrastructure.

Polymarket’s international platform entered cancel-only mode after unauthorized withdrawals. Hudson Rock found malicious JavaScript delivered through a DebugBear address that reused authenticated trading authority to sell positions or transfer position tokens; Polymarket said the provider was compromised and pledged to reimburse affected traders.

Polymarket said a compromised third-party provider caused outages and that it temporarily halted trading. Hudson Rock and blockchain security companies linked the incident to code that siphoned more than $2.1 million in cryptocurrency from user accounts, although the total loss and victim count were not independently established by Polymarket.

Attackers replaced the DebugBear page-speed script loaded by Polymarket with malicious code. The script abused signed-in traders’ browser sessions and transaction-signing mechanisms to sell positions or transfer funds; blockchain records showed about $2.64 million reaching the attackers’ wallet from 33 wallets.

Attackers compromised DebugBear DNS records and served malicious JavaScript through Polymarket's website. The script targeted logged-in traders, used active trading sessions to dump or transfer positions, and affected 726 wallets; Polymarket reported approximately $2.7 million stolen directly.

An attacker replaced the performance-monitoring script loaded by Polymarket.com with code that used active user sessions to sell positions and transfer funds. Polymarket paused trading, reset active sessions, and reported $2.7 million in initial losses plus $1.2 million related to the shutdown; 95% of affected wallets had been refunded by the report date.

incidents.title: Florida financial-aid breach exposed records of 4.9 million people
incidents.victim: Florida Department of Education, including the Florida Student Financial Aid website
incidents.attacker: Unknown; Florida Department of Education reported access by an unauthorized party and did not identify the attacker.
incidents.what: An unauthorized party accessed a system or database containing financial-aid applicant information, including names, addresses, phone numbers, genders, email addresses, Social Security numbers, and dates of birth. The state took the financial-aid website offline and began an investigation with the Florida Digital Service and Florida Department of Law Enforcement.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The incident exposed sensitive identity and financial-aid applicant data for approximately 4.9 million people, creating substantial identity-theft risk. Financial aid disbursements, tuition payments, scholarships, grants, and student loans were reported as unaffected.
incidents.significance: Florida officials confirmed unauthorized access and warned that sensitive records, including Social Security numbers and dates of birth, were exposed for nearly 5 million financial-aid applicants. The affected site was taken offline, although core aid payments and programs continued.

severity.reason: The Florida Student Financial Aid website was taken down and other department services could face temporary disruption, but financial-aid disbursements and related programs were reported unaffected. Officials confirmed exposure of sensitive personal records affecting approximately 4.9 million people; financial losses were not reported.

updates.what: Hackers breached the Florida Student Financial Aid website. Potentially accessible data included names, Social Security numbers, dates of birth, addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, and gender codes. The department detected the intrusion on October 19 and contained it.

incidents.title: Ivanti Connect Secure attack chain gained root access
incidents.victim: A limited number of Ivanti Connect Secure customers, including one investigated by Volexity
incidents.attacker: UTA0576, an attribution by Volexity to a previously unknown threat actor; criminal motivation assessed with low confidence
incidents.what: Attackers chained CVE-2026-104935, CVE-2026-111357, and CVE-2026-118527 to obtain unauthenticated root-level code execution on fully patched Ivanti Connect Secure appliances. Volexity observed credential theft, data exfiltration, network scanning, and log tampering.
incidents.ai_role: Volexity assessed with medium confidence that UTA0576 used large language models for exploit development and post-exploitation activity.
incidents.why: The incident involved confirmed exploitation of VPN appliances and consequential privileged access, credential theft, data exfiltration, and log tampering at a limited number of customers.
incidents.significance: Volexity observed real-world exploitation beginning October 3, including root access to fully patched appliances and theft or attempted concealment activity. The newly reported vulnerabilities extend the previously tracked Connect Secure attack chain.

severity.reason: Volexity reported root-level compromise, credential theft, data exfiltration, network scanning, and log tampering at a limited number of customers. The reporting does not establish service disruption, financial losses, or the final number of affected organizations.

updates.what: Attackers chained three zero-days to obtain unauthenticated, root-level access to a fully patched Ivanti Connect Secure appliance. They stole domain credentials, exfiltrated limited Active Directory metadata, searched for LAPS passwords and BitLocker recovery keys, conducted reconnaissance and credential attacks, and tampered with logs.

Volexity observed exploitation in the wild during the first week of October using a chain of three zero-day vulnerabilities against a fully patched Ivanti Connect Secure appliance. The attackers achieved remote root-level code execution and could steal credentials and exfiltrate data.

incidents.title: Connecticut DSS breach affected 41,000 people
incidents.victim: Connecticut Department of Social Services
incidents.attacker: Unknown; no attribution reported.
incidents.what: A hacking incident involving a provider reimbursement account exposed or impermissibly accessed protected health information of 41,000 people.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The incident affected a state public-service agency and thousands of healthcare-related records through unauthorized access to a reimbursement account.
incidents.significance: HHS OCR reporting records a confirmed hacking/IT incident affecting 41,000 individuals at a state department.

severity.reason: DSS confirmed exposure of protected health information and Medicaid claims/payment records, but did not establish data theft or service disruption.

updates.what: An unauthorized user accessed a Connecticut Medicaid provider reimbursement account. Claims and payment information was exposed; data theft could not be ruled out.

incidents.title: Public Partnerships breach involved insider data theft
incidents.victim: Public Partnerships LLC
incidents.attacker: A former network facilitator; the report describes insider data theft rather than external attribution.
incidents.what: A former facilitator stole data from a network server, affecting protected health information of 12,018 people.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The report explicitly characterizes the event as insider data theft involving a healthcare business associate.
incidents.significance: Confirmed theft by a trusted insider affected more than 12,000 healthcare records.

severity.reason: Public Partnerships confirmed that sensitive participant records were offered for sale; the attempted transaction was refused and no completed sale was reported.

updates.what: Public Partnerships learned that a former facilitator had attempted to sell consumer data to another New York CDPAP facilitator. The recipient refused the offer and reported it; the data included names, addresses, dates of birth, Medicaid IDs, PPL IDs, and Medicaid enrollment information.

incidents.title: Hattiesburg Eye Clinic patient data exposed after network disruption
incidents.victim: Hattiesburg Eye Clinic, P.A.
incidents.attacker: The Gentlemen claimed responsibility, but the claim was not independently verified; the confirmed unauthorized actor was not identified.
incidents.what: After a network disruption on August 18, third-party investigators determined that patient data had been exposed and may have been acquired. The potentially affected data of 6,137 people included names, phone numbers, Social Security numbers, and medical diagnoses or conditions.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: A healthcare provider confirmed exposure of potentially sensitive patient records following a cybersecurity incident, although acquisition of the data was not conclusively established.
incidents.significance: The investigation confirmed patient-data exposure affecting 6,137 individuals, including potentially Social Security numbers and medical information.

severity.reason: The clinic confirmed patient-data exposure and possible acquisition after a network disruption; prolonged care disruption and verified theft were not reported.

updates.what: After a network disruption on August 18, 2026, an investigation confirmed that patient data had been exposed and may have been acquired. Potentially affected information included names, phone numbers, Social Security numbers, and medical diagnoses or conditions.

incidents.title: Eye Care Center of Snohomish network access exposed patient files
incidents.victim: Anup K. Deol, OD PS, doing business as Eye Care Center of Snohomish
incidents.attacker: Unauthorized third party; attribution was not reported.
incidents.what: An unauthorized third party accessed limited network files on or around July 28, 2026. The affected records of 3,059 patients may have included names, addresses, birth dates, laboratory results, diagnoses, medications, and treatment information.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: A healthcare provider confirmed unauthorized access to files containing protected health information and reported the incident to law enforcement.
incidents.significance: The provider's investigation confirmed unauthorized access to limited files containing potentially detailed medical information for 3,059 patients.

severity.reason: The provider confirmed access to limited files containing protected health information; service disruption and confirmed copying or publication were not reported.

updates.what: An unauthorized third party accessed limited network files on or around July 28, 2026. The files could contain names, addresses, birth dates, and medical information such as lab results, diagnoses, medications, and treatment details.

incidents.title: AT&T breach exposed communication logs of 109 million customers
incidents.victim: AT&T and approximately 109 million current and former customers
incidents.attacker: Not reported; the source describes the breach as part of credential-based thefts involving Snowflake customers but does not establish attribution.
incidents.what: A breach exposed AT&T communication logs covering May–October 2022 and January 2023. The records included phone numbers, call and text counts, call durations, and location data, but reportedly did not include call content, customer names, or Social Security numbers.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: Call and location metadata can reveal relationships, movements, workplaces, homes, and daily routines at very large scale.
incidents.significance: AT&T reportedly lost sensitive communication metadata belonging to approximately 109 million people, including current and former customers. The exposed records covered a broad period and included location-related information.

severity.reason: The reported breach exposed communication and location metadata for approximately 109 million customers. The reporting does not establish service disruption or financial losses.

incidents.title: XCPE malware preinstalled on 1.3 million Android TV boxes
incidents.victim: More than 1.3 million Android TV streaming boxes, plus at least 10 million additional devices using related XCPE C2 infrastructure
incidents.attacker: Google attributes the botnet with high confidence to Videostrong Technology Co.; criminal affiliates used the infected devices and related malware families.
incidents.what: Videostrong allegedly embedded the XCPE backdoor in device firmware during manufacturing. The malware operated with Android system privileges, enabled remote commands, additional malware installation, screenshots, keystroke injection, account and device-data collection, ad fraud, and unauthorized residential-proxy use. Google and partners disrupted the C2 infrastructure, but the malware remained on infected devices and could reinstall from the OEM partition.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The incident represents a large-scale supply-chain compromise in which a device manufacturer allegedly distributed persistent malware across multiple consumer-device brands, enabling criminal affiliates to control devices and monetize them without users' consent.
incidents.significance: Google and industry partners identified and disrupted a botnet involving more than 1.3 million directly infected Android TV boxes and C2 infrastructure serving at least 10 million additional compromised devices. The backdoor had system-level privileges and supported data collection, remote control, malware deployment, ad fraud, and proxy abuse.

severity.reason: Google reported more than 1.3 million TV boxes with a manufacturer-installed backdoor and at least 10 million additional compromised devices connected to related C2 infrastructure. The malware provided system-level control and enabled data collection and further malware deployment; no service outage or quantified financial loss was reported.

updates.what: Malware was embedded in device firmware during manufacturing. It provided Android system-level control, enabled additional malware installation, shell commands, screenshots, keystroke injection, device and account-data collection, ad fraud, and use of devices as residential proxies. Google and partners disrupted the command-and-control infrastructure, but the malware remains on infected devices unless clean firmware is installed.

incidents.title: Vapor Panda used ARTEX AI against organizations in 14 countries
incidents.victim: At least nine organizations, including U.S. and Belgian telecommunications providers, government organizations in Greece, the Middle East and Latin America, and U.S. pharmaceutical firms
incidents.attacker: Vapor Panda, according to CrowdStrike; described as China-nexus, with attribution not independently established in the supplied report
incidents.what: Attackers used the ARTEX multi-agent AI penetration-testing framework, DeepSeek, and another commercial language model across simultaneous intrusions. The agents performed reconnaissance, vulnerability exploitation, web-shell deployment, credential theft, and alternate attack-path selection; in one Greek government intrusion they forged an administrator token and read mailboxes using authentication keys from a 2022 mail-server export.
incidents.ai_role: AI agents carried out reconnaissance, exploitation, credential access, web-shell deployment, and other unauthorized intrusion actions under human operator direction.
incidents.why: The operation compromised at least nine organizations and combined automated multi-target intrusion activity with human intervention, including access to government, telecommunications, pharmaceutical, defense, nuclear, semiconductor, and financial-sector targets.
incidents.where: Organizations across 14 countries; explicitly reported affected areas include the United States, Belgium, Greece, the Middle East, and Latin America
incidents.significance: CrowdStrike researchers reported at least nine confirmed organizational compromises, including mailbox access and forged administrator-token use in a Greek government intrusion. The campaign demonstrates operational use of AI agents across simultaneous real-world intrusions rather than a research demonstration.

severity.reason: Credible researcher reporting substantiates compromises of at least nine organizations and privileged or administrative access, including mailbox reading. Service disruption, data volume, and financial losses were not established in the available reporting.

updates.what: Vapor Panda used ARTEX AI together with DeepSeek and another commercial language model to coordinate simultaneous intrusions. The agents performed reconnaissance, vulnerability exploitation, web-shell deployment, credential theft, and alternative attack-path selection; one Greek government intrusion involved forged administrator tokens and mailbox access.

incidents.title: Hackers hijacked Ukraine’s Air Alert app with fake emergency warnings
incidents.victim: Ukraine’s Air Alert mobile app, operated by Ukrainian security technology company Ajax Systems with Ministry of Digital Transformation support
incidents.attacker: Unknown hackers; the previously unknown group Hitcore Corp claimed responsibility, but attribution was not independently confirmed.
incidents.what: Hackers gained unauthorized control of the Air Alert app’s notification function and sent Kyiv users fabricated warnings about radiation, chemical threats, street fighting and a possible Oreshnik missile strike. Developers disabled push notifications and temporarily suspended the service before beginning a gradual restoration.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The compromised app was a trusted emergency-alert channel with 6.6 million active users as of January 2026. False nuclear, chemical and attack warnings created a serious public-safety and information-integrity risk, although Ukraine’s broader emergency warning infrastructure remained operational.
incidents.significance: The app’s developers acknowledged unauthorized interference, and a reporter directly received apparently genuine false alerts. Push notifications and some map functionality were temporarily disabled, while authorities confirmed that the national warning system and Kyiv Digital app were unaffected.

severity.reason: Unauthorized actors controlled the app’s emergency-notification function, causing false alerts and temporary suspension of push notifications. The reporting does not establish disruption to Ukraine’s wider emergency-warning infrastructure or any physical harm.

updates.what: Unauthorized individuals interfered with the app and sent apparently genuine push notifications warning of radiation, chemical threats, street fighting and a possible nuclear-capable missile strike. Developers disabled push notifications and temporarily suspended the service before gradually restoring it.

incidents.title: Hackers compromised Russia’s EMERCOM mobile emergency app
incidents.victim: Russia’s Ministry of Emergency Situations (EMERCOM) mobile app
incidents.attacker: DC8044, a Kyiv-based group that claimed responsibility and said it used the app’s API; the claim and technical details were not independently verified, though Russia’s Emergency Situations Ministry acknowledged the app compromise.
incidents.what: Unauthorized actors used the compromised app to distribute false warnings that nuclear warheads had been launched toward Russia and advised residents to stockpile food and shelter in basements. Russia’s ministry said its supplementary app was hacked but that the primary public warning infrastructure was unaffected.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The incident abused a government emergency-information channel to spread fabricated nuclear-attack warnings. The ministry stated that sirens, loudspeakers, text messages, television and radio remained available, limiting the documented operational impact.
incidents.significance: The ministry publicly acknowledged that its mobile app had been hacked, while emphasizing that the national warning system was not affected. The report does not establish the number of users who received the false messages or any physical consequences.

severity.reason: The app was compromised and used to distribute false emergency messages, but Russia’s primary public-warning infrastructure continued operating. User reach and downstream harm were not established.

updates.what: The compromised app was used to distribute false warnings claiming nuclear warheads had been launched toward Russia and urging people to stockpile food and shelter in basements. EMERCOM said its primary public warning infrastructure was unaffected.

incidents.title: CyberDakait Android malware campaign compromised 17,960 devices
incidents.victim: At least 17,960 Android users in India, including customers of Indian banks
incidents.attacker: CyberDakait, a financially motivated threat cluster identified by Group-IB; attribution is based on the reporting and is not independently established here.
incidents.what: Since July 2025, seven Android trojan families were distributed through smishing and vishing, often via GitHub-hosted applications. The malware harvested banking credentials, payment information and SMS messages, while also enabling banking fraud and cryptojacking.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: Group-IB identified at least 17,960 compromised devices and approximately 7.6 million intercepted SMS messages, demonstrating a multi-victim campaign affecting banking credentials and communications.
incidents.significance: The campaign involved confirmed compromises of thousands of devices, interception of approximately 7.6 million SMS messages, and targeting of bank credentials and payment information.

severity.reason: Group-IB reported 17,960 compromised devices and 7.6 million intercepted SMS messages. The reporting describes banking fraud capability, but does not establish a final monetary loss or a specific bank-service outage.

incidents.title: Searchjacked extensions hijacked searches and captured user queries
incidents.victim: Users of 319 Chrome extensions with a reported combined 13.4 million installations
incidents.attacker: Operators of the Searchjacked extension campaign; attribution was not reported.
incidents.what: Socket found 319 Chrome extensions that redirected or hijacked user searches through tracking servers, captured search queries and collected referral payments. The extensions were promoted through deceptive advertisements and were hosted on the Chrome Web Store as unlisted add-ons.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The campaign affected a large installed user base and collected users' search activity through malicious extensions, creating downstream privacy and tracking consequences.
incidents.significance: The reported combined installation base was 13.4 million, and the extensions were observed capturing search queries rather than merely being vulnerable or advertised.

severity.reason: Socket observed search hijacking, tracking-server collection of queries and referral monetization. The report gives installation counts, not confirmed unique users or a quantified financial loss.

incidents.title: SysGoRAT campaign compromised government-linked Linux infrastructure
incidents.victim: Government entities and state-affiliated infrastructure; specific victims were not reported
incidents.attacker: CL-UNK-1211, an unattributed activity cluster tracked by Palo Alto Networks Unit 42
incidents.what: Unit 42 reported compromises involving PHP and shell web shells, credential-theft scripts, in-memory reverse shells, and the cross-platform SysGoRAT backdoor. The operators maintained persistent access, collected credentials, searched government mailboxes for social-media-related messages, and attempted to prepare email archives for exfiltration; one archive script failed because of syntax errors.
incidents.ai_role: Unit 42 said multiple malicious PHP and shell scripts were likely generated by AI or deployed by an automated AI agent, based partly on conversational reasoning notes embedded in the code.
incidents.why: The activity combined persistent unauthorized access, credential theft, and remote command capability against government-linked Linux infrastructure. The reporting substantiates compromise and attempted collection, but does not establish the number of victims or completed large-scale data exfiltration.
incidents.significance: Researchers observed persistent backdoors, credential harvesting, arbitrary command execution, file exfiltration capability, and attempts to disable protections and erase logs on government-associated systems. Attribution and final data loss remain unresolved.

severity.reason: Unit 42 reported actual access and persistence across government-related Linux infrastructure, including web shells and SysGoRAT. Credential theft and attempted mailbox exfiltration were observed, but completed data theft and operational disruption were not established.

updates.what: Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 observed intrusions using web shells, malicious PHP and shell scripts, credential theft, and the cross-platform SysGoRAT backdoor. The operators used scripts likely generated by AI or automated agents, and attempted reconnaissance, persistence, credential collection, database dumping, mailbox exfiltration, and social-media-account discovery.

incidents.title: DarkBlinders compromised Israeli target and Iraqi Kurdish government cloud
incidents.victim: A high-profile individual in Israel and a government cloud environment in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq
incidents.attacker: DarkBlinders, assessed as an Iran-aligned threat actor; attribution and links to related clusters remain assessed with medium confidence
incidents.what: The campaign used spear-phishing, credential-phishing lookalike domains, and trojanized utilities or coding challenges to deliver SHELBYLOADER V2 and the SHELBYC2 backdoor. Researchers reported that the activity resulted in the compromise of the Israeli target and the Kurdish government cloud environment.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The campaign achieved unauthorized access to a high-profile individual and a government cloud environment, demonstrating consequential espionage activity and potential access to government-held information. The available report does not establish the amount or type of data ultimately exfiltrated.
incidents.where: Israel and the Kurdistan Region of Iraq
incidents.significance: Dream Research Labs reported actual compromises, while the described malware provided persistence, remote control, and data-exfiltration capability. The victims included a government cloud environment and a high-profile individual.

severity.reason: Research reporting substantiates compromises of two separately described targets, including a government cloud environment. Access and persistence were reported, but specific stolen data, service disruption, and financial loss were not established.

updates.what: Researchers reported compromises involving an Israeli high-profile individual and a government cloud environment in the Kurdistan Region. The campaign used spear-phishing, credential-phishing sites, trojanized utilities and coding challenges, SHELBYLOADER/SHELBYC2 malware, DLL sideloading, and AppDomainManager injection.

incidents.title: Microsoft reports two Teams-based intrusions using AD CS abuse
incidents.victim: Two unnamed companies
incidents.attacker: Unattributed attackers; Microsoft did not link the activity to a known group.
incidents.what: Attackers impersonated IT support on Microsoft Teams, persuaded employees to provide Quick Assist access, and abused insecure Active Directory Certificate Services configurations to obtain certificates for privileged accounts, including a domain controller. In one intrusion, they accessed a domain controller, ran DCSync, reached a file server, and copied data to an external SFTP server; in the other, containment stopped further activity after a domain-controller certificate was obtained.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The intrusions achieved privileged identity access and resulted in confirmed organizational data copying, while demonstrating persistence that could survive password resets and workstation replacement.
incidents.significance: Microsoft documented two real organizational compromises involving domain-controller or highly privileged certificates. One incident included DCSync activity and confirmed data transfer to an external server, although the amount of credential and company data obtained was not reported.

severity.reason: Microsoft reported two separate company intrusions, privileged certificate issuance, domain-controller access, and data copied to an external SFTP server in one case. The quantity of copied data and any operational or financial loss were not reported.

updates.what: Attackers impersonated company IT or help-desk staff on Microsoft Teams, obtained remote access through Quick Assist, and abused misconfigured Active Directory Certificate Services. In one intrusion, they obtained certificates for privileged accounts, accessed a domain controller, initiated DCSync, and copied company data to an external SFTP server; in the other, they obtained a domain-controller certificate but were stopped after containment.

incidents.title: Ivanti Connect Secure zero-days enabled root access and credential theft
incidents.victim: A limited number of Ivanti Connect Secure customers, including one customer investigated by Volexity
incidents.attacker: UTA0576, according to Volexity; attribution and motive remain uncertain. Volexity assessed criminal motivation with low confidence and possible espionage motivation.
incidents.what: Attackers chained three zero-days in Ivanti Connect Secure appliances, including an authentication bypass and remote-code-execution flaw, to obtain unauthenticated root-level access on a fully patched appliance. They stole domain credentials, exfiltrated limited Active Directory metadata, searched for LAPS passwords and BitLocker recovery keys, conducted reconnaissance and password spraying, and tampered with logs.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The operation was detected and disrupted before the attackers’ ultimate goals were clear, but the observed access and credential theft indicated preparation for lateral movement and a wider network compromise.
incidents.significance: Volexity directly observed exploitation beginning October 3 at a customer and documented root-level appliance access, credential theft, data exfiltration, reconnaissance, and log tampering. Ivanti confirmed exploitation affecting a limited number of customers, while the full scope remains unknown.

severity.reason: Volexity documented unauthorized root access, credential theft, data exfiltration, network reconnaissance, and log tampering at a customer; the reporting does not establish service disruption or financial loss.

updates.what: Volexity observed in-the-wild exploitation of a three-vulnerability chain against a fully patched Ivanti Connect Secure appliance. The attacker achieved remote root-level code execution and was able to steal credentials and exfiltrate sensitive data.

Attackers chained an authentication-bypass flaw with remote code execution and privilege-escalation vulnerabilities to obtain unauthenticated root-level code execution on Ivanti Connect Secure appliances. Observed activity included credential and limited Active Directory metadata theft, host reconnaissance, and searches for administrator passwords and BitLocker recovery keys.

Attackers chained CVE-2026-104935, CVE-2026-111357, and CVE-2026-118527 to obtain unauthenticated code execution with root privileges on a fully patched Ivanti Connect Secure appliance. Volexity observed credential theft, data exfiltration, network scanning, and log tampering.

incidents.title: Trojanized Claude Code extension distributed through Cursor Marketplace
incidents.victim: Users who installed Claude Code extension version 2.1.313 through the Cursor Marketplace; at most 5,000 users
incidents.attacker: Unknown; the method used to introduce the unauthorized update remains unclear.
incidents.what: Attackers distributed a modified version of Anthropic's Claude Code extension under its legitimate publisher identity and extension ID. The update added an SSH key, attempted persistence through scheduled tasks, crontab, and LaunchAgent, created a reverse tunnel, and sent host reconnaissance data to attacker-controlled infrastructure.
incidents.ai_role: The compromised package was Anthropic's Claude Code extension, an AI coding tool; reporting does not establish that AI was used by the attacker.
incidents.why: The extension could provide persistent access to developer systems and expose information about usernames, hosts, Git configuration, and credential-related environment variables. Cursor shut down its marketplace, removed the malicious version, and Anthropic released version 2.1.314.
incidents.significance: A legitimate AI coding-extension update was compromised in a software-distribution marketplace and reached up to 5,000 users. Researchers observed persistence, reverse-tunnel functionality, and reconnaissance collection, although successful SSH access was constrained on many Windows and macOS systems by administrative requirements.

severity.reason: The malicious update was distributed to at most 5,000 users and was observed adding an attacker SSH key, installing persistence, and transmitting host details. The reporting does not establish confirmed follow-on commands, file theft, or operational outages.

updates.what: A trojanized Claude Code extension distributed for about 11 hours installed persistence, attempted to add an attacker-controlled SSH key and establish a reverse tunnel, and sent host reconnaissance including usernames, hostnames, public IPs, Git email addresses, and environment-variable names. Researchers found coding errors likely prevented remote SSH access on many Windows and macOS systems, although persistence and reconnaissance still functioned.

A tampered Claude Code extension distributed through Cursor's marketplace inserted an SSH key, attempted to enable SSH and establish a reverse tunnel, installed persistence, and sent host reconnaissance data. Cursor removed the versions, rebuilt the marketplace, rotated keys, and took the attack server offline; the incident affected at most 5,000 users.

A tampered copy of Anthropic’s Claude Code extension was published in the Cursor VS Code Extension Marketplace for about 11 hours. Its JavaScript attempted host reconnaissance, file and OS-command execution, SSH-key installation, reverse tunneling, and persistence on macOS and Windows systems. About 5,000 developer systems might have downloaded the versions, while Cursor removed them, suspended the marketplace, rotated keys, and rebuilt the marketplace.

incidents.title: NetamLoader infected a government Windows system in Asia
incidents.victim: An unnamed Asian government organization using a customized Windows 10 version
incidents.attacker: Unknown; Kaspersky could not link the operation to a known state-sponsored group
incidents.what: Kaspersky identified NetamLoader on one government computer in the first half of 2026. The malware was found in a package stored in a Windows-update directory and could evade security tools, collect host information, download additional code, communicate with attacker infrastructure, and delete files and logs. Researchers suspected a supply-chain route but could not confirm that update infrastructure was compromised.

severity.reason: CrowdStrike reported intrusions in multiple U.S. organizations and deployment of malware after access to VMware environments. The available reporting confirms administrative-level activity and suppressed audit logging but does not establish service disruption, data theft, or financial loss.

updates.what: CrowdStrike reported that Warp Panda exploited VMware ESXi vulnerability CVE-2026-41709 as a zero-day to reduce audit-trail visibility, pivot into VMware vCenter environments, deploy malware, harvest cloud-session tokens, and in at least one case register a rogue MFA device.

incidents.title: Cisco ASA and FTD VPN zero-day exploited in the wild
incidents.victim: Organizations operating affected Cisco Secure Firewall ASA or FTD software; specific victims were not reported
incidents.attacker: Unknown; Cisco confirmed exploitation in the wild but disclosed no threat actor details
incidents.what: Attackers remotely exploited CVE-2026-76418 in the Remote Access SSL VPN service without authenticating. A malicious connection request could force an affected firewall to restart, disrupting availability.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: This is a confirmed, actively exploited zero-day affecting network perimeter devices and remote-access infrastructure. The reporting does not establish the number of compromised devices or observed outages.
incidents.significance: Cisco confirmed real-world exploitation of an unauthenticated VPN flaw that can remotely restart firewalls. Specific victims, attack scale, and consequences were not disclosed.

severity.reason: Cisco confirmed exploitation in the wild, but the available reporting provides no victim-specific evidence, scale, or confirmed outage. The exploit path can cause device restarts, but actual disruption was not established.

updates.what: Attackers exploited CVE-2026-76418, an unauthenticated Cisco ASA and FTD flaw, to remotely force vulnerable SSL VPN firewall devices to reload and enter a denial-of-service condition. Cisco said its PSIRT observed active exploitation in October 2026.

Attackers remotely exploited CVE-2026-76418 in the SSL VPN service without authenticating or completing a successful VPN login. A successful exploit can force vulnerable firewalls to restart and disrupt availability.

Attackers exploited CVE-2026-76418 in the SSL remote-access VPN service of Cisco Secure Firewall ASA and FTD software. The unauthenticated flaw can cause affected firewalls to reload; a successful VPN login is not required.

incidents.title: KeyDrift malware compromised Cisco SD-WAN control systems
incidents.victim: An unnamed organization operating Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN control systems
incidents.attacker: UAT-11473, according to Cisco Talos; Talos found considerable infrastructure overlap with Silent Train but did not establish that they are the same group. Lumen separately linked Silent Train to Volt Typhoon, but did not tie that activity to KeyDrift.
incidents.what: Attackers exploited CVE-2026-20127 to bypass authentication and obtain administrative access to Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controllers, Managers, or Validators. They installed KeyDrift malware, including components that injected into the vdaemon process, could execute commands and relay traffic, and attempted to extract AES-256 key material used to encrypt traffic between sites. Talos described the exploitation as historical, with activity dating back to at least 2023; whether keys were transmitted or reused was not established.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The compromise affected systems that manage an organization's SD-WAN network and could expose encryption keys protecting inter-site traffic. The reporting confirms malware deployment and privileged access, but does not establish the number of affected organizations, successful key exfiltration, or downstream decryption.
incidents.significance: Cisco Talos observed custom malware implanted in SD-WAN control-plane systems after exploitation of a critical authentication-bypass flaw. The malware was capable of accessing decrypted control messages and extracting traffic-encryption key material, creating a consequential risk to network confidentiality and control.

severity.reason: Talos reported historical real-world compromises in which attackers gained administrative access and planted KeyDrift on Cisco SD-WAN control systems. Key extraction was the malware's purpose, but the reporting does not confirm that keys were successfully sent or used, nor does it document service disruption or financial loss.

updates.what: Attackers exploited CVE-2026-76504, an authentication bypass caused by improper URI-encoding handling, to reach a restricted API endpoint and potentially obtain administrative API access without authentication. Cisco and CISA provided remediation guidance and indicators of compromise, but did not disclose specific victims or exploitation outcomes.

Cisco Talos observed exploitation of the CVE-2026-20127 authentication-bypass flaw to gain privileged access to Cisco SD-WAN controllers, add rogue peers, and deploy the KeyDrift framework. Its components can execute commands, intercept decrypted control traffic, extract IPsec key material, and exfiltrate collected data.

Attackers exploited CVE-2026-20127 to gain administrative access to Cisco SD-WAN Controller, Manager, or Validator systems and install KeyDrift malware. The malware hooked SD-WAN processes to read decrypted inter-site traffic keys, store encrypted records, potentially transmit them over UDP, and provide command execution and relay functions.

incidents.title: PAN-OS zero-day exploited against Palo Alto firewalls
incidents.victim: Organizations operating Palo Alto Networks PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls or Panorama
incidents.attacker: Not reported; Palo Alto Networks observed limited exploitation but did not identify a threat actor.
incidents.what: CVE-2026-0322, a PAN-OS management-interface vulnerability, was exploited in malicious attacks. An authenticated attacker with network access could execute arbitrary code with root privileges; Palo Alto Networks released patches and indicators of compromise.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The incident involved observed exploitation of a zero-day affecting security management infrastructure. The number of compromised devices and resulting victim impact were not reported.
incidents.significance: Palo Alto Networks confirmed very limited exploitation targeting PAN-OS management interfaces, and CISA added the vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

severity.reason: Observed exploitation resulted in root access to 25 servers and credential extraction, but the reporting does not establish service outages, data theft beyond credentials, or financial losses.

updates.what: CVE-2026-0322, a PAN-OS management-interface vulnerability, was exploited in malicious attacks to execute arbitrary code with root privileges on affected firewalls. Palo Alto Networks released patches and indicators of compromise.

Palo Alto Networks reported active exploitation of CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 against internet-exposed management interfaces. Dream observed the vulnerabilities chained with the Fragnesia Linux privilege-escalation flaw to root 25 servers in the United States, Japan, Taiwan, and South Korea; recovered artifacts showed credential extraction, directory enumeration, and attacks against Active Directory.

incidents.title: Wiz observed agentic cloud intrusion with bulk secret theft
incidents.victim: Unnamed organization; specific victim was not reported
incidents.attacker: Not reported; Wiz investigated the intrusion and attributed the hands-on activity to an AI agent, but did not identify the operator.
incidents.what: Wiz reported a chained remote-code-execution intrusion that reached cloud credentials and Kubernetes tokens, achieved persistence, replicated across several pods, and exfiltrated bulk secrets. The operation showed machine-paced adaptive scripting and parallel lateral movement.
incidents.ai_role: An AI agent appears to have performed reconnaissance, exploitation, privilege escalation, cloud and Kubernetes credential theft, persistence, and secret exfiltration; the human operator and framework were not reported.
incidents.why: The incident demonstrates confirmed unauthorized access to production cloud and Kubernetes environments with theft of reusable credentials and secrets, although the victim and final scope were not disclosed.
incidents.significance: Wiz reported observed compromise, persistence across pods, and bulk secret exfiltration rather than merely attempted exploitation. The incident illustrates AI-agent involvement in consequential cloud intrusion activity.

severity.reason: Wiz described a real investigated intrusion involving RCE, cloud-credential and Kubernetes-token theft, persistence, and bulk secret exfiltration. Service disruption and financial loss were not reported.

updates.what: Wiz CIRT documented an AI agent exploiting an exposed Kafka UI for Java remote code execution, deploying malware and backdoors, harvesting credentials, escalating to cluster and cloud administration, creating an administrator identity, modifying GitOps and CI/CD systems, and accessing sensitive data. The agent also attempted to exfiltrate data through webhooks, source control, Kubernetes ConfigMaps, and cloud storage.

incidents.title: Hermes AI agent compromised Thailand ministry systems
incidents.victim: Thailand’s Ministry of Finance
incidents.attacker: Not reported; Hunt.io found attacker-controlled infrastructure running the Hermes AI agent.
incidents.what: Hunt.io found logs showing Hermes operating unattended in “YOLO” mode during an intrusion. The agent enumerated internal hosts, inspected files, and investigated privilege-escalation opportunities; multiple ministry systems were compromised, with web shells, stolen credentials, and a custom Go-based implant discovered.
incidents.ai_role: The Hermes AI agent performed unattended reconnaissance, file inspection, and privilege-escalation activity during the intrusion. The initial access method and human operator were not reported.
incidents.why: Multiple government systems were actually compromised and persistence artifacts and stolen credentials were found, even though investigators had not established data exfiltration.
incidents.significance: This is a confirmed government-system compromise in which independent researchers found evidence of an AI agent carrying out hands-on post-compromise activity and persistence.

severity.reason: Hunt.io reported compromise of multiple ministry systems, web shells, stolen credentials, and an implant. No data exfiltration or service disruption had been established at discovery.

incidents.title: BAE security incident disrupted US bankruptcy noticing services
incidents.victim: BAE Systems’ Bankruptcy Noticing Center (BNC), operated for the US federal bankruptcy courts
incidents.attacker: Not reported; BAE and the judiciary have not determined or disclosed whether the incident was a cyberattack.
incidents.what: A confirmed security incident affecting BAE infrastructure made the BNC systems and websites unavailable. The center stopped generating and sending bankruptcy notices, and the National Creditor Registration Service went offline, preventing electronic-filing users from generating creditor mailing lists.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The disruption affected bankruptcy-noticing operations across federal bankruptcy courts, while courts continued accepting filings and sending some electronic filing notifications through other channels. The cause, scope, and whether data was compromised remained undisclosed.
incidents.significance: The BNC handles notices for every US federal bankruptcy court, and notices issued through the center since October 9 were reportedly not delivered. Restoration had no estimated date at publication.

severity.reason: BAE and the Administrative Office of the US Courts confirmed a security incident and the resulting unavailability of BNC systems. The reporting did not establish data theft, destructive effects, financial losses, or the incident’s technical cause.

updates.what: A security incident affecting BAE infrastructure made BNC systems and websites unavailable. Federal bankruptcy courts could not generate or send notices or creditor mailing lists; electronic filing notifications and court filings continued.

The Bankruptcy Noticing Center stopped processing federal bankruptcy notices around October 9 and was restored on October 26, after which delayed notices were cleared. BAE said no data was extracted and no personally identifiable information was breached.

A cyberattack took the Bankruptcy Noticing Center offline, halting production and distribution of bankruptcy notices and taking related judiciary websites offline. Services began resuming with a backlog dating to October 7; BAE Systems said no data was extracted and no personally identifiable information was breached.

incidents.title: Japan Airlines provider breach exposed data of 92,000 customers
incidents.victim: Japan Airlines and Japan Transocean Air customers; reservation provider Amadeus IT Group
incidents.attacker: Unknown hackers; no attribution was reported.
incidents.what: Amadeus informed Japan Airlines that hackers accessed part of the reservation data for Japan Airlines and Japan Transocean Air flights. Exposed information included names, reservation codes, and flight information for 92,000 customers; for about 2,000 customers, passport numbers, frequent-flyer numbers, email addresses, and phone numbers were also accessed.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The incident compromised a trusted provider supporting airline reservation, ticketing, and check-in systems and exposed sensitive travel and identity information. Flight operations were not affected, and credit-card numbers were not compromised.
incidents.significance: Japan Airlines confirmed that its IT provider reported unauthorized access affecting 92,000 customers, including passport and contact data for approximately 2,000 people.

severity.reason: The provider breach exposed reservation and, for approximately 2,000 customers, passport, frequent-flyer, email, and phone information. Japan Airlines said flight operations and credit-card data were unaffected; financial loss was not reported.

updates.what: Japan Airlines said hackers accessed part of customer reservation data held by Amadeus IT Group. Data for 92,000 customers included names, reservation codes and flight information; about 2,000 customers also had passport numbers, frequent-flyer numbers, email addresses and phone numbers accessed.

Amadeus notified Japan Airlines that its Passenger Service System was accessed without authorization. Data exposed included reservation codes, names, flight dates, routes and travel classes for about 90,000 customers; about 2,000 additional customers also had contact, passport, nationality, frequent-flyer, flight, ticket and seat data exposed.

incidents.title: Malicious Hugging Face models hijacked GPU hosts
incidents.victim: Users of self-hosted inference servers and a shared research GPU cluster
incidents.attacker: Pluto Security attributed the campaign to a financially motivated Chinese-speaking operator; attribution is uncertain.
incidents.what: Researchers found 31 malicious Hugging Face repositories across seven accounts. Models abused trust_remote_code to execute Python code, install cryptocurrency miners, remove competing miners, and in some versions open reverse shells; nine machines in a shared research GPU cluster were observed mining for the operator.
incidents.ai_role: The compromised model repositories targeted AI model-loading and self-hosted inference environments; AI was the abused platform rather than the confirmed autonomous attacker.
incidents.why: The campaign compromised or attempted to compromise systems used for AI inference, with observed unauthorized mining and backdoor functionality. Repository downloads exceeded 32,000, but researchers stated that downloads do not establish infections.
incidents.significance: Researchers observed nine GPU-cluster machines mining for the operator and confirmed reverse-shell code in malicious models. The campaign also returned under new accounts after the initial repositories were removed.

severity.reason: Unauthorized mining was observed on nine machines, and the payload included reverse-shell functionality. The reported cryptocurrency proceeds were approximately $5,000, while broader victim losses and service disruption were not established.

updates.what: Pluto Security found 31 malicious Hugging Face repositories across seven accounts. Models abusing trust_remote_code ran code on GPU hosts, installed cryptocurrency miners, opened reverse shells, and in one later version attempted container escape and server takeover. Researchers observed nine machines in a shared GPU cluster mining for the operator.

incidents.title: China-linked hackers rooted firewalls and accessed management systems
incidents.victim: A US government-affiliated organization and other organizations operating the targeted firewalls; specific organizations were not reported
incidents.attacker: Unattributed China-linked or Chinese-nexus actor, according to Dream; specific threat actor not identified
incidents.what: Attackers exploited PHP2Shell and Fragnesia vulnerabilities against internet-facing firewalls. They installed root webshells on 24 devices, then used a reverse SSH tunnel to access an internal firewall-management server at a US government-affiliated organization, retrieve configurations and credentials, decrypt an LDAP service-account password, enumerate the domain, conduct password spraying, and attempt to create Active Directory backdoor accounts.
incidents.ai_role: Dream found Anthropic Claude Code, FOFA and aiscan-related API keys, and code characteristics suggesting AI-assisted tooling and development; the reporting does not establish that an AI agent autonomously carried out the intrusion.
incidents.why: The incident involved confirmed root-level access to firewalls and subsequent access to an internal management server containing enterprise firewall configurations and credentials. Dream observed no post-exploitation activity on 22 devices, while the US government-affiliated environment was subjected to deeper intrusion activity.
incidents.where: US government-affiliated environment; other affected firewall locations were not reported
incidents.significance: Observed exploitation progressed from internet-facing firewalls to an internal management server, exposing configurations and credentials for every firewall managed by the organization and enabling attempted domain compromise.

severity.reason: Dream observed root webshells on 24 firewalls and confirmed deeper access at a US government-affiliated environment, including access to firewall configurations, credentials, and LDAP service-account information. Operational disruption or data theft was not reported.

updates.what: The attacker exploited PHP2Shell vulnerabilities together with the Fragnesia Linux kernel privilege-escalation flaw to gain root access to 25 firewall servers in the United States, Japan, Taiwan, and South Korea. The operation installed web shells, used a reverse SSH tunnel to reach an internal government firewall, and attempted Active Directory credential extraction, enumeration, password spraying, and backdoor-account creation.

Dream researchers found 24 firewalls successfully compromised using PHP2Shell chained with CVE-2026-46300. Attackers planted webshells on most systems; two government-related servers received additional attention, with evidence of root access, credential extraction, directory enumeration, private-key access, and network-topology discovery.

incidents.title: Cyberattack disrupts Belgium’s MyMinfin tax portal
incidents.victim: Belgium’s Federal Public Service Finance (FPS Finance)
incidents.attacker: Unknown; Belgian authorities have not identified the attacker.
incidents.what: FPS Finance took the MyMinfin online tax and financial-services platform offline after a cyberattack and was investigating its scope. Several other government applications remained fully or partially operational.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The shutdown occurred days before an October 31 filing deadline, forcing authorities to extend the deadline for affected taxpayers. Authorities said there was no current indication of data theft, but the possibility of exposure remained under investigation.
incidents.significance: A cyberattack caused a national government tax portal to be taken offline during a filing period, disrupting public financial administration and requiring a deadline extension. Data theft had not been established in the available reporting.

severity.reason: FPS Finance suspended access to the main MyMinfin tax platform and extended the filing deadline for affected taxpayers. The authority reported no current indication of data theft, while investigation of scope and possible exposure continued.

updates.what: FPS Finance suspended access to MyMinfin after a cyberattack while investigators assessed the intrusion and secured systems. The agency said there was no current indication of data theft, but the possibility of exposure remained under examination.

incidents.title: FortiBleed campaign exposed more than 40,000 secrets
incidents.victim: Organizations using affected FortiGate devices; specific victims were not reported
incidents.attacker: Not reported; Hudson Rock documented the campaign data
incidents.what: Hudson Rock identified 975 additional domains and 40,573 exposed secrets, including local-user records and Active Directory LDAP bind records, in source files associated with 1,689 FortiGate host identifiers.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The exposed material included reusable authentication information that could enable unauthorized access to organizational networks and directories.
incidents.significance: Independent researcher evidence documents a large volume of organizational credentials and directory-binding records tied to FortiGate systems, although the final extent of successful reuse is not reported.

severity.reason: Hudson Rock reported 40,573 exposed secrets and associated organizational host identifiers. Operational disruption and financial loss were not established.

incidents.title: Attackers hijacked DNS for school and government domains
incidents.victim: Unnamed school and government domain owners, including an Indian government domain
incidents.attacker: Hidden Hawk was linked to one cluster; the second campaign's attribution was not reported
incidents.what: Infoblox reported unauthorized access to DNS administration in two operations. Attackers created CNAME records or delegated subzones so institutional hostnames served illegal-gambling doorway pages.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The attackers abused trusted institutional namespaces and DNS control to redirect or host content under legitimate school and government domains.
incidents.where: India; other affected countries were not reported
incidents.significance: The reporting describes actual unauthorized DNS administration access affecting institutional domains, with reputational and web-service integrity consequences even though data theft was not reported.

severity.reason: Unauthorized DNS control and domain changes were observed. No material outage, data theft, or quantified financial loss was reported.

incidents.title: China-linked hackers accessed a Suva regional organization
incidents.victim: An unnamed regional organization in Suva
incidents.attacker: Hackers linked to China; the U.S. Embassy in Fiji did not identify a specific threat actor
incidents.what: The U.S. Embassy in Fiji said the hackers maintained access to the organization's network for several days during July and August 2026.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The incident involved confirmed persistent unauthorized access to an organizational network, although accessed data and operational consequences were not disclosed.
incidents.significance: A government source disclosed a real network intrusion with maintained access; the absence of reported data or service impact limits the observed severity assessment.

severity.reason: The U.S. Embassy confirmed several days of network access, but did not report what systems or data were accessed or whether services were disrupted.

incidents.title: Camera-management software was used to breach enterprise networks
incidents.victim: Multiple unnamed enterprise organizations using the compromised camera-management software
incidents.attacker: Not reported; Huntress observed the incidents
incidents.what: Huntress observed multiple September and October incidents in which attackers entered enterprise networks through compromised camera-management software associated with a Korean camera and recorder vendor. Attackers abused WpcMon.exe to sideload DLLs and establish outbound connections.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: A trusted camera-management application served as the entry point into enterprise networks, creating a downstream software compromise with confirmed unauthorized access.
incidents.significance: The incidents demonstrate compromise of a trusted enterprise software component used for camera infrastructure and resulting network intrusions, although victims and downstream losses were not named.

severity.reason: Huntress observed multiple enterprise-network intrusions and outbound connections through the compromised application. Data theft and service disruption were not reported.

incidents.title: Philippine agency lost 68 GB of case-management data
incidents.victim: An unnamed Philippine government agency responsible for overseas employment and migrant-worker administration
incidents.attacker: Unknown threat actor; Hunt.io identified the exposed transfer log and toolkit
incidents.what: Hunt.io reported that an attacker copied 68 GB in under 24 minutes, including 27 SQL Server backups whose filenames corresponded to the agency's case-management systems. The attacker left the transfer log and tools exposed online.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The incident involved confirmed bulk exfiltration from government case-management systems, with the exact records and number of affected people not reported.
incidents.significance: Bulk theft of government case-management backups represents a substantial sensitive-data compromise, even though the agency and final scope were not named.

severity.reason: Hunt.io observed a 68 GB transfer and 27 case-management SQL backups. The contents, affected individuals, and operational disruption were not established.

incidents.title: Miasma-linked worm hijacked 42 GitHub repositories
incidents.victim: 42 GitHub repositories across 11 owners, plus developers who installed affected packages
incidents.attacker: Threat actors associated with the Miasma family; JFrog and SafeDep reported the activity
incidents.what: Attackers hijacked 42 third-party GitHub repositories and inserted large payload blobs and execution hooks for AI coding assistants and IDEs. Malicious packages stole credentials, propagated to other repositories, and installed a wiper that deleted home directories when stolen GitHub tokens were revoked.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The campaign compromised software-development repositories and developer credentials, enabling further malicious releases and destructive actions in downstream environments.
incidents.significance: The campaign compromised source repositories across multiple owners and used developer tooling and CI workflows to propagate, making it a material software-supply-chain incident.

severity.reason: JFrog and SafeDep reported repository compromise, credential theft, malicious releases, and a wiper capable of deleting victims' home directories. The number of downstream installations and actual deletions was not reported.

incidents.title: MR ROBOT banking trojan infected 153 Android devices
incidents.victim: Customers of Indian banks; at least 153 infected Android-device users
incidents.attacker: MR ROBOT crimeware platform operators and affiliates; attribution was not reported
incidents.what: CloudSEK described a rented Android banking-trojan service distributed through fake app pages and messaging lures. One affiliate reportedly intercepted 5,407 text messages from 153 infected devices and used the malware to target OTPs, card details, UPI PINs, credentials, and calls.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The campaign compromised real mobile devices and intercepted authentication messages and banking-related information, creating a credible risk of account and payment compromise.
incidents.significance: This was a multi-victim banking-malware operation with observed SMS interception across 153 devices; the report does not establish completed theft or quantify financial losses.

severity.reason: CloudSEK reported 153 infected devices and 5,407 intercepted text messages, alongside targeting of banking secrets. Completed fraudulent transfers and monetary losses were not reported.

incidents.title: DHS employee database leaked online
incidents.victim: U.S. Department of Homeland Security employees and contractors, including CBP, ICE, HSI, and CISA personnel
incidents.attacker: Threat actor using the handle Department of Peace claimed responsibility; attribution and the original access method are unverified. DHS is investigating, while Okta said it had no evidence its systems were compromised.
incidents.what: More than 41,000 records containing employee names, work contact details, job titles, office locations, and system/application access information were posted online. Distributed Denial of Secrets reportedly obtained a copy of the database, but the source and authenticity of all records remain under investigation.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The exposed access-mapping information could facilitate targeted phishing or follow-on intrusion against DHS personnel and sensitive operations. The reported dataset includes personnel involved in covert, undercover, rendition, and deportation programs, although the full scope and authenticity remain unresolved.
incidents.significance: SecurityWeek reported that more than 41,000 DHS-related records were publicly leaked, and an independent organization reportedly obtained a copy. The records reportedly include sensitive personnel and system-access information, creating meaningful follow-on security risk.

severity.reason: A database containing tens of thousands of DHS employee and contractor records was reportedly leaked online, including system-access information. DHS described it as a potential breach and said it was responding; operational disruption and the complete scope were not established.

incidents.title: Yoba campaign disguised crypto miners as fake AI desktop apps
incidents.victim: Users who downloaded the malicious fake ChatGPT or Claude desktop applications; specific victims were not reported
incidents.attacker: Unknown threat actors; attribution was not established. Check Point Research documented the campaign.
incidents.what: Attackers created fake GitHub projects and websites for purported ChatGPT and Claude applications. Malicious YobaDropper and YobaLoader DLLs were sideloaded alongside signed OpenAI or Anthropic executables, established persistence, retrieved a payload, and injected it into svchost.exe to run an XMRig cryptocurrency miner.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The campaign abused interest in AI tools and trusted signed executables and GitHub hosting to distribute malware, with anti-analysis measures intended to evade detection.
incidents.significance: Check Point observed a real malware distribution campaign using fake AI applications, signed-executable DLL sideloading, persistence, and execution of a cryptocurrency miner. The reporting does not establish the number or identities of infected users.

severity.reason: Researchers documented malware that executes an XMRig miner on compromised systems. Victim count, operational disruption, and financial losses were not reported.

updates.what: Attackers hosted fake ChatGPT and Claude desktop applications in GitHub repositories. The packages sideloaded malicious DLLs, established persistence, retrieved commands through DNS-over-HTTPS, and injected an XMRig cryptocurrency miner into svchost.exe.

incidents.title: Fake App Store crypto app drained Solana wallets
incidents.victim: 27 Solana wallet holders; one victim was confirmed compromised through the fake Padre Terminal app
incidents.attacker: Unidentified operator; blockchain investigator Iris attributed the wallet-draining activity to the malicious app, but the compromise method for the other wallets was not established.
incidents.what: A fake Padre Terminal cryptocurrency-trading app distributed through Apple's App Store drained cryptocurrency after users imported private keys. Iris traced approximately $23,000 in theft from 27 Solana wallets; the malicious app was subsequently removed from the App Store.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The incident demonstrates a real software-distribution compromise causing cryptocurrency theft, with at least one wallet compromise independently confirmed by a blockchain investigator. The precise compromise method for 26 other wallets and the operator's identity remain unresolved.
incidents.significance: A malicious app reached Apple's App Store and enabled theft from 27 cryptocurrency wallets, with approximately $23,000 traced to the operation. Reporting confirms the app was removed, but says the drainer remained active after removal and that four other suspicious apps had not been independently linked to theft.

severity.reason: Iris reported theft from 27 wallets totaling approximately $23,000, with one compromise confirmed through the fake app. The reporting does not establish service disruption or theft from the other suspicious App Store apps.

updates.what: A malicious Padre Terminal app formerly listed on Apple's App Store induced users to import private keys and drained cryptocurrency wallets. Iris confirmed the app's role in one compromise; the other 26 wallet compromises were not independently linked to the app.

incidents.title: UNM Health ransomware attack diverted ambulances
incidents.victim: University of New Mexico Health System, including UNM Hospital and the Health Sciences Center
incidents.attacker: Not confirmed. The ransomware group Byod claimed responsibility, but that claim is unverified.
incidents.what: UNM Health detected a cyberattack that blocked access to critical systems. It cancelled appointments and outpatient surgeries, limited new patients, temporarily diverted ambulances from 12:30 to 2:30 p.m., and later restored critical systems and normal ambulance operations. UNM said containment prevented the threat actor from reaching core systems and servers; the nature and scope of unauthorized access remain under investigation.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The incident disrupted care at UNM Hospital, New Mexico’s only level 1 trauma center, creating a documented patient-safety and essential-service impact. Patient-data involvement and the final extent of compromise were not established.
incidents.significance: UNM Health temporarily diverted ambulances, cancelled clinical activity, and limited patient intake during a system outage. The outage affected the university health sciences system, although UNM reported that core systems and servers were protected and restored by October 27.

severity.reason: UNM confirmed unauthorized cyber activity and a system outage that cancelled appointments and outpatient surgeries and diverted ambulances for two hours. The available reporting does not establish whether patient or other sensitive data was stolen; the attacker’s claimed exfiltration is unverified.

updates.what: UNM Health reported a cyberattack that caused system outages, temporarily limited new admissions, diverted ambulances, suspended outpatient surgeries and appointments, and canceled health-sciences classes. Critical systems and normal ambulance, clinic, and hospital operations were restored by October 27; UNM said the event affected some end-user devices but did not penetrate core systems or servers.

UNM confirmed a cyberattack affected the Health Sciences Center. For about two hours, ambulances were diverted to health systems in Albuquerque and Santa Fe; outpatient surgeries and appointments were suspended, and academic and research operations were temporarily closed.

incidents.title: ShinyHunters exploited Oracle PeopleSoft customers
incidents.victim: More than 100 Oracle PeopleSoft customers, including the University of Nottingham, NAIC, and Nissan
incidents.attacker: ShinyHunters, tracked by Google as UNC6240; attribution is based on Mandiant and Google Threat Intelligence Group reporting.
incidents.what: The group modified its exploit for CVE-2026-35273 to bypass web-application-firewall rules protecting the PeopleSoft Environment Management Hub. Mandiant and GTIG observed web-shell deployment, SideEye backdoors, Neo-reGeorg tunneling, MeshCentral, and commands executed with root or System privileges.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: PeopleSoft supports core finance, human-resources, payroll, and supply-chain functions. The campaign reached more than 100 customers and enabled privileged access to application data, configuration files, and database connection strings, with potential extortion based on the group’s established data-theft pattern.
incidents.where: Organizations in multiple countries; specifically reported victims include the University of Nottingham in the United Kingdom and NAIC in the United States. Nissan was also identified as a confirmed victim, but its affected location was not reported.
incidents.significance: Google and Mandiant reported observed compromise of dozens of systems, including persistent web shells and backdoors, and commands executed with root or System privileges. The campaign affected more than 100 PeopleSoft customers, although incident-specific data theft and operational losses were not established.

severity.reason: Researchers observed real compromises across more than 100 PeopleSoft customers, including persistence, backdoors, internal tunneling, and root/System-level command execution. The reporting does not establish campaign-wide service disruption, confirmed data exfiltration, or financial loss.

updates.what: Attackers modified an exploit for CVE-2026-35273 to bypass web-application-firewall rules protecting the PeopleSoft Environment Management Hub. Mandiant and GTIG observed web-shell deployment, SideEye backdoors, credential theft capabilities, tunneling, MeshCentral, and commands executed with root or System privileges.
