Attackers exploited a pre-patch PeopleSoft zero-day chain involving SSRF, trusted loopback access to the Environment Management Hub, and paths to remote code execution. Mandiant reported an initial campaign from May 27 to June 9, followed by a larger September wave; attackers used URL encoding to bypass some web-application-firewall rules and deployed web shells or other code-execution mechanisms.

incidents.title: GMO Onamae Desktop Cloud breach exposed customer data
incidents.victim: GMO Internet's Onamae Desktop Cloud and its customers
incidents.attacker: Unidentified threat actor; attribution was not reported. The attacker demanded ¥8 billion (about US$50 million), but GMO refused to pay.
incidents.what: GMO detected an intrusion into its Onamae Desktop Cloud on October 20. The company shut down servers and reduced service availability, warned that malware may have been planted on customer servers, and later confirmed that company and customer data had been stolen and published online. MT4/MT5 credentials and trading-account details may have been exposed; payment information was reportedly not exposed.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The compromise of a VPS provider created downstream risk for customer-hosted systems and exposed sensitive credentials and trading information. GMO also reported operational containment measures and confirmed publication of stolen data, although it said no ransomware was activated on customer machines and was still checking the authenticity of leaked material.
incidents.significance: A trusted Japanese VPS provider was breached, with consequences extending to customer servers and data. GMO shut down servers and reduced availability, while confirming that company and customer data had been published; the final scope and authenticity of all leaked information remained under review.

severity.reason: GMO confirmed a real intrusion, server shutdowns and reduced availability, and theft and online publication of company and customer data. The reporting says payment information was not exposed and that ransomware was not activated; final data scope and financial loss were not established.

updates.what: GMO detected an intrusion into Onamae Desktop Cloud on October 20. The company said data belonging to GMO and customers was published online; up to 26,739 customer servers may have had malware installed, while MT4/MT5 credentials and trading-account details may have been exposed. No ransomware activation on customer machines was reported.

GMO found malicious programs installed on some customer servers, confirmed unauthorized access and exfiltration of customer information, and shut down servers across all plans. Data stored on the servers, including credentials saved in MT4/MT5 trading software, may have been viewed. OANDA Japan confirmed unauthorized logins and trades on some customer accounts using credentials believed to have leaked from GMO servers.

incidents.title: PolyShell breached hundreds of Adobe Commerce stores
incidents.victim: Hundreds of e-commerce stores using Adobe Commerce or Magento
incidents.attacker: Unknown; Sansec observed the exploitation campaign
incidents.what: Attackers exploited CVE-2026-48356, also called PolyShell, to breach stores and inject a malicious loader through Magento CMS blocks. The loader could fetch and execute an attacker-controlled payload, but no next-stage malware was recovered.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The campaign involved confirmed compromise of hundreds of production e-commerce stores and insertion of executable attacker-controlled code.
incidents.significance: Hundreds of stores were reportedly breached, demonstrating broad compromise of business-critical e-commerce infrastructure. The exact attacker objective and downstream payload remain unknown.

severity.reason: Sansec reported that attackers breached hundreds of stores and injected a malicious loader into Magento CMS blocks. The available reporting does not establish service outages, financial losses, or the contents of a follow-on payload.

updates.what: Attackers injected malicious JavaScript loaders into Magento CMS blocks, using multiple domains and scanner-evasion techniques. Sansec observed compromises through PolyShell and SessionReaper vulnerabilities, as well as a rogue administrator account at one patched store; the final payload was not established.

incidents.title: Metabase exploits exposed Blueberry Pediatrics patient data
incidents.victim: Blueberry Pediatrics and its patients
incidents.attacker: Two different unidentified threat actors; attribution not reported
incidents.what: Attackers exploited a critical Metabase vulnerability through Blueberry Pediatrics and its prescription-service provider Photon, obtaining copies of patient data. The exposed information included names, dates of birth, health-plan details, medical records, service dates, medical codes, charges, contact details, member IDs, and medication information; financial information, Social Security numbers, photos, and videos were not involved.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The incident affected 340,915 individuals and involved theft of sensitive medical and insurance information from a telemedicine provider and a healthcare supplier.
incidents.where: United States; affected residents in Oregon and Texas were reported
incidents.significance: Blueberry Pediatrics confirmed that patient data was obtained after Metabase exploitation, and the Oregon and Texas attorneys general were notified of affected residents. The scale and medical sensitivity make this a substantial healthcare data breach, although the final overlap between the two related exposures is not fully established.

severity.reason: Blueberry Pediatrics reported theft of data affecting 340,915 individuals, including medical records, health-plan information, and medication data. The available reporting does not establish service disruption or financial losses.

updates.what: Attackers exploited a critical Metabase vulnerability used by Blueberry and Photon and obtained copies of patient data. Exposed information included names, dates of birth, health-plan details, medical records, service dates, medical codes, charges, contact details, member IDs, and medication information; financial information, Social Security numbers, photos, and videos were not involved.

incidents.title: Moldova government systems breached, exposing data and disrupting services
incidents.victim: Moldovan government services, information systems and administrative panels
incidents.attacker: Unknown; Moldovan authorities are investigating possible foreign state involvement but have made no attribution.
incidents.what: Attackers exploited vulnerabilities in unauthenticated government services, made approximately 11 million data-access requests, and extracted information associated with about 750,000 identification numbers. The access path also enabled retrieval of additional data from interconnected government systems.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: Potentially exposed information included identity, health-insurance, benefits, pension, disability, driver's-license, vehicle-ownership and possible financial records. Authorities temporarily disconnected vulnerable services and more than 30 government information systems, disrupting online applications and registrations for construction, veterinary transport, medicine imports and food safety.
incidents.significance: Moldovan authorities disclosed extraction of data linked to approximately 750,000 identification numbers and confirmed disruption of dozens of public services. Bank-card information was reportedly not compromised, and authorities found no evidence that official records were altered.

severity.reason: The government temporarily disconnected more than 30 information systems and vulnerable public services, while preliminary findings indicated extraction of personal and potentially financial information linked to about 750,000 identification numbers. Final scope and individual-level exposure remain under investigation.

updates.what: Attackers exploited vulnerabilities in unauthenticated government services and interconnected systems, making approximately 11 million data-access requests. Preliminary findings indicate information linked to about 750,000 identification numbers was extracted, potentially including personal, health, benefits, pension, identity-document, vehicle and financial information; bank-card data was not compromised.

incidents.title: UNM Health cyber incident diverted ambulances and closed clinics
incidents.victim: University of New Mexico Health System, including UNM Hospital, UNM Health Sciences Center, and more than 30 clinics
incidents.attacker: Not reported; the incident was under active law-enforcement investigation.
incidents.what: A cybersecurity incident forced UNM Health to divert ambulances, cancel appointments, close or restrict access to clinics, and temporarily leave New Mexico without a Level 1 trauma center capable of treating the most serious injuries. Hospitals and clinics began resuming operations in phases later that day. Employees also saw messages claiming that student, employee, and patient data had been stolen, but the reporting did not establish that claim.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The incident disrupted hospital operations and emergency-care access at the state’s only Level 1 trauma center, prompting other major healthcare providers to take additional patients.
incidents.where: Albuquerque and Rio Rancho, New Mexico, United States
incidents.significance: UNM Health conducted about 100,000 emergency-room visits annually and operated New Mexico’s only Level 1 trauma center. Ambulance diversion, canceled appointments, clinic closures, and coordination with other hospitals demonstrate consequential healthcare-service disruption; the incident’s mechanism and any data theft remained unresolved.

severity.reason: UNM Health diverted ambulances, canceled appointments, restricted hospital and clinic access, and temporarily disrupted the state’s only Level 1 trauma center. Alleged data theft appeared in on-screen messages but was not independently confirmed in the available reporting.

locations.label: Rio Rancho, New Mexico, United States

updates.what: UNM reported a cybersecurity event affecting end-user devices and causing system outages. Ambulance traffic was diverted from 12:30 to 2:30 p.m., while outpatient surgeries and appointments were suspended for the remainder of the day; systems and clinical operations were later restored.

A cybersecurity incident disrupted UNM Health operations. Ambulances were diverted, appointments at more than 30 clinics were canceled, the main hospital advised patients not to arrive, and the Health Sciences Center canceled classes. Employees also saw messages claiming theft of student, employee, and patient data, but the claims were not independently confirmed in the report.

UNM Health detected a cyberattack that blocked access to critical electronic systems. Ambulances were diverted for about two hours, appointments and outpatient surgeries were canceled, new-patient intake was limited, and some classes were canceled. UNM said core systems and servers were protected; the extent of any patient-data involvement remains under investigation.

incidents.title: GhostAction workflow spread to 772 GitHub repositories
incidents.victim: 373 GitHub users and organizations whose 772 public repositories received the malicious workflow
incidents.attacker: Not identified in the available reporting; GitGuardian attributed the findings to the GhostAction supply-chain campaign.
incidents.what: The campaign pushed a secret-stealing GitHub Actions workflow to 772 public repositories and targeted 2,577 secrets, including SSH keys and Azure, AWS, and database credentials. GitGuardian reported that the campaign continued using its 2025 playbook.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The campaign compromised production repository and CI/CD infrastructure and targeted reusable credentials, creating confirmed exposure across hundreds of repositories and organizations.
incidents.significance: GitGuardian documented malicious workflow placement in 772 repositories belonging to 373 users and organizations, with 2,577 secrets targeted. The observed compromise of GitHub Actions workflows and credential theft creates potential access to downstream development and cloud environments, although downstream misuse was not reported.

severity.reason: GitGuardian reported that the workflow was pushed to 772 public repositories and targeted SSH keys and cloud/database credentials. The available reporting does not establish service outages, financial loss, or confirmed downstream intrusions.

updates.what: The GhostAction supply-chain campaign spread a malicious workflow to 772 public GitHub repositories across 373 users and organizations. Reporting says the campaign shifted toward developer endpoints and cloud access, while attackers remained active on GitHub.

incidents.title: LiteLLM compromised in supply-chain attack
incidents.victim: LiteLLM and packages published to PyPI and Docker
incidents.attacker: Hackers; no attribution reported.
incidents.what: Attackers used compromised GitHub CLI OAuth tokens to push and approve malicious packages on PyPI and Docker.
incidents.ai_role: The targeted LiteLLM software package was compromised as part of the AI software supply chain.
incidents.why: Not reported

locations.label: San Francisco, California, United States
locations.basis: Vendor headquarters (approximate; not an attack-site claim)

severity.reason: The malicious LiteLLM releases were published and executed on affected installations, with reporting of broad sensitive-information compromise involving credentials, keys, tokens, and runtime data. CloudSEK cautioned that the 2,500-organization and 434,000-pipeline figures represent reconstructed exposure, not confirmed compromise of every listed organization.

updates.what: A malicious LiteLLM version, 1.107.0, was uploaded to PyPI and Docker. It contained a credential stealer targeting browser, cloud, and AI secrets, plus dormant command-and-control capability.

The attacker published malicious LiteLLM 1.107.0 PyPI wheels and corresponding GHCR and Docker Hub images. The packages installed persistence files that executed at interpreter startup and collected cloud, Kubernetes, SSH, GPG, registry, AI-provider, coding-tool, browser, and shell-history credentials; the data was encrypted and sent to a lookalike domain. PyPI quarantined the release and the container tags were pulled the same day.
Wiz reported that LiteLLM version 1.107.0 was uploaded to PyPI and Docker with a credential stealer targeting browser, cloud, and AI secrets, plus dormant command-and-control capability.

Wiz Research reported that malicious LiteLLM version 1.107.0 was uploaded to PyPI and Docker. The package contained a credential stealer targeting browser, cloud, and AI secrets, plus dormant command-and-control capability.

Attackers used stolen GitHub CLI credentials to disable protections, alter the release workflow, and publish LiteLLM 1.107.0 and matching Docker/GHCR tags. The artifacts contained a credential stealer and a backdoor that collected system, browser, developer, cloud, and AI-tool secrets and could execute remotely.

Attackers used compromised developer credentials to disable branch protections, redirect the release workflow, and publish malicious LiteLLM version 1.107.0 artifacts to PyPI and Docker. The malware included an information stealer and RAT; Wiz observed stolen AWS credentials being used to query Amazon Bedrock.

An exposed, unrevoked LiteLLM Agent Platform master key was used to access the platform, extract an organization-owner GitHub OAuth token, harvest additional credentials, alter the release pipeline, and publish malicious LiteLLM 1.107.0 packages and container images. The compromised release contained credential-stealing code and a backdoor that could execute when Python started.

Attackers used a master key exposed in a public repository to obtain an organization-owner GitHub token, steal additional maintainer tokens, subvert LiteLLM’s release workflow, and publish credential-stealing artifacts.

incidents.title: Hackers compromised Dahua surveillance cameras in Ukraine
incidents.victim: Dahua camera and video-recorder operators in Ukraine; specific organizations were not reported
incidents.attacker: Unknown; CERT-UA reported the compromises, but did not identify the responsible actors
incidents.what: CERT-UA identified cases in which hackers gained unauthorized access to internet-connected Dahua cameras and video recorders, changed device settings, and created unauthorized user accounts. The attackers appear to have abused the Easy4IP remote-access feature, weak or default passwords, or outdated-firmware vulnerabilities including CVE-2021-33044 and CVE-2021-33045.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: Compromised surveillance devices could expose video feeds and permit remote control. The risk is particularly significant because Dahua equipment is used by Ukrainian government institutions and military units, although the affected devices were not tied to those organizations in the available reporting.
incidents.significance: CERT-UA confirmed actual unauthorized access, configuration changes, and creation of persistent unauthorized accounts on surveillance infrastructure. The reporting does not establish how many devices were compromised or whether government or military cameras were affected.

severity.reason: Unauthorized access to camera video streams and device configuration was observed, including creation of third-party accounts and persistent backdoors. Operational disruption and financial losses were not reported.

updates.what: CERT-UA reported unauthorized access to internet-connected Dahua cameras and video recorders. Attackers changed device settings and created unauthorized user accounts, apparently abusing the Easy4IP cloud-access feature, weak or default passwords, and outdated firmware vulnerabilities including CVE-2021-33044 and CVE-2021-33045.

CERT-UA reported unauthorized access to Dahua surveillance systems through the Easy4IP P2P platform, weak or known passwords, and authentication-bypass flaws in outdated firmware. Attackers accessed video streams, changed configurations, and created third-party accounts. The report also describes the separately documented Operation CameraSwarm campaign, which compromised more than 14,530 Dahua cameras between June 17 and July 22, 2026, including 1,923 with persistent backdoor accounts.

Apple said CVE-2026-86950, an out-of-bounds-write flaw in CoreGraphics capable of arbitrary code execution, may have been exploited in real-world attacks against devices running iOS versions before iOS 27. Apple backported fixes to older supported iPhones and iPads.

incidents.title: NorthShore Health Centers patient files accessed in cyber incident
incidents.victim: NorthShore Health Centers
incidents.attacker: An unnamed unauthorized third party accessed NorthShore's IT environment. The Insomnia ransomware group claimed responsibility and later alleged it leaked stolen data, but that attribution is not independently verified in the report.
incidents.what: NorthShore detected suspicious network activity and confirmed unauthorized access to parts of its IT environment. Files potentially containing patient personal and protected health information may have been viewed or obtained; the investigation and data review remain ongoing.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The incident involved confirmed unauthorized access to a healthcare provider's systems and potentially sensitive medical, insurance, and identity information. The number of affected individuals and the exact data involved have not yet been established.
incidents.where: Northwest Indiana, United States, including Porter, Lake, La Porte, and Jasper Counties
incidents.significance: NorthShore confirmed access to its IT environment and possible exposure of patient records, including likely medical and insurance information. The event matters despite the unresolved scope because it affected a healthcare provider's sensitive data systems.

severity.reason: NorthShore confirmed unauthorized access to parts of its IT environment and potential viewing or acquisition of patient files. The investigation had not established the final scope or whether all suspected data was obtained; the ransomware group’s leak claim is not independently verified.

locations.label: La Porte County, Indiana, United States

updates.what: NorthShore detected suspicious network activity and determined that an unauthorized party accessed parts of its IT environment and potentially viewed or obtained files containing patient information. The provider’s investigation and data review remained ongoing; Insomnia separately claimed the attack and reportedly leaked data.

incidents.title: ENGIE partner marketing platform breach exposed French customer data
incidents.victim: ENGIE customers in France; partner marketing platform
incidents.attacker: Unknown; ENGIE did not attribute the incident to a specific threat group.
incidents.what: Attackers breached a marketing platform used by ENGIE business partners and stole customer data. The exposed information included names, addresses, email addresses, phone numbers, energy delivery or metering-point identifiers, customer IDs, and contract numbers.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: ENGIE said the incident was limited to customers in France, notified authorities and affected customers, and cut off attacker access. The company stated that its internal IT systems and banking data were not compromised.
incidents.significance: This was a confirmed theft of energy customers’ contact, account-identifying, and contract information from a trusted partner platform. The number of affected customers was not disclosed, and the incident did not compromise ENGIE’s internal systems.

severity.reason: ENGIE confirmed unauthorized access and theft of customer contact and energy-contract information, but reported no internal-system compromise or banking-data exposure. The number of affected customers and any financial loss were not established.

incidents.title: Apple CoreGraphics zero-day exploited in targeted iOS attacks
incidents.victim: Specific targeted individuals using vulnerable Apple devices; identities were not reported
incidents.attacker: Not reported; Apple described the attacks as extremely sophisticated and targeted
incidents.what: Apple confirmed that CVE-2026-86950, an out-of-bounds write in CoreGraphics, was exploited against versions of iOS before iOS 27. Processing a maliciously crafted file could enable arbitrary code execution. Apple backported patches to additional older iPhones and iPads.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: This is a confirmed exploitation of a zero-day against real devices, with potential code-execution consequences, although the attackers, victims, and resulting actions were not identified.
incidents.significance: Apple confirmed exploitation in highly targeted attacks, and the flaw could provide arbitrary code execution through a maliciously crafted file. The available report does not establish data theft, persistence, or broader operational impact.

severity.reason: ENGIE confirmed theft of customer contact and contract-related information through a partner marketing platform. The company stated that internal IT systems and banking data were not compromised, and no service disruption or financial loss was reported.

updates.what: Attackers breached a marketing platform used by ENGIE business partners and accessed customer contact and energy-contract data. ENGIE said its internal IT systems were not compromised and it cut off access to the platform.

Attackers exploited CVE-2026-86950, an out-of-bounds write in Apple’s CoreGraphics framework, through maliciously crafted files. Apple confirmed exploitation and released patches for affected iPhones and iPads.

Apple said CVE-2026-86950, an out-of-bounds write in CoreGraphics capable of arbitrary code execution when processing a malicious file, was exploited in real-world attacks against specific individuals using older iOS versions.

incidents.title: Lazarus FlashHole campaign breached South Korean organizations
incidents.victim: At least three South Korean organizations in the construction, software, and wire-communication equipment manufacturing sectors
incidents.attacker: North Korea-linked Lazarus Group, attributed by Kaspersky; attribution remains an assessment
incidents.what: Attackers used spear-phishing and malicious websites to abuse vulnerable South Korean financial-security software, deploy TechHub, TouchHub, ClientHub, LPEClient, and Cubridge malware, establish persistence, execute commands, and steal files and browser data. Kaspersky reported that at least one infection resulted in data exfiltration to the ULOSE dark-web leak site.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The campaign demonstrates a confirmed compromise of multiple South Korean organizations through trusted, widely used security software and included observed data exfiltration. The malware also used ML-KEM-1024 post-quantum encryption for command-and-control communications.
incidents.significance: Kaspersky documented intrusions affecting at least three organizations and described malware capable of command execution, persistence, and file and browser-data theft; at least one infection led to reported data exfiltration.

severity.reason: Kaspersky reported compromises at at least three South Korean organizations and data exfiltration in at least one case. Service disruption, financial losses, and the precise scope or sensitivity of stolen data were not established.

updates.what: Operation FlashHole used spear-phishing and malicious websites to abuse Initech INISAFE CrossWeb EX and deploy a multi-stage malware framework including TechHub, TouchHub, ClientHub, LPEClient, and Cubridge. The malware could execute commands and steal files and browser data; at least one infection reportedly resulted in data exfiltration to the ULOSE dark-web leak site.

incidents.title: Keystone website breach exposed wallet-verification key and customer data
incidents.victim: Keystone
incidents.attacker: Unknown; an attacker exploited a vulnerability in a third-party data-monitoring tool used by Keystone's website.
incidents.what: The attacker escalated privileges on Keystone's website, obtained the hardware-wallet device-verification key, and accessed customer records. Keystone said 25,964 buyer records and 12,873 unpaid checkout records were affected; payment-card, bank, and government-ID data and recovery phrases/private keys were not involved.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: Possession of the verification key could allow counterfeit Keystone devices to pass the online authenticity check, although Keystone reported no counterfeit devices or resulting cryptocurrency theft. The company blocked access, replaced the key, paused shipping, and plans to destroy 18,835 unsold devices containing the old key.
incidents.significance: Keystone confirmed unauthorized privileged access, theft of a device-authentication secret, and access to tens of thousands of customer records. The compromised key created a downstream hardware-supply risk even though no counterfeit devices or crypto theft had been reported.

severity.reason: Keystone confirmed website compromise, access to customer shipping and order records, and theft of the wallet-verification key. Shipping was paused and 18,835 unsold devices are being destroyed; no cryptocurrency theft or counterfeit-device sales were reported.

updates.what: An attacker exploited a vulnerability in a third-party monitoring tool used by Keystone's website to escalate privileges and obtain the hardware-wallet authenticity-verification key and customer records. Keystone said 25,964 buyer records and 12,873 unpaid checkout records were affected; recovery phrases, private keys, payment-card details, bank details, and government IDs were not involved.

incidents.title: ASD disrupted Amadey controller serving 180,000 infected computers
incidents.victim: Users and organizations operating approximately 180,000 computers infected with Amadey worldwide, including some in Australia
incidents.attacker: Criminal Amadey operator; specific actor not identified. ASD said it accessed the operator's backend.
incidents.what: Australian Signals Directorate operators gained access to an Amadey command-and-control backend and disconnected it from approximately 180,000 infected computers. Amadey could install additional malware, steal credentials, and provide remote access.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The operation affected a large multi-victim malware population and involved demonstrated unauthorized access to infected systems, although the reporting does not establish how much data was previously stolen or which individual victims were affected.
incidents.where: Worldwide; some affected computers were in Australia
incidents.significance: ASD and ABC reporting describe a confirmed Amadey infection set of about 180,000 computers and a successful disruption of the criminal controller. Earlier theft was not reversed, and stolen credentials or session cookies may remain usable.

severity.reason: ASD disconnected the controller from approximately 180,000 infected computers, ending that controller's access, but the available reporting does not quantify prior theft, operational outages, or financial losses.

updates.what: The Australian Signals Directorate gained access to an Amadey command-and-control backend and disconnected it from approximately 180,000 infected computers. Amadey could install additional malware, steal credentials, and provide remote access.

incidents.title: ASD destroyed 5 TB of stolen business and personal data
incidents.victim: An unnamed business and individuals in Australia and other countries whose data was stolen
incidents.attacker: Unidentified attackers; ASD said it received a tip about the stolen data and intervened. Attribution was not reported.
incidents.what: ASD accessed and destroyed approximately 5 terabytes of data stolen from a business and offered for sale. The files included business documents, personal data, login credentials, and passwords; approximately 4.8 million files related to Australians, with hundreds of thousands from victims in other countries.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The case documents confirmed theft of a large volume of sensitive organizational and personal data, although the original intrusion method, affected business, and whether attackers retained other copies were not reported.
incidents.significance: ASD's intervention identified and destroyed an estimated 5 TB of stolen data, including reusable credentials and passwords affecting millions of files. The unnamed victim organization and original compromise remain unspecified.

severity.reason: ASD reported approximately 5 TB of stolen business and personal data, including credentials and passwords, with an estimated 4.8 million files concerning Australians. Operational disruption and financial loss were not reported.

updates.what: After receiving a tip that approximately 5 terabytes of stolen data were being offered for sale, ASD accessed and destroyed the files. The data included business documents, personal data, and login credentials and passwords.

incidents.title: Kenaitze Indian Tribe network breach exposed health and identity data
incidents.victim: Kenaitze Indian Tribe
incidents.attacker: Unauthorized third party; attribution not reported
incidents.what: An unauthorized party accessed the tribe’s network. Files may have been accessed or acquired, including names, dates of birth, Social Security numbers, driver’s-license or state-ID numbers, financial-account numbers, health-insurance information, and medical information.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The incident involved confirmed unauthorized network access and potentially exposed sensitive health, financial, and identity records affecting 9,319 individuals.
incidents.significance: The tribe confirmed unauthorized access to its network and identified sensitive medical, financial, and identity information in affected files; the reporting does not establish that every listed record was acquired.

severity.reason: The investigation confirmed network access and exposure of sensitive records. Service disruption and direct financial losses were not reported.

updates.what: An unauthorized third party accessed the tribe’s network, and files on compromised network segments may have been accessed or acquired. The confirmed exposed data included names, dates of birth, Social Security numbers, identity documents, financial-account, insurance, and medical information for 9,319 individuals.

incidents.title: Wichita Family Dental email account breach exposed patient records
incidents.victim: Wichita Family Dental
incidents.attacker: Unauthorized party; attribution not reported
incidents.what: An unauthorized party accessed an employee email account. The account contained personal and protected health information for 1,273 individuals, including Social Security numbers, payment-card and financial-account information, health-insurance information, and dental records.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: A compromised organizational email account exposed sensitive medical, financial, and identity information.
incidents.where: Wichita and Derby, Kansas, United States
incidents.significance: The dental practice confirmed unauthorized access to an employee account containing reusable identity and financial information as well as dental records.

severity.reason: Unauthorized email access and the presence of sensitive patient records were confirmed. No service interruption or financial loss was reported.

updates.what: An unauthorized party accessed an employee’s email account. The account contained personal and protected health information for 1,273 individuals, including identity, payment, financial, insurance, and dental-record data.

incidents.title: UNM Health cybersecurity event disrupted patient care
incidents.victim: University of New Mexico Health Sciences Center, including UNM Health
incidents.attacker: Not reported; the incident remains under an active law-enforcement investigation.
incidents.what: UNM Health reported a cybersecurity event affecting the Health Sciences Center. The organization contained the event, temporarily limited acceptance of new patients, diverted ambulance traffic, canceled outpatient surgeries and appointments, and brought systems back online in phases.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The event caused a documented interruption to hospital and clinical operations and required coordination with other health systems to receive patients.
incidents.significance: UNM Health temporarily diverted all ambulance traffic and suspended outpatient surgeries and appointments, demonstrating a consequential cybersecurity disruption to healthcare delivery. The organization activated an emergency operations center and involved law enforcement and external incident-response partners.

severity.reason: UNM Health confirmed that the cybersecurity event disrupted clinical operations: ambulance traffic was diverted from 12:30 to 2:30 p.m., while outpatient surgeries and appointments were suspended for the remainder of the day. Data theft, system compromise details, and financial losses were not established in the available reporting.

updates.what: UNM identified a cybersecurity threat affecting some end-user devices and took containment measures. System outages temporarily diverted ambulance traffic, suspended outpatient surgeries and appointments, canceled classes, and sent nonessential personnel home; UNM said core systems and servers were not penetrated.

UNM Health suffered a cyberattack that caused system outages, temporarily limited new admissions, diverted ambulances, and suspended outpatient surgeries and appointments. UNM later said critical electronic systems were restored and that the incident affected some end-user devices but did not penetrate core systems or servers.

A cyberattack caused significant IT issues across the University of New Mexico Health Sciences Center. UNM contained the incident, disconnected devices, notified federal law enforcement, and began restoring systems; the attack mechanism and whether ransomware was involved remain unconfirmed.

incidents.title: Warp breach exposed AI-agent logs and telemetry
incidents.victim: Warp and users of its agentic development environment
incidents.attacker: Not identified; reporting says the attack exploited a third-party vendor in Warp’s infrastructure and may have used an agent swarm.
incidents.what: Warp disclosed an active, narrowly targeted exploitation of a third-party vendor in its infrastructure. Agent traces and telemetry belonging to Warp users were potentially exposed; the company said roughly 1% of users may have been affected, while the investigation continues.
incidents.ai_role: The compromised service is an AI-agent development environment. Reporting does not confirm that attackers used AI to conduct the intrusion.
incidents.why: The breach affected infrastructure supporting an agentic coding platform and may have exposed operational logs and telemetry for a portion of its user base. Warp has not established whether source code, prompts, credentials, or other sensitive data were included.
incidents.significance: Warp confirmed exploitation of a third-party vendor within its infrastructure and notified potentially affected users. The platform reportedly has at least 800,000 users, although the affected population and data scope remain under investigation.

severity.reason: Warp detected and mitigated the operation within hours, with no reported service outage. Agent traces and telemetry were potentially exposed, but the reporting does not establish theft of source code, prompts, credentials, or other sensitive data.

updates.what: Warp said an attack on a third-party vendor in its infrastructure exposed potentially affected agent traces and telemetry belonging to users. The company detected and mitigated the operation, notified identified users, and is investigating with CrowdStrike and law enforcement.

incidents.title: Convertr analytics script hijacked to skim e-commerce payment data
incidents.victim: Convertr and e-commerce merchants using its checkout platform
incidents.attacker: A Brazilian credit-card-skimming group, according to Sansec; attribution is not independently confirmed. The suspected CVE-2026-8467 exploitation has not been confirmed.
incidents.what: Attackers modified a Plausible analytics tracker hosted on Convertr’s self-managed infrastructure and injected a skimmer that loaded on merchants’ checkout pages. The script targeted card numbers, expiration dates, CVVs, cardholder names, and Brazilian CPF taxpayer-identification numbers.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: A trusted shared script used by Convertr merchants was compromised, creating a supply-chain-style payment-data theft risk across multiple online stores. Convertr removed the skimmer, patched Plausible, and said it was notifying affected merchants and payment providers.
incidents.significance: Sansec observed the altered Convertr-hosted tracker and the injected payment skimmer affecting checkout pages across the platform’s merchant ecosystem. The report does not establish how many shoppers’ data was actually exfiltrated.

severity.reason: Researchers observed a live compromise of a shared e-commerce analytics script configured to collect payment-card and identity data. Actual numbers of stolen records and confirmed financial losses were not reported.

updates.what: Attackers modified a Plausible analytics tracker hosted on Convertr-managed infrastructure and injected a payment skimmer that loaded on checkout pages for merchants using the platform. The script targeted card numbers, expiration dates, CVVs, cardholder names, and Brazilian CPF taxpayer identification numbers.

incidents.title: UK police-data suppliers repeatedly breached since 2021
incidents.victim: Multiple unnamed third-party ICT suppliers holding UK police information, and potentially affected police forces
incidents.attacker: Unknown; the watchdog reported repeated compromises but no attribution
incidents.what: His Majesty’s Inspectorate of Constabulary and Fire & Rescue Services said police and policing bodies shared information about multiple cyberattacks compromising third-party ICT supply chains that held police information since 2021. The report did not identify suppliers, attack methods, or confirm whether data was stolen.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The incidents affected trusted suppliers handling potentially sensitive victim, safeguarding, intelligence, and investigation information. The watchdog also cited attacks involving operational-system compromise, data compromise, and service disruption within policing and fire services, but the supplier incidents’ individual consequences remain undisclosed.
incidents.significance: A UK policing watchdog confirmed repeated compromises of suppliers holding police data, outside police monitoring and with limited contractual cybersecurity assurance. The affected information could include sensitive operational and investigative records, although the report does not establish data theft or the final scope.

severity.reason: The watchdog reported multiple actual cyberattacks affecting third-party ICT supply chains holding police information. It did not establish whether police data was stolen, how many suppliers or forces were affected, or the extent of service disruption.

updates.what: His Majesty’s Inspectorate of Constabulary and Fire & Rescue Services reported multiple cyberattacks since 2021 affecting third-party ICT supply chains that held police information. The report said incidents involving operational systems, compromised data and service disruption occurred, but withheld supplier, force and attack-level details.

incidents.title: AI-assisted intrusion stole GIS server records and credentials
incidents.victim: An unnamed organization operating an exposed GIS server
incidents.attacker: Unidentified human-led threat actor; researchers reported LLM assistance in planning and tool development
incidents.what: The attackers exploited a GIS server protected by default credentials during a 24-day campaign. They stole cadastral and commercial records, Windows credentials, and email data; the campaign also targeted AI workflow platforms and inference services.
incidents.ai_role: A large language model assisted the human operator with attack planning and tool development; the reporting does not establish that an autonomous AI agent carried out the intrusion.
incidents.why: The incident involved unauthorized access to a real organization's server and confirmed theft of organizational records and reusable credentials.
incidents.significance: Researchers analyzed exposed attack infrastructure and artifacts documenting the intrusion, including the stolen cadastral, commercial, credential, and email data. The victim and final scope were not identified.

severity.reason: Researchers reported that the GIS server intrusion resulted in theft of cadastral and commercial records, Windows credentials, and email data. Service disruption and financial losses were not reported.

updates.what: Attackers accessed a GIS server using default credentials and stole cadastral and commercial records, Windows credentials, and email data during a 24-day campaign.

incidents.title: Paylogix breach exposed sensitive records of at least 67,789 people
incidents.victim: Paylogix
incidents.attacker: Akira ransomware group claimed responsibility; attribution is based on the reported claim.
incidents.what: Attackers stole files from Paylogix’s network over several days in November. The files reportedly contained Social Security numbers, financial and health-insurance information, medical data, passport numbers, and taxpayer IDs.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The incident involved confirmed network compromise and theft of highly sensitive personal and medical information affecting at least 67,789 people.
incidents.where: South Carolina, New Hampshire, and Vermont, United States
incidents.significance: Paylogix confirmed file theft involving medical, financial, identity, and tax information; at least 67,789 people were reported affected.

severity.reason: Reported stolen files contained sensitive medical, financial, identity, and tax information affecting at least 67,789 people. Operational disruption and financial losses were not reported.

updates.what: Attackers stole files from Paylogix’s network over several days in November. The exposed information included Social Security numbers, financial and health-insurance information, medical data, passport numbers, and taxpayer IDs.

An unauthorized party accessed Paylogix’s network and copied files containing personal and protected health information. The exposed data included Social Security numbers, benefit information, and, for some individuals, credentials, financial, insurance, medical, passport, and identity-document information.

incidents.title: eMudhra certificates revoked after eight keys were compromised
incidents.victim: eMudhra, an Indian certificate authority, and users relying on its certificates
incidents.attacker: Not reported; the method and attribution remain unclear.
incidents.what: Eight eMudhra keys were compromised, prompting Google, Mozilla, Apple, the Go project, and others to block the associated certificates. The reporting does not establish how the keys were compromised or identify affected end users.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: Compromise of certificate-authority keys can undermine trust in certificates used by downstream systems, leading major technology providers to block the affected certificates.
incidents.significance: The compromise affected trusted certificate infrastructure and triggered coordinated blocking by major browser, platform, and software ecosystem operators, although downstream damage is not reported.

severity.reason: Eight intermediate CA private keys were recoverable and had to be revoked or blocked across major browsers and trust stores. No confirmed fraudulent certificates, impersonation, data theft, or financial loss was reported.

updates.what: Eight eMudhra intermediate-certificate private keys were compromised because a key-generation flaw created weak keys that could be recovered nearly instantly. eMudhra revoked the certificates, while Mozilla, Google, Apple, Microsoft, Sectigo, and Cloudflare blocked or remediated against them.

Eight eMudhra intermediate certificate authority keys generated in April 2025 were compromised because of extremely weak key values. Microsoft and other browser and operating-system vendors revoked or distrusted the related certificates; the keys could have enabled forged website or code-signing certificates and interception of encrypted communications, but exploitation was not reported.

incidents.title: BUGSTER Used AI Agents to Breach Indian Universities
incidents.victim: Two Indian public universities, an Indian e-commerce site, and large Ethereum holders
incidents.attacker: Unit 42 reported a financially motivated, English-speaking operator running Hermes Agent profiles over Telegram.
incidents.what: The operator's agents brute-forced a university WordPress login, exfiltrated more than 5,200 student and faculty PII records from another university's MongoDB, obtained an e-commerce API token and merchant IDs, and compiled files on 45 large ETH holders.
incidents.ai_role: Hermes Agent used DeepSeek V4 for reasoning, while Cursor used Claude Opus 4.8, GPT-5.5, and Composer 2.5 for code. Safety controls, sandboxing, permission checks, and MCP approvals were disabled, allowing the agents to perform the actions.
incidents.why: The activity was financially motivated; the operator targeted university data, e-commerce credentials, and large Ethereum holders.

severity.reason: The report documents university compromises, theft of over 5,200 personal records, and acquisition of an e-commerce API token. This establishes sensitive-data theft across multiple affected systems.

updates.what: The attacker accessed the organization’s network and exfiltrated files containing patient information. The number of affected people and exact data types remained under review; at least 501 affected individuals were estimated for reporting purposes.

The actor used Hermes Agent with DeepSeek V4, Cursor, AI-generated reconnaissance and scripts, and other tooling. Unit 42 confirmed a university intrusion involving exfiltration of more than 5,200 records containing student and faculty personally identifiable information; a separate university was subjected to AI-assisted enumeration and brute-force activity.

BUGSTER used an AI-agent framework in a WordPress campaign and breached a second Indian public university, exfiltrating a database containing more than 5,200 records, including student personally identifiable information.

incidents.title: University of Copenhagen breach exposed data of 525,000 people
incidents.victim: University of Copenhagen
incidents.attacker: Not reported
incidents.what: Hackers accessed a University of Copenhagen test environment containing personal data belonging to 525,000 people.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The university confirmed unauthorized access to personal data affecting 525,000 people.
incidents.significance: The University of Copenhagen confirmed that hackers accessed personal data belonging to 525,000 people, meeting the reported large-scale data-theft threshold.

severity.reason: The university confirmed unauthorized access to personal data affecting 525,000 people. The report does not establish service disruption, financial losses, or the identity of the attackers.

updates.what: Hackers accessed a University of Copenhagen test environment containing personal data. The university later said data associated with another 20,000 staff and students, including PIN codes, was exposed; the full scope remains under investigation.

incidents.title: Teams IT-support scams led to malware and ransomware intrusions
incidents.victim: Multiple unnamed organizations targeted through Microsoft Teams
incidents.attacker: Activity was assessed by Arctic Wolf Labs as aligned with STAC4749; Sophos linked some attacks to Chaos ransomware. Attribution is not independently established in the report.
incidents.what: Attackers used mail bombing, impersonation through newly created or acquired Microsoft 365 tenants, and Teams external chats to persuade users to grant remote access or execute PowerShell commands. Observed follow-on activity included malware deployment, reconnaissance, lateral movement, LDAP queries, data exfiltration, and in some cases ransomware deployment.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The campaign turns trusted collaboration and remote-management tools into an initial-access path and has produced broader organizational intrusions across hundreds of investigated cases.
incidents.significance: Arctic Wolf reported a recurring pattern across hundreds of cases, including observed implants that queried Active Directory and transmitted information externally; the activity also led to Chaos ransomware deployment in some cases. Specific victims and aggregate losses were not reported.

severity.reason: Researchers reported multiple real-world organizational intrusions, including sensitive-data exfiltration and ransomware deployment in some cases. The source does not establish the number of organizations suffering each consequence or the duration and financial impact.

updates.what: Attackers used mail bombing, Microsoft Teams impersonation, fake IT-support tenants and domains, vishing, and remote-access tools to obtain hands-on access. Observed intrusions included reconnaissance, lateral movement, deployment of backdoors and additional RMM tools, data exfiltration, and in some cases ransomware deployment.

incidents.title: Gheist campaign stole secrets through compromised GitHub tokens
incidents.victim: More than 850 compromised GitHub accounts, including enterprise organizations and private repositories
incidents.attacker: Unknown operators using stolen GitHub tokens; attribution is not established. Wiz observed overlap with other campaigns and credential sources including infostealer logs.
incidents.what: Since September 15, 2026, the Gheist campaign planted malicious GitHub Actions workflows in repositories accessible to compromised tokens. In private repositories and GitHub Enterprise environments, the workflows executed, printed repository and environment secrets into logs, and deleted the runs; Wiz recovered more than 13,500 planted branches. Some cloud credentials were subsequently used to enumerate AWS Secrets Manager, and self-hosted-runner payloads attempted host and credential discovery.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The campaign achieved unauthorized access across hundreds of accounts and exposed sensitive repository, production, cloud, and other credentials. GitHub's approval control blocked the observed public-repository runs, but it did not protect private repositories or GitHub Enterprise environments.
incidents.significance: Wiz directly observed malicious branches and completed workflow runs in private and enterprise environments, with secrets printed into logs and cloud-role activity following attacker-branch execution. The reported scale was more than 850 compromised accounts and 13,500 planted branches, although the amount of successfully exfiltrated secret material is not quantified.

severity.reason: Wiz observed unauthorized workflow execution and secret dumping in private and enterprise repositories, including production-scoped and cloud credentials. Public-repository runs were held for approval and did not execute; financial loss and broader operational effects were not established.

updates.what: Attackers used stolen GitHub tokens to plant workflows in accessible repositories, execute them in private and enterprise environments, and dump repository and environment secrets into workflow logs before deleting the runs. Wiz recovered more than 13,500 planted branches; activity also included cloning private repositories and using obtained cloud credentials to enumerate AWS Secrets Manager.
An ongoing campaign weaponized stolen GitHub tokens to access developer repositories and harvest cloud credentials and other sensitive data.

Attackers used stolen GitHub tokens to create ci-sync branches and workflows that encoded repository and deployment-environment secrets into GitHub Actions logs, downloaded the logs, and deleted the workflow runs. Wiz recovered more than 13,500 planted branches from over 850 compromised accounts; private repositories and GitHub Enterprise Server were affected, while public runs checked by Wiz were held before execution.

incidents.title: Magento loader campaign compromised 953 online stores
incidents.victim: At least 953 online stores, mostly using Magento
incidents.attacker: An unattributed criminal group tracked by Sansec
incidents.what: The group compromised online stores and inserted JavaScript loaders into Magento CMS blocks. The loaders fingerprinted visitors and could retrieve and execute attacker-controlled code; Sansec found evidence of webshells, backdoors, rogue administrator accounts, and persistent database write access in affected stores.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The campaign involved confirmed unauthorized access to hundreds of business-critical e-commerce systems. Sansec reported 953 affected stores since July 2025, including 83 using the newly registered deepveindrilling.com loader, although the final payload was not captured for the latest wave.
incidents.significance: Sansec and eComscan observed the loader across 953 stores and found that infected stores could remain under attacker control even after the script was deleted because the attacker retained database write access. The reporting does not establish confirmed payment-data theft or a specific financial loss.

severity.reason: Researchers observed unauthorized code and persistence mechanisms across hundreds of real online stores, including webshells, backdoors, rogue admin accounts, and database write access. The available reporting does not confirm the final payload, data theft, service interruption, or financial losses.

updates.what: Sansec and eComscan found malicious JavaScript loaders written into Magento CMS blocks across a campaign affecting 953 stores since July 2025. The loader fingerprinted visitors and could receive further instructions; Sansec reported that the attacker could write to the store database, with earlier waves involving webshells and backdoors.

Attackers injected loader code into at least 953 online stores using rogue administrator accounts, backdoors, and exploitation of PolyShell or SessionReaper vulnerabilities. The loader fingerprinted visitors and selectively delivered scripts, but Sansec had not captured the final payload.

Sansec observed malicious JavaScript loaders injected into Magento storefronts, including through PolyShell and SessionReaper exploitation. The code selectively served content to real shoppers while evading scanners; the final payload was not established. One store also had a rogue administrator account used to inject the code.

incidents.title: Microsoft 365 token-replay campaign compromised 97 accounts
incidents.victim: 97 Microsoft 365 accounts at 79 organizations
incidents.attacker: Unidentified threat actors; Huntress traced activity to infrastructure including the 193.26.115[.]0/24 range, but attribution was not established.
incidents.what: Attackers used adversary-in-the-middle login pages, device-code phishing, and social engineering to capture Microsoft 365 session tokens and replay them. They registered at least 48 rogue Entra devices, added authenticator methods, removed existing MFA methods at 19 organizations, created hidden mailbox rules, and used at least one compromised mailbox to send spam.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The campaign bypassed the need to defeat MFA again by replaying stolen authenticated sessions, enabling persistent access to organizational email accounts and directories.
incidents.significance: Huntress observed 497 successful Microsoft 365 sign-in events and confirmed 97 compromised accounts across 79 organizations. The attackers established persistence through rogue devices and MFA changes, and manipulated email handling in compromised mailboxes.

severity.reason: Researchers confirmed unauthorized access to 97 accounts, rogue Entra device registration, MFA changes, and mailbox-rule manipulation across 79 organizations. One mailbox sent spam to hundreds of recipients; broader operational or financial losses were not reported.

updates.what: Attackers used adversary-in-the-middle phishing, device-code phishing, and social engineering to steal Microsoft 365 session tokens and replay them. They registered at least 48 rogue Entra devices, added authenticator apps, removed existing MFA methods at 19 organizations, and created mailbox rules; one compromised account sent spam to hundreds of recipients.

incidents.title: uCreator/Baohuo spyware infected Android devices and targeted messaging accounts
incidents.victim: Android users who installed tampered Telegram or WeChat apps, including users in China, the United States, India, Brazil, and Indonesia
incidents.attacker: uCreator/YingGai kit operators and possible customers; Ovi links parts of the operation to three companies in Hunan, China, but shared ownership remains unproven
incidents.what: The rentable uCreator Android spyware was embedded in modified Telegram and WeChat apps distributed through sideloading, social engineering, third-party stores, and a container app. Its code can capture Telegram 2FA passwords, read chat databases, reset sessions, change phone numbers, hide attacker sessions, and clone WeChat accounts. Doctor Web previously estimated that more than 58,000 devices were infected by the related Baohuo backdoor.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The campaign compromises real Android devices and can take over messaging and mobile-wallet-related accounts, creating risks of credential theft, private-message access, fraud, and account lockout. The researchers cautioned that the analysis demonstrated technical capability and did not establish that every takeover function was used against victims.
incidents.where: Android users in multiple reported countries
incidents.significance: Doctor Web reported more than 58,000 infected devices for the related Baohuo backdoor, while Ovi found victim records apparently located in China and the United States. The incident is significant because a commercial spyware kit provides remote account-takeover functions across widely used messaging and payment-related applications, although the final number of victims and confirmed account takeovers are unknown.

severity.reason: Doctor Web reported more than 58,000 infected devices for the related Baohuo backdoor, and researchers accessed backend data containing apparent victim records. The available reporting does not establish the number of accounts actually hijacked, financial losses, or service disruption.

updates.what: Researchers found the rentable uCreator Android spyware embedded in tampered Telegram and WeChat apps or delivered through a container app. It can steal Telegram 2FA passwords, access chat history, change account details, clone WeChat accounts, and collect account and contact data. Doctor Web previously estimated more than 58,000 devices infected by Baohuo samples sharing code and infrastructure with uCreator, although the operator relationship and the full victim count remain unresolved.

incidents.title: Johns Hopkins Bayview patient data uploaded to outside AI platform
incidents.victim: Johns Hopkins Bayview Medical Center
incidents.attacker: Not reported; the hospital said a staff member uploaded the data to an unapproved outside AI platform.
incidents.what: A staff member uploaded a spreadsheet containing personal health information for 3,182 patients to an outside AI platform that was not approved for use. The hospital contacted the provider to request deletion.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The spreadsheet included names, admission and treatment dates, medical-record and account numbers, treating departments, medications, and provider names.
incidents.significance: A confirmed healthcare data exposure involved sensitive patient and treatment information and an external AI platform. The reporting does not establish malicious access, onward disclosure, or whether deletion was successful.

severity.reason: The hospital confirmed exposure of a spreadsheet involving 3,182 patients to an unapproved external AI platform. No service disruption or financial loss was reported.

updates.what: A staff member uploaded a spreadsheet containing limited patient information to a public AI tool. The medical center detected the incident on September 21, 2026, deleted the prompt and thread, requested deletion from the provider, and offered affected patients credit monitoring.

incidents.title: OpenCode Console Breach Exposed Users’ Third-Party AI API Keys
incidents.victim: OpenCode Console and 1.4% of its users with linked external provider keys
incidents.attacker: Unknown; no attribution was reported
incidents.what: An intruder accessed an older OpenCode system and exposed centrally stored OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google API keys. The keys were misused for unauthorized charges ranging from hundreds of dollars to more than $1,700.
incidents.ai_role: The compromised system was a hosted gateway for the OpenCode coding agent, and the exposed credentials provided access to external AI providers.
incidents.why: The keys were exposed for resale or misuse, resulting in unauthorized use and charges. OpenCode described the incident as part of a large-scale distillation attack, but that framing was reported as unproven.

severity.reason: Users' reusable AI provider keys were exposed and abused for unauthorized charges. The reporting establishes credential exposure across users; the total victim count is not stated.

updates.what: Attackers breached an older OpenCode system and accessed stored OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google API keys belonging to users of OpenCode Console. Affected users reported unauthorized API usage and charges, including individual losses in the hundreds of dollars and some above $1,000; providers blocked exposed keys and refunds were initiated.

OpenCode said API keys stored by some Console users for Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google were exposed. Affected users reported unauthorized charges ranging from several hundred dollars to $1,700, and some Google Cloud projects were suspended for abusive activity.

incidents.title: BASS Medical Group network intrusion exposed health information
incidents.victim: BASS Medical Group
incidents.attacker: Unknown unauthorized third party; attribution was not reported.
incidents.what: BASS Medical Group identified suspicious network activity on September 4, 2026. Its investigation determined on September 22 that an unauthorized party accessed its network and that medical treatment codes, billing information, and health-insurance information may have been viewed or acquired.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The incident involved confirmed unauthorized network access and potential exposure of protected health and billing information. The number of affected individuals was not disclosed.
incidents.significance: A healthcare provider confirmed a network intrusion involving information that could reveal patients’ treatment, billing, and insurance details, although the scope of affected people and whether the data was actually acquired remain unknown.

severity.reason: The organization confirmed unauthorized network access and potential viewing or acquisition of medical, billing, and insurance information; operational disruption and the number of affected individuals were not reported.

updates.what: BASS Medical Group detected suspicious network activity on September 4, 2026. Its investigation determined on September 22 that an unauthorized party accessed the network and that medical treatment codes, billing information, and health insurance information may have been viewed or acquired.

incidents.title: Genesys internal CRM and LMS accessed without authorization
incidents.victim: Genesys
incidents.attacker: Unauthorized third party; attribution not reported.
incidents.what: Genesys confirmed that an unauthorized third party accessed certain internal business systems, including its learning management system and customer relationship management platform. Information in those systems was accessed and/or downloaded without authorization; Genesys said its customer-facing platforms and customer and partner environments were not compromised.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The incident involved confirmed unauthorized access to business-critical internal systems and unauthorized access/download of organizational and customer-account information. Genesys suspended use of the affected learning management system while assessing scope and impact.
incidents.significance: Genesys confirmed compromise of internal CRM and learning systems, with unauthorized access or downloads involving names, business email addresses, telephone numbers, job titles, company and account information, and customer-interaction data. The scope and full impact remained under review.

severity.reason: Genesys confirmed unauthorized access and downloading of business and account information and suspended use of the affected LMS. The available report does not establish the number of affected records, financial losses, or access to customer-platform data.

updates.what: Genesys confirmed that an unauthorized third party accessed certain internal business systems, including its customer relationship management platform and learning management system. Information in those systems was accessed and/or downloaded without authorization, including business and account information, contact details, job titles, company information, and customer-interaction data.

Genesys confirmed unauthorized access to internal business systems, including its CRM and learning-management system. Information such as customer and account details, names, business contact information, job titles, and interaction data was accessed and likely downloaded; Genesys Cloud, Genesys Engage, customer environments, and partner data were not compromised.

incidents.title: Malicious AGENTS.md File Tricked Coding Agent Into Installing Rogue Package
incidents.victim: An unnamed customer using an AI coding agent
incidents.attacker: Not reported
incidents.what: Researchers found a malicious AGENTS.md instruction file in the customer’s Downloads folder that caused an AI coding agent to install a rogue npm package.
incidents.ai_role: The AI coding agent followed malicious instructions in the AGENTS.md file and installed the rogue npm package.
incidents.why: The incident demonstrates unauthorized package installation by an AI coding agent after processing attacker-controlled instructions.
incidents.significance: The reported impact is limited to installation of a rogue npm package on one customer environment; further compromise or damage was not reported.

severity.reason: Forever Security observed the attempt on a real customer's machine and stopped the agent before any code ran; no resulting compromise or loss was reported.

incidents.title: ARTEX and Claude Code Used to Breach South Korean Banks
incidents.victim: South Korean financial institutions, including Shinhan Bank, KB Kookmin Bank, Hana Bank, and Yegaram Savings Bank.
incidents.attacker: CrowdStrike reported with moderate confidence that a likely Chinese-speaking, financially motivated actor carried out the intrusions. Reuters reported at least nine banks were targeted.
incidents.what: Between late September and early October 2026, the actor breached a bank's loan-progress inquiry service for brokers and another bank's employee mobile work-support system. Reuters reported that about 25,000 Shinhan customers and 119 KB Kookmin customers were affected.
incidents.ai_role: The actor used ARTEX, an open-source multi-agent penetration-testing tool developed in China, alongside Claude Code sessions. DeepSeek v4.1-flash was the main backend, with GLM-5.3 and Grok 4.6 used in other sessions; exposed server files included Claude Code histories, memory files, a Chinese-language pentest prompt, and ARTEX configurations.
incidents.why: The activity was reported as financially motivated; the actor asked Claude where to sell Korean breach data. CrowdStrike attributed the enabling conditions to freely available agentic offensive tooling and commercial model access.

severity.reason: Bank systems were breached and customer data affecting about 25,119 people was reported. Operational disruption and confirmed financial losses were not established in the available reporting.

updates.what: The actor used ARTEX, an open-source multi-agent penetration-testing tool, alongside Claude Code sessions and multiple commercial AI models to conduct parallel intrusions into South Korean banking systems. Reported targets included a broker loan-progress inquiry service and an employee mobile work-support system; Reuters reported at least nine banks were targeted, with about 25,000 Shinhan customers and 119 KB Kookmin customers affected.

incidents.title: MeshCentral servers and remote clients actively targeted
incidents.victim: Organizations operating MeshCentral servers and connected remote clients; specific victims were not reported
incidents.attacker: Unknown threat actors; attribution was not reported
incidents.what: The MeshCentral developer warned that attackers were actively exploiting servers and taking control of the servers and remote clients. Users were urged to update to version 1.3.1.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The report describes active unauthorized control of remote-access infrastructure and connected clients, creating a consequential intrusion risk beyond a merely theoretical vulnerability.
incidents.significance: The developer reported active attacks capable of controlling MeshCentral servers and remote clients, although the number and identities of affected organizations were not disclosed.

severity.reason: The developer reported active exploitation and control of servers and remote clients, but the available reporting does not establish service disruption, victim count, data theft, or financial loss.

incidents.title: AI-Assisted PHP2Shell Attack Hit European Government Entity
incidents.victim: A government entity in Europe
incidents.attacker: Not reported
incidents.what: Threat actors exploited PHP2Shell vulnerabilities CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, then used agentic AI platforms for post-exploitation. Within two hours, they accessed password hashes and multi-factor authentication data.
incidents.ai_role: Attackers used agentic AI platforms for post-exploitation activity.
incidents.why: The reporting explicitly links agentic AI use to post-exploitation following exploitation of the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities.
incidents.significance: Not reported

severity.reason: The attackers were observed accessing password hashes and multi-factor authentication data at a European government entity. The available reporting does not establish service disruption, broader victim reach, or a qualifying critical-network impact.

updates.what: Unit 42 observed an attacker access password hashes and multifactor-authentication secrets within two hours of an intrusion, conduct host and Active Directory reconnaissance, and establish an NTLM-relay tunnel while attempting Domain Admin escalation. Unit 42 later said it could not confirm that initial access involved the PHP2Shell CVEs.

incidents.title: Leaked LiteLLM key enabled malicious package release
incidents.victim: LiteLLM and its Python package release pipeline
incidents.attacker: An unidentified threat actor; attribution was not reported.
incidents.what: A configuration file committed to a public LiteLLM GitHub repository exposed an Agent Platform master key. The threat actor used it to steal GitHub tokens and push a malicious version of the Python package.
incidents.ai_role: The compromised asset was LiteLLM's Agent Platform and its associated Python package.
incidents.why: Not reported

locations.label: San Francisco, California, United States
locations.basis: Vendor headquarters (approximate; not an attack-site claim)

severity.reason: An exposed master key was used to steal GitHub tokens and publish a malicious package. Downstream victim counts and resulting damage are not established.

updates.what: An accidentally exposed, unrevoked LiteLLM Agent Platform master key was used to access a GitHub OAuth token with organization-owner privileges. The attacker altered the release pipeline, published LiteLLM 1.107.0 to PyPI and corresponding container images, and added workflows that harvested GitHub, cloud, AI-provider, database, browser-session, and other credentials.

incidents.title: CVE-2026-110447 exploited to backdoor Nextcloud servers
incidents.victim: Organizations operating Nextcloud with Collabora Online Built-in CODE Server
incidents.attacker: Unattributed threat actors; CISA and reporting confirm exploitation, but no actor attribution was provided.
incidents.what: Attackers exploited CVE-2026-110447, an operating-system command-injection flaw in Collabora Online Built-in CODE Server when integrated with Nextcloud. Reported activity included installing web shells, reconnaissance, and searching for credential stores, password-manager artifacts, and cryptocurrency wallets.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The exploitation provided a path to remote code execution and involved actual compromise of Nextcloud servers, with searches for reusable credentials and financial assets.
incidents.significance: This was active exploitation of a critical collaboration and file-management platform vulnerability, and reporting observed web-shell deployment and post-compromise reconnaissance for credentials, password-manager data, and cryptocurrency wallets.

severity.reason: Reporting describes compromised Nextcloud servers with web shells and reconnaissance for sensitive credential and wallet artifacts. Service disruption, confirmed theft, and financial losses were not reported.

updates.what: Attackers exploited CVE-2026-110447, an operating-system command-injection flaw, to backdoor Nextcloud servers with web shells. Reporting says they conducted reconnaissance and searched for credential stores, password-manager artifacts, and cryptocurrency wallets.

incidents.title: CVE-2026-114625 exploited against Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator
incidents.victim: Organizations operating on-premise Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator
incidents.attacker: Unattributed threat actors; Arista acknowledged active exploitation but provided no actor attribution. Two Japan-geolocated source IP addresses were reported, which does not establish attacker identity or victim location.
incidents.what: Attackers exploited CVE-2026-114625, an SQL-injection vulnerability in on-premise VeloCloud Orchestrator, to access privileged internal functionality. Exploitation required network access to the VCO web interface, a valid authenticated session, and at least an Enterprise Read Only role.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The incident demonstrates unauthorized exploitation of a network-management platform with access to privileged internal functionality, although post-escalation actions and the number of affected organizations were not disclosed.
