incidents.why: The incident involved confirmed unauthorized network access, data exfiltration, and disruption at a healthcare-navigation company; the number of affected individuals has not been disclosed.
incidents.significance: Quantum Health confirmed theft of sensitive medical, identity, and insurance-related information after a vishing-enabled network compromise, along with disruption to internal and external systems.

severity.reason: Quantum Health reported network disruption and confirmed acquisition of files containing protected health and personal information. The number of affected people and financial losses were not reported.

updates.what: An attacker tricked a Quantum Health user into providing network access. The unauthorized party accessed the network and acquired files; Quantum Health reported that the stolen data included personal, protected health, insurance, claims, and benefits information.

incidents.title: Heart of America Medical Center network breach exposed patient data

incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The incident affected a hospital and involved confirmed theft of patient information; the number of affected individuals was not reported.
incidents.significance: A healthcare provider confirmed network intrusion and exfiltration of patient medical and identity data, demonstrating meaningful harm even though the final affected population remains unknown.

severity.reason: The hospital confirmed unauthorized access and exfiltration of files containing patient information. No service disruption, victim count, or financial loss was reported.

updates.what: Suspicious activity was identified around June 12, 2025. The investigation determined that an unauthorized party accessed the hospital network and exfiltrated files containing patient information, including names, Social Security numbers, medical records, and other medical information.

incidents.title: Precision Imaging Centers confirmed network intrusion and file theft
incidents.victim: Precision Imaging Centers, operated by The Medical Imaging Partnership
incidents.attacker: Unidentified unauthorized third party; attribution was not reported.

incidents.why: The imaging provider confirmed unauthorized access and copying of files, but the scope and sensitivity of the stolen information remain under investigation.
incidents.significance: A healthcare provider confirmed a real network compromise and file theft; the available reporting does not yet establish the final data contents or number of affected people.

severity.reason: The organization confirmed that an unauthorized party copied files from its network, and reported the incident to HHS using a provisional estimate of 501 individuals. The exact contents and final number of affected people were not established.

updates.what: Precision Imaging Centers identified suspicious activity in its network and determined that an unauthorized party accessed the network and copied files. The investigation and data review were ongoing, so the specific data types and affected individuals had not yet been determined.

incidents.title: SafePal breach exposed order data of nearly 40,000 customers
incidents.victim: SafePal and approximately 39,798 customers
incidents.attacker: Unknown; a threat actor advertised the stolen data, while SafePal confirmed the breach and vulnerability exploitation.
incidents.what: Attackers exploited a vulnerability in SafePal's order-tracking customer-information plugin and accessed order-related data, including names, addresses, email addresses, phone numbers, and order details. SafePal said seed phrases, private keys, wallet passwords, bank information, payment-card numbers, and government identification were not affected.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The confirmed compromise exposed personal information belonging to approximately 39,798 customers and prompted SafePal to rebuild its order-processing pipeline, notify affected individuals, and investigate possible related phishing or financial losses.
incidents.significance: SafePal confirmed unauthorized access and theft of personal order data affecting nearly 40,000 people. The exposed information could support targeted phishing, including attempts to obtain cryptocurrency wallet secrets, although compromise of wallet credentials was not reported.

severity.reason: SafePal confirmed that approximately 39,798 customers' names, contact details, and order information were compromised. No service outage or verified financial loss was reported, and the company said wallet credentials and payment information were not involved.

incidents.title: French tax authority breach exposed data of 678,000 users
incidents.victim: France’s Directorate General of Public Finances (DGFiP)
incidents.attacker: Unidentified threat actor; the actor boasted on a hacking forum. Access used compromised employee and third-party credentials, but attribution is unconfirmed.
incidents.what: Attackers accessed DGFiP systems in June and July and stole data from approximately 678,000 users. Compromised information included reference tax income, withholding-tax rates, company names and identifiers, and cadastral real-estate data.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The breach exposed sensitive tax and property-related information at a national public finance agency, with confirmed unauthorized access and data theft affecting hundreds of thousands of people.
incidents.significance: DGFiP confirmed that compromised credentials enabled access to its systems and that information on approximately 678,000 users was stolen. Usernames and passwords were reportedly not affected, and the investigation into scope continues.

severity.reason: DGFiP confirmed theft of tax, withholding-tax, company-identifier, and cadastral data affecting approximately 678,000 users. Service disruption and financial losses were not reported.

updates.what: Attackers used compromised credentials for a DGFiP employee and a third-party account to access internal systems and steal tax and cadastral information. Compromised data included reference tax income, withholding-tax rates, company names, unique identifiers, and real-estate address and surface data; usernames and passwords were reportedly not affected.

incidents.title: Boston healthcare nonprofit breach affected 201,260 people

incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The breach exposed sensitive medical, identity, and financial information of 201,260 individuals, according to the HHS OCR breach portal.
incidents.significance: A confirmed network compromise affected more than 200,000 people and involved medical, identity, and financial data. The source says the data was potentially viewed or obtained; the final extent of exfiltration was not established.

severity.reason: The organization detected the incident through a network disruption and investigators confirmed unauthorized network access involving files containing sensitive patient information. The reporting does not establish the duration of service disruption or any direct financial loss.

updates.what: A network security incident caused a network disruption. Investigators confirmed unauthorized network access and potential viewing or acquisition of files containing patient information, including Social Security numbers, financial information, medical information, and health insurance data.

incidents.title: Texas Hearing Institute network breach exposed patient data

incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The affected information potentially included names, personal identifiers, Social Security numbers, diagnosis and treatment information, and financial account information.
incidents.significance: A confirmed network compromise exposed sensitive medical, identity, and financial information of nearly 30,000 patients. The reported 540 GB copied and ransomware attribution came from the attacker and are not independently established.

severity.reason: The organization confirmed unauthorized network access and exposure of patient files affecting 29,744 people. Service disruption, actual data exfiltration, and financial losses were not independently established; the 540 GB copying claim is attributed to Interlock.

updates.what: The institute identified suspicious network activity on March 20, 2026. Investigation found that an unauthorized third party accessed network areas containing patient files, including names, identifiers, Social Security numbers, diagnosis and treatment information, and financial account information. The data was later reportedly leaked online.

severity.reason: The organization confirmed network access and exfiltration, and reported that the affected data was leaked online. Operational disruption and financial losses were not reported.

updates.what: The organization confirmed that a threat actor accessed its network and exfiltrated files containing names, birth dates, Social Security numbers, driver’s-license numbers, state IDs, financial-account information, and personal health information. The stolen data was reportedly published online.

locations.label: Glen Rock, New Jersey, United States

updates.what: SportsMed identified suspicious activity in an employee’s email account and confirmed unauthorized access. The account was secured, and exposed information included names combined with dates of service, provider, diagnosis, treatment, or health-insurance information.

incidents.title: RingCentral social-engineering breach potentially exposed 1.6 million people

incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The incident involved confirmed unauthorized activity at a major cloud communications provider and potentially exposed substantial personal information, although the final scope and authenticity of all published data remain under investigation.
incidents.significance: RingCentral confirmed a cybersecurity incident affecting customer-related data, while HaveIBeenPwned documented approximately 1.6 million unique email addresses with associated personal details. The core RingCentral platform and services reportedly continued operating without disruption.

severity.reason: RingCentral confirmed unauthorized activity and stated that affected individuals were notified, while HaveIBeenPwned reported a dataset containing about 1.6 million email addresses plus names, addresses, and phone numbers. The company has not confirmed the attackers’ claims or the final number of impacted people; services reportedly continued without disruption.

updates.what: RingCentral said a sophisticated social-engineering campaign caused unauthorized activity affecting a limited portion of customers. HaveIBeenPwned reported approximately 1.6 million unique email addresses in the published data, accompanied by names, addresses, and phone numbers.

incidents.title: ShipMonk breach exposed data of nearly 14,000 Trezor customers

incidents.attacker: Unauthorized actor; identity not established. ShipMonk reportedly attributed access to exploitation of a Metabase vulnerability, while ShinyHunters claimed a separate Metabase attack; neither attribution is confirmed here.
incidents.what: Trezor said a breach at its third-party shipping provider, ShipMonk, exposed names, email addresses, phone numbers, shipping addresses, and in some cases cities for 13,689 customers. incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.

The compromise occurred at a third-party shipping provider rather than Trezor itself, illustrating downstream supply-chain exposure.

severity.reason: Trezor confirmed unauthorized access to personal information of nearly 14,000 customers, including contact and shipping data. No service outage or financial loss was reported, and the full scope remained under investigation.

updates.what: Attackers accessed ShipMonk-held Trezor order information. Data included names, email addresses, phone numbers, shipping addresses, and, for some customers, cities; 11,742 customers had more complete data exposed and 1,947 had partial data exposed.

incidents.title: AmnesiaStealer campaign targeted macOS users via fake GitHub pages
incidents.victim: MacOS users targeted in recent ClickFix attacks; specific victims were not reported
incidents.attacker: Unknown; no attribution was reported
incidents.what: Attackers distributed the Rust-based AmnesiaStealer through counterfeit GitHub download pages. The malware prompted users to paste a Terminal command, then harvested keychains, browser databases, Apple Notes, documents, and cookies, sent archives to command-and-control infrastructure, and could provide interactive control of browser sessions.
incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The campaign used social engineering to obtain execution and then enabled theft of reusable credentials, browser sessions, and private files, with an on-demand module providing hands-on browser control.
incidents.significance: Jamf analysis described active distribution in ClickFix attacks and observed functionality for harvesting sensitive macOS data, exfiltration, persistence, and live browser-session control. The number and identities of compromised victims were not reported.

severity.reason: Jamf reported the malware being distributed in recent attacks and documented its collection and exfiltration of keychains, browser data, notes, documents, and cookies. The available reporting does not establish the number of successful infections or downstream losses.

updates.what: ClickFix pages induced users to paste a Terminal command that installed AmnesiaStealer. The malware harvested keychains, browser databases, Apple Notes and documents, attempted macOS security bypasses, sent archives to command-and-control infrastructure, established persistence, and could provide interactive browser-session control.

incidents.title: North Korean IT worker breached an unnamed US federal agency

incidents.attacker: A North Korean IT worker using a fraudulent identity, according to the FBI investigation; attribution and the worker’s exact role remain under investigation.

incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The incident matters because a suspected North Korean operative obtained trusted insider access to a US federal agency, creating a confirmed organizational compromise even though the scope and consequences remain unknown.
incidents.significance: The FBI is investigating an actual breach involving a federal agency and a suspected foreign intelligence-linked insider; the report does not establish data theft or operational disruption.

severity.reason: The agency was reportedly breached through a worker placed in the organization, but the available reporting does not establish which systems or data were accessed or whether services were disrupted.

incidents.victim: LexisNexis, including its Diligence, Metabase API, and Newsdesk services
incidents.attacker: Not reported; LexisNexis identified unusual activity on servers managed by a third-party vendor.

incidents.title: Uber Freight investigates unauthorized access to systems and repositories

incidents.title: Beacon CRM breach exposed data from more than 1,000 charities
incidents.victim: Beacon CRM and more than 1,000 UK charity customers
incidents.attacker: Unknown; no cybercrime group has claimed responsibility.
incidents.what: Attackers used a compromised AWS access key, possibly exposed in public JavaScript build artifacts, to access Beacon’s AWS environment and download customer database backups. Beacon said the backups were encrypted but attackers may have been able to decrypt them before exfiltration; financial-card and bank-account data were reportedly not stored in the affected systems.
incidents.significance: A trusted CRM provider was compromised, creating a multi-organization data-theft incident affecting more than 1,000 charities. Beacon confirmed database-backup downloads and assessed that the threat actor likely exported the system’s stored data, though the precise records accessed remain undetermined.

severity.reason: Beacon confirmed unauthorized access and downloads of customer database backups, and charities reported potential compromise of supporter personal information. The reporting does not establish service disruption or financial loss, and exact accessed objects could not be determined.

updates.what: Attackers accessed Beacon’s AWS environment and downloaded customer database backups. Beacon assessed that the threat actor exported all data stored in the database, which could have included supporters’ names, phone numbers, email addresses, and postal addresses; the data was encrypted but may have been decrypted before exfiltration.

incidents.ai_role: AI involvement not confirmed in the reporting.
incidents.why: The breach resulted in confirmed exfiltration of protected health information and financial and identity data from a healthcare-management provider.
incidents.significance: Optalis confirmed both unauthorized network access and exfiltration of sensitive healthcare, financial, and identity information affecting 13,723 individuals.

severity.reason: Files containing protected health information, Social Security numbers, financial information, and payment data were confirmed exfiltrated. No actual misuse of the stolen data was identified in the reporting.

updates.what: Suspicious activity led to confirmation that an unauthorized party accessed Optalis’s computer network. The review found protected health information for 13,723 people, including Social Security numbers, financial information, diagnoses, treatment information, and insurance details.

incidents.title: AnMed cyberattack closed 83 healthcare facilities and disrupted care

incidents.significance: AnMed confirmed a consequential cyber incident affecting core healthcare operations: 83 facilities initially closed, some appointments were postponed, and transfers and diversions occurred. updates.what: AnMed confirmed a malware-related cybersecurity disruption on July 26. Computer systems, phone lines, and internet connectivity went down; recovery required downtime procedures and restoration of clinical systems.

incidents.title: Women’s Center for Radiology network breach exposed patient data

updates.what: An unauthorized party accessed the radiology practice’s network and accessed or downloaded files containing information on 66,422 patients, including diagnoses, test results, medical-record numbers, driver’s-license numbers, and health-insurance information.
